--[[
	PreSimulate mixin: forward motion pre-simulation.
	  :PreSimulateForward / :PreSimulateAttachmentForward return local CFrames per step without
	  emitting. Used by Motion Preview, by Emit for InvertMotion's SimLocalCFrames cache, and by
	  EngineReplay's per-cycle cache rebuild.
]]

local GraphMod = require(script.Parent.Graph)
local Constants = require(script.Parent.PartConstants)
local LinkCF = require(script.Parent.LinkCF)
local Turbulence = require(script.Parent.Turbulence)
local DirectionVectors = Constants.DirectionVectors

-- The three PosOffset graphs at normalized life steppedI, in no frame yet.
local function rawOffset(data, seeds, steppedI)
	local oX = data.PosOffsetX and GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(steppedI, data.PosOffsetX, seeds.PosOffsetX) or 0
	local oY = data.PosOffsetY and GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(steppedI, data.PosOffsetY, seeds.PosOffsetY) or 0
	local oZ = data.PosOffsetZ and GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(steppedI, data.PosOffsetZ, seeds.PosOffsetZ) or 0
	return Vector3.new(oX, oY, oZ)
end

-- The rotation angles a play starts from: none in Speed mode, its graphs' first values otherwise.
local function startAngles(data, seeds, rotMode)
	if rotMode == "Speed" then
		return 0, 0, 0
	end
	local rotX = GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(0, data.RotSpeedX, seeds.RotSpeedX)
	local rotY = GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(0, data.RotSpeedY, seeds.RotSpeedY)
	local rotZ = GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(0, data.RotSpeedZ, seeds.RotSpeedZ)
	return rotX, rotY, rotZ
end

return function(Particle)

-- Walks a Part/Beam/Model emit's motion forward and returns the per-step local CFrames, so the live
-- simulation matches the preview. The CFrames are local to `parentCF` (Link target or world origin)
-- so a moving Link carries the path. spawnEmitterRotation is the emitter's world rotation at spawn,
-- as initialCF is; a live play keeps its own link-local under a welded link (UpdateCommon._posOffsetFrameDelta).
function Particle:PreSimulateForward(data, seeds, initialCF, baseDirection, spreadRotation, link, lifetime, previewMaxSteps, spawnEmitterRotation, linkLocal, maskRefCF)
	local linkMode = data.LinkMode or "Follow"
	-- maskRefCF (the emitter's own frame) engages the per-axis link masks as the emit does.
	local parentCF = LinkCF.emitParentFrame(linkMode, link, linkLocal, maskRefCF and data.LinkAxes or nil, maskRefCF)
	local useVOS = LinkCF.usesLinkSpace(linkMode, link)
	-- previewMaxSteps caps preview callers; InvertMotion caps emit (per-particle CFrame allocation).
	local INVERT_MAX_STEPS = 500
	local totalKeyFrames = math.max(1, data.TotalKeyFrames)
	if previewMaxSteps and totalKeyFrames > previewMaxSteps then
		totalKeyFrames = previewMaxSteps
	elseif data.InvertMotion and totalKeyFrames > INVERT_MAX_STEPS then
		totalKeyFrames = INVERT_MAX_STEPS
	end
	local stepDT = lifetime / totalKeyFrames

	local currentPosition = initialCF.Position
	local localCF = parentCF:ToObjectSpace(initialCF)
	local baseDir = baseDirection
	local emissionDirection = data.EmissionDirection
	local rotMode = data.RotMode or "OverLife"
	local accRotX, accRotY, accRotZ = 0, 0, 0

	-- Snapshot AccelTarget position at start; InvertMotion's cached CFrames cannot track a moving target.
	local hasTargetAccel = data.AccelerationTowardsInstance == true and data.AccelTarget ~= nil and data.AccelStrength ~= nil and not data.InvertMotion
	local targetWorldPos
	if hasTargetAccel then
		local t = data.AccelTarget
		-- Same type dispatch as Update.getTargetPosition.
		if t:IsA("Bone") then targetWorldPos = t.TransformedWorldCFrame.Position
		elseif t:IsA("BasePart") then targetWorldPos = t.Position
		elseif t:IsA("Attachment") then targetWorldPos = t.WorldPosition
		elseif t:IsA("Model") then local ok, cf = pcall(t.GetPivot, t); if ok and cf then targetWorldPos = cf.Position end
		end
		if not targetWorldPos then hasTargetAccel = false end
	end
	local targetVel = Vector3.zero
	local accelStrengthSeed = seeds.AccelStrength or {}

	-- PosOffset state. DisplacementMode and spawnEmitterRotation go through Constants.resolveDisplacement
	-- so cached SimLocalCFrames use the same frame as the live Update path. Without spawnEmitterRotation
	-- (preview) it falls back to spawnRotation, so RigidLocal degrades to Local.
	local hasPosOffset = data.PosOffsetX ~= nil or data.PosOffsetY ~= nil or data.PosOffsetZ ~= nil
	-- Under a useVOS link, spawnRotation is link-local as in the live Update path. Cross-file: the
	-- no-VOS branch below mirrors Update._composeLocalDelta; keep the two in sync.
	local spawnRotation = useVOS and (parentCF:ToObjectSpace(initialCF)).Rotation or initialCF.Rotation
	local prevWorldOff = Vector3.zero
	local rotOrder = data.RotOrder or "Global"

	-- A "Rotating" displacement steps as UpdateCommon._turnedFrameDelta does: the offset of t = 0 in the
	-- spawn frame, every later step along the particle's axes mid-step.
	local turns = hasPosOffset and data.DisplacementMode == Constants.TURNING_DISPLACEMENT
	local prevRaw = Vector3.zero
	local startOff = Vector3.zero
	local lastRotX, lastRotY, lastRotZ = 0, 0, 0
	if turns then
		prevRaw = rawOffset(data, seeds, 0)
		startOff = spawnRotation:VectorToWorldSpace(prevRaw)
		lastRotX, lastRotY, lastRotZ = startAngles(data, seeds, rotMode)
	end

	-- Turbulence wander, as Update._posOffsetFrameDelta. Seeds roll lazily into the shared seeds table
	-- so the live emit's Turbulence.buildInto reuses them and InvertMotion replay matches this pre-sim.
	local turbGraph = Turbulence.isLive(data.Turbulence)
	local prevTurbOff = Vector3.zero
	if turbGraph then
		seeds.Turbulence = seeds.Turbulence or GraphMod.GenerateSeed(turbGraph)
		seeds._turbSeed = seeds._turbSeed or (math.random() * 997 + 0.5)
		prevTurbOff = Constants.resolveDisplacement(
			Turbulence.sampleRaw(turbGraph, seeds.Turbulence, seeds._turbSeed, data.TurbulenceFrequency or 1, lifetime, 0),
			data.DisplacementMode or "Global", spawnRotation, spawnEmitterRotation or spawnRotation)
	end

	local localCFrames = {}
	localCFrames[0] = parentCF:ToObjectSpace(initialCF)

	for step = 1, totalKeyFrames do
		local steppedI = step / totalKeyFrames
		local elapsedSec = steppedI * lifetime

		local speed = GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(steppedI, data.Speed, seeds.Speed)
		local draggedSpeed = speed * math.exp(-data.ParticleData.Drag * elapsedSec)

		local accelVelocity = data.ParticleData.Acceleration * elapsedSec

		local displacement = (baseDir * draggedSpeed + accelVelocity) * stepDT

		if hasTargetAccel then
			local toTarget = targetWorldPos - currentPosition
			local dist = toTarget.Magnitude
			if dist > 1e-4 then
				local mag = GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(steppedI, data.AccelStrength, accelStrengthSeed)
				if mag and mag ~= 0 then
					targetVel = targetVel + toTarget * (mag * stepDT / dist)
					displacement = displacement + targetVel * stepDT
				end
			end
		end

		-- This step's rotation angles come before the position: a turning displacement needs them.
		local rotSpeedX = GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(steppedI, data.RotSpeedX, seeds.RotSpeedX)
		local rotSpeedY = GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(steppedI, data.RotSpeedY, seeds.RotSpeedY)
		local rotSpeedZ = GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(steppedI, data.RotSpeedZ, seeds.RotSpeedZ)
		local rotX, rotY, rotZ = rotSpeedX, rotSpeedY, rotSpeedZ
		if rotMode == "Speed" then
			accRotX = accRotX + rotSpeedX * stepDT
			accRotY = accRotY + rotSpeedY * stepDT
			accRotZ = accRotZ + rotSpeedZ * stepDT
			rotX, rotY, rotZ = accRotX, accRotY, accRotZ
		end

		local posDelta = Vector3.zero
		if turns then
			local raw = rawOffset(data, seeds, steppedI)
			local turn = Constants.midRotation(rotOrder, lastRotX, lastRotY, lastRotZ, rotX, rotY, rotZ)
			posDelta = startOff + (spawnRotation * turn):VectorToWorldSpace(raw - prevRaw)
			startOff = Vector3.zero
			prevRaw = raw
			lastRotX, lastRotY, lastRotZ = rotX, rotY, rotZ
		elseif hasPosOffset then
			local worldOff = Constants.resolveDisplacement(rawOffset(data, seeds, steppedI),
				data.DisplacementMode or "Global", spawnRotation,
				spawnEmitterRotation or spawnRotation)
			posDelta = worldOff - prevWorldOff
			prevWorldOff = worldOff
		end
		if turbGraph then
			local turbOff = Constants.resolveDisplacement(
				Turbulence.sampleRaw(turbGraph, seeds.Turbulence, seeds._turbSeed, data.TurbulenceFrequency or 1, lifetime, steppedI),
				data.DisplacementMode or "Global", spawnRotation, spawnEmitterRotation or spawnRotation)
			posDelta = posDelta + (turbOff - prevTurbOff)
			prevTurbOff = turbOff
		end

		-- As Update._composeLocalDelta: only the world velocity goes link-local; a Local-mode offset is
		-- already link-local, else a spinning Weld precesses it.
		local posIsLinkLocal = useVOS and (turns or (data.DisplacementMode or "Global") == "Local")
		local velLocal = useVOS and parentCF:VectorToObjectSpace(displacement) or displacement
		local posLocal = (useVOS and not posIsLinkLocal) and parentCF:VectorToObjectSpace(posDelta) or posDelta
		localCF = CFrame.new(velLocal + posLocal) * localCF

		local rotCF = Constants.composeRotation(rotOrder, rotX, rotY, rotZ)
		local worldCF = (parentCF * localCF) * rotCF
		currentPosition = worldCF.Position

		if data.VelocityVectored then
			local dirInfo = DirectionVectors[emissionDirection] or DirectionVectors[Enum.NormalId.Top]
			baseDir = (worldCF * spreadRotation)[dirInfo.vector] * dirInfo.multiplier
		end

		localCFrames[step] = parentCF:ToObjectSpace(worldCF)
	end

	return localCFrames, totalKeyFrames
end

-- Attachment variant: no Link param, attachment-local space (initialCF doubles as localCF).
function Particle:PreSimulateAttachmentForward(data, seeds, initialCF, baseDirection, spreadRotation, lifetime, previewMaxSteps, spawnEmitterRotation)
	local INVERT_MAX_STEPS = 500
	local totalKeyFrames = math.max(1, data.TotalKeyFrames)
	if previewMaxSteps and totalKeyFrames > previewMaxSteps then
		totalKeyFrames = previewMaxSteps
	elseif data.InvertMotion and totalKeyFrames > INVERT_MAX_STEPS then
		totalKeyFrames = INVERT_MAX_STEPS
	end
	local stepDT = lifetime / totalKeyFrames

	local localCF = initialCF
	local baseDir = baseDirection
	local emissionDirection = data.EmissionDirection
	local rotMode = data.RotMode or "OverLife"
	local accRotX, accRotY, accRotZ = 0, 0, 0
	-- AccelerationTowardsInstance is not integrated here (local space vs world target), so previews
	-- diverge from the live emit when target acceleration is on.

	-- PosOffset state, via Constants.resolveDisplacement as in PreSimulateForward.
	local hasPosOffset = data.PosOffsetX ~= nil or data.PosOffsetY ~= nil or data.PosOffsetZ ~= nil
	local spawnRotation = initialCF.Rotation
	local prevWorldOff = Vector3.zero
	local rotOrder = data.RotOrder or "Global"

	-- A "Rotating" displacement; state and steps mirror PreSimulateForward.
	local turns = hasPosOffset and data.DisplacementMode == Constants.TURNING_DISPLACEMENT
	local prevRaw = Vector3.zero
	local startOff = Vector3.zero
	local lastRotX, lastRotY, lastRotZ = 0, 0, 0
	if turns then
		prevRaw = rawOffset(data, seeds, 0)
		startOff = spawnRotation:VectorToWorldSpace(prevRaw)
		lastRotX, lastRotY, lastRotZ = startAngles(data, seeds, rotMode)
	end

	-- Turbulence wander; seed handling mirrors PreSimulateForward.
	local turbGraph = Turbulence.isLive(data.Turbulence)
	local prevTurbOff = Vector3.zero
	if turbGraph then
		seeds.Turbulence = seeds.Turbulence or GraphMod.GenerateSeed(turbGraph)
		seeds._turbSeed = seeds._turbSeed or (math.random() * 997 + 0.5)
		prevTurbOff = Constants.resolveDisplacement(
			Turbulence.sampleRaw(turbGraph, seeds.Turbulence, seeds._turbSeed, data.TurbulenceFrequency or 1, lifetime, 0),
			data.DisplacementMode or "Global", spawnRotation, spawnEmitterRotation or spawnRotation)
	end

	local localCFrames = {}
	localCFrames[0] = initialCF

	for step = 1, totalKeyFrames do
		local steppedI = step / totalKeyFrames
		local elapsedSec = steppedI * lifetime

		local speed = GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(steppedI, data.Speed, seeds.Speed)
		local draggedSpeed = speed * math.exp(-data.ParticleData.Drag * elapsedSec)

		local accelVelocity = data.ParticleData.Acceleration * elapsedSec
		local displacement = (baseDir * draggedSpeed + accelVelocity) * stepDT

		-- This step's rotation angles come before the position: a turning displacement needs them.
		local rotSpeedX = GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(steppedI, data.RotSpeedX, seeds.RotSpeedX)
		local rotSpeedY = GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(steppedI, data.RotSpeedY, seeds.RotSpeedY)
		local rotSpeedZ = GraphMod.QueryPointsWithTime(steppedI, data.RotSpeedZ, seeds.RotSpeedZ)
		local rotX, rotY, rotZ = rotSpeedX, rotSpeedY, rotSpeedZ
		if rotMode == "Speed" then
			accRotX = accRotX + rotSpeedX * stepDT
			accRotY = accRotY + rotSpeedY * stepDT
			accRotZ = accRotZ + rotSpeedZ * stepDT
			rotX, rotY, rotZ = accRotX, accRotY, accRotZ
		end

		if turns then
			local raw = rawOffset(data, seeds, steppedI)
			local turn = Constants.midRotation(rotOrder, lastRotX, lastRotY, lastRotZ, rotX, rotY, rotZ)
			displacement = displacement + startOff + (spawnRotation * turn):VectorToWorldSpace(raw - prevRaw)
			startOff = Vector3.zero
			prevRaw = raw
			lastRotX, lastRotY, lastRotZ = rotX, rotY, rotZ
		elseif hasPosOffset then
			local worldOff = Constants.resolveDisplacement(rawOffset(data, seeds, steppedI),
				data.DisplacementMode or "Global", spawnRotation,
				spawnEmitterRotation or spawnRotation)
			displacement = displacement + (worldOff - prevWorldOff)
			prevWorldOff = worldOff
		end
		if turbGraph then
			local turbOff = Constants.resolveDisplacement(
				Turbulence.sampleRaw(turbGraph, seeds.Turbulence, seeds._turbSeed, data.TurbulenceFrequency or 1, lifetime, steppedI),
				data.DisplacementMode or "Global", spawnRotation, spawnEmitterRotation or spawnRotation)
			displacement = displacement + (turbOff - prevTurbOff)
			prevTurbOff = turbOff
		end

		localCF = CFrame.new(displacement) * localCF

		local rotCF = Constants.composeRotation(rotOrder, rotX, rotY, rotZ)
		local worldCF = localCF * rotCF

		if data.VelocityVectored then
			local dirVecInfo = DirectionVectors[emissionDirection] or DirectionVectors[Enum.NormalId.Top]
			baseDir = (worldCF * spreadRotation)[dirVecInfo.vector] * dirVecInfo.multiplier
		end

		localCFrames[step] = worldCF
	end

	return localCFrames, totalKeyFrames
end

end

--[[
	Reactor mixin  -  a transformed Model or Part whose parts are pieces that Forces push.
	At rest a Reactor costs nothing. When a Force is emitted, every Reactor it could reach
	(Reactor/Index) gets a play (Reactor/Play) and a pData; the play moves stand-ins and hides the
	originals (Reactor/Display), never moving them. A play whose pieces lie still goes dormant.
	Emit puts a Reactor back as built; at an origin it stands it up there as stand-ins (Play:place).
	Disable, the engine's shutdown and a Reactor leaving the world restore it.
	Break = "Shards" (and "Blocks" on a part that is not a plain box): the engine cuts fragments
	(Reactor/Shards), which yields; a Reactor without its shards is cut first and answers a few frames
	late (_reactorCutting). PrepareReactor cuts ahead (every Reactor when a game starts, the selected
	one in the plugin). "Around hit" and "Cracks" are cut around the first Force, so always answer it
	late; a later Impulse cracks the ground again (Reactor/Recrack).
	What one Force sets off breaks in one frame (Reactor/Batch, _tellEntry).
	A mesh part-icle with Reacts becomes a Reactor when a Force reaches its copy (Reactor/HandOver);
	its entry has an owner (Reactor/Owned) and ends with the copy.
	Cross-file: Lifecycle.Disable calls RestoreReactor and Engine's Deactivate RestoreAllReactors, or
	a hidden original stays hidden; Engine's Activate calls ShowStrandedReactors.
]]

local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")

local TypeRegistry = require(script.Parent.TypeRegistry)
local ForceRegistry = require(script.Parent.Force.Registry)
local Index = require(script.Index)
local Entries = require(script.Entries)
local Pieces = require(script.Pieces)
local Display = require(script.Display)
local Owned = require(script.Owned)
local HandOver = require(script.HandOver)
local Batch = require(script.Batch)

return function(Particle)

-- reactor -> its entry (Reactor/Entries): every Reactor that is not at rest.
Particle._reactorPlays = {}
-- reactor -> { records, place, emitCtx }: Reactors being cut now.
Particle._reactorCutting = {}

-- Shared by the Emit and EmitAnimate dispatch.
function Particle._isReactor(item)
	return (item:IsA("Model") or item:IsA("BasePart")) and item:GetAttribute("IsReactor") == true
end

-- Marks a Model or Part as a Reactor: the config, the attributes every transformed item carries
-- (Reactor/Index.MARKS) and the tag. Nothing under it changes.
function Particle:TransformReactor(item, typeDef)
	if item:GetAttribute("Transformed") then return end
	TypeRegistry.createConfig(item, typeDef)
	item:SetAttribute("Transformed", true)
	item:SetAttribute("Qwinkle", true)
	item:SetAttribute("EmitCount", 1)
	item:SetAttribute("EmitDuration", 0)
	item:SetAttribute("EmitDelay", 0)
	item:SetAttribute("IsEmitter", true)
	item:SetAttribute("EmissionMode", "Emit")
	item:SetAttribute("AnimateLoop", false)
	CollectionService:AddTag(item, Index.TAG)
	pcall(function() Particle.TransformCompleted:Fire(item) end)
end

-- A ball around a Reactor at rest, without reading its pieces (a one-part Reactor's parts included).
local function roughBounds(reactor)
	if reactor:IsA("Model") then
		local frame, size = reactor:GetBoundingBox()
		return frame.Position, size.Magnitude / 2
	end
	local centre = reactor.ExtentsCFrame.Position
	local radius = reactor.ExtentsSize.Magnitude / 2
	for _, descendant in ipairs(reactor:GetDescendants()) do
		if descendant:IsA("BasePart") then
			radius = math.max(radius, (descendant.ExtentsCFrame.Position - centre).Magnitude + descendant.ExtentsSize.Magnitude / 2)
		end
	end
	return centre, radius
end

-- Whether a Force just emitted could reach a Reactor at rest.
local function couldReach(record, reactor)
	local config = TypeRegistry.getConfig(reactor)
	if not config or not Index.groupMatches(record.group, config:GetAttribute("Group") or "") then
		return false
	end
	local centre, radius = roughBounds(reactor)
	return Index.reaches(record.field, centre, radius)
end

-- Tells an entry of a Force. One nothing has moved yet answers with the rest of the pass
-- (Reactor/Batch), its grounds struck now; any other follows at once.
function Particle:_tellEntry(entry, record, fresh)
	local waiting = entry.waiting
	if not fresh and not waiting then
		Entries.follow(self, entry, record)
		return
	end
	if entry.wounds then
		entry.wounds:strike(record)
	end
	if waiting then
		if not table.find(waiting, record) then
			table.insert(waiting, record)
		end
		return
	end
	waiting = { record }
	entry.waiting = waiting
	Batch.hold(function(late)
		entry.waiting = nil
		local reactor = entry.reactor
		local owner = entry.owner
		if self._reactorPlays[reactor] ~= entry or (owner and owner.leaving) then
			return
		end
		-- A copy's Impulse strikes when answered: it may be over before the play's first step.
		late = late or owner ~= nil
		for _, told in ipairs(waiting) do
			if self._reactorPlays[reactor] == entry then
				Entries.follow(self, entry, told, late)
			end
		end
		-- Nothing moved and no Force is left: at rest again.
		if self._reactorPlays[reactor] == entry and not entry.pData then
			Entries.discard(self, entry)
		end
	end)
end

-- One pass over the Reactors for one Force (Reactor/Batch.pass).
local function tellReactors(self, record)
	for _, reactor in ipairs(Index.reactors()) do
		local entry = self._reactorPlays[reactor]
		local fresh = false
		if entry then
			if not Index.groupMatches(record.group, entry.group) then
				entry = nil
			end
		elseif couldReach(record, reactor) then
			local cutting
			entry, cutting = Entries.entryFor(self, reactor, nil, record)
			fresh = entry ~= nil
			if cutting then
				Entries.owe(cutting, record)
			end
		end
		if entry then
			self:_tellEntry(entry, record, fresh)
		end
	end
	self:_followReacted(record)
end

-- A Force emitted or moved (Force/Registry announces it again): every Reactor it could reach follows
-- it; one out of place follows any Force of its Group. Safe to call again.
function Particle:_reactToForce(record)
	if not self.Connection then return end
	Batch.pass(tellReactors, self, record)
end

function Particle:UpdateReactor(pData, dt, currentTime)
	local entry = pData._entry
	local reactor = entry.reactor
	if not reactor.Parent or self._reactorPlays[reactor] ~= entry then
		Entries.putBack(entry)
		if self._reactorPlays[reactor] == entry then
			self._reactorPlays[reactor] = nil
			Owned.gone(self, entry.owner, false)
		end
		return true
	end

	-- The slowest of the Containers whose Forces reached it; SetTimescale wins.
	local timescale = ForceRegistry.slowest(entry.play.times)
	local override = nil
	if pData._tsOverride ~= nil and currentTime < (pData._tsOverrideUntil or 0) then
		override = pData._tsOverride
		timescale = override
	end
	local frozen = pData._timeFrozen == true
	local step = 0
	if not frozen then
		step = dt * math.max(timescale, 0)
	end

	local status = Entries.step(entry, step, dt, override, frozen)
	if status == "active" then
		return false
	end
	if status == "done" then
		self._reactorPlays[reactor] = nil
		Owned.gone(self, entry.owner, true)
	elseif Owned.spent(entry) then
		-- A copy with nothing left to show.
		Entries.discard(self, entry, true)
	end
	return true
end

-- Puts a Reactor back as built; at an origin, stands it up there as stand-ins.
function Particle:EmitReactor(item, link, emitCtx)
	if not item or not item.Parent then return end
	local standing = self._reactorPlays[item]
	if standing then
		Entries.discard(self, standing)
	end
	Entries.forget(self._reactorCutting[item])
	if not Entries.emitOrigin(emitCtx) then return end
	local entry, cutting = Entries.entryFor(self, item, emitCtx)
	if cutting then
		cutting.place = true
		cutting.emitCtx = emitCtx
	end
	if not entry then return end
	entry.play:place()
	if not Entries.resume(self, entry) then
		Entries.discard(self, entry)
	end
end

-- Puts one Reactor back; one being cut gets no play.
function Particle:RestoreReactor(item)
	Entries.forget(self._reactorCutting[item])
	local entry = self._reactorPlays[item]
	if entry then
		Entries.discard(self, entry)
	end
end

function Particle:RestoreAllReactors()
	for _, cutting in pairs(self._reactorCutting) do
		Entries.forget(cutting)
	end
	for _, entry in pairs(table.clone(self._reactorPlays)) do
		Entries.discard(self, entry)
	end
	-- A copy still being cut has no entry.
	for _, owner in ipairs(table.clone(self._reacted)) do
		Owned.gone(self, owner, false)
	end
end

-- Shows every Reactor part hidden with no play to answer for it (a session that crashed or
-- reloaded mid-play). From Engine's Activate.
function Particle:ShowStrandedReactors()
	for _, reactor in ipairs(Index.reactors()) do
		if not self._reactorPlays[reactor] then
			for _, part in ipairs(Pieces.parts(reactor)) do
				if part.LocalTransparencyModifier ~= 0 then
					Display.unhide(part)
				end
			end
		end
	end
end

-- Cuts a Reactor's shards now, so its first Force finds them. Returns at once.
function Particle:PrepareReactor(item)
	Entries.prepare(self, item)
end

-- Every Reactor in the world, when a game starts.
function Particle:PrepareReactors()
	for _, reactor in ipairs(Index.reactors()) do
		self:PrepareReactor(reactor)
	end
end

HandOver(Particle)

ForceRegistry.onAdded(function(record)
	Particle:_reactToForce(record)
end)

end

--[[
	After  -  what a play does once its pieces have come to rest and After is Fade or Return. Part
	of Reactor/Play: it reads and writes the play's own tables.

	After.fade(play, dt): every piece that lies where it fell sinks into the surface it lies on,
	along that surface's normal, until it is wholly under it, and its stand-in is then removed.
	How far a piece sinks is its own thickness along the normal and a little more, so a thin
	slab goes just under while a tall block goes all the way.
	After.back(play, dt): each such piece flies its last path backwards, and before that goes
	back the way a Continuous Force carried it (Reactor/Driven: round a tornado as it came),
	then eases onto its rest pose; pieces of cracked ground stood out of place (Reactor/Crack)
	ease back with them. A play in place is then restored; a placed one stands again where it
	was placed.
	After.anyLanded(play): whether there is anything to fade or to return.
	After.close(play, dt): the ground grows back. Every piece that is gone (sunk away by a
	Fade, or lost in the air) gets a stand-in again and rises into its place from under it,
	the cracked ones ease to rest, and the play is restored. For a play whose settings say
	`closes`: a wound of a ground (Reactor/Wounds), which gives its ground back when it is done.
	After.begin(play) -> the phase a play enters when its wait is over.

	All of them return what Play:step returns: "active", "dormant" or "done".
]]

local Trajectory = require(script.Parent.Parent.Rocks.Trajectory)
local Crack = require(script.Parent.Crack)
local Driven = require(script.Parent.Driven)

local RESTING = 0
local LANDED = 2
local GONE = 3

local UP = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
local TINY = 1e-4
-- Fade: a piece ends this share of its thickness, and this many studs, under the surface.
local SINK_MARGIN_SHARE = 0.15
local SINK_MARGIN_STUDS = 0.1
-- Return: the share of the time spent flying the path backwards; the rest eases onto the rest pose.
local RETURN_PATH_SHARE = 0.85

local After = {}

-- How far a box of `halfExt`, turned as `frame`, reaches along a unit direction.
local function reachAlong(frame, halfExt, direction)
	return math.abs(frame.XVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.X
		+ math.abs(frame.YVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.Y
		+ math.abs(frame.ZVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.Z
end

-- How far a landed piece must sink along `normal` to be wholly under the surface it lies on.
function After.sinkDepth(frame, halfExt, normal)
	local thickness = 2 * reachAlong(frame, halfExt, normal)
	return thickness * (1 + SINK_MARGIN_SHARE) + SINK_MARGIN_STUDS
end

function After.anyLanded(play)
	for index in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] == LANDED then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

function After.fade(play, dt)
	play.phaseTime += dt
	local progress = math.clamp(play.phaseTime / math.max(play.settings.AfterTime, TINY), 0, 1)
	local sink = progress * progress
	local count = 0
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] == LANDED then
			local frame = play.lastFrame[index]
			local normal = play.path[index].restNormal or UP
			count += 1
			play.moveIndices[count] = index
			play.moveFrames[count] = frame + normal * (-After.sinkDepth(frame, piece.halfExt, normal) * sink)
		end
	end
	play:_flush(count)
	if progress < 1 then
		return "active"
	end
	for index in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] == LANDED then
			play.state[index] = GONE
			play.display.drop(index)
			play.awake -= 1
		end
	end
	if play.settings.closes then
		play.phase = "closing"
		play.phaseTime = 0
		return "active"
	end
	play.phase = "live"
	return "dormant"
end

function After.begin(play)
	if play.settings.After == "Return" then
		return "returning"
	end
	if After.anyLanded(play) or not play.settings.closes then
		return "fading"
	end
	return "closing"
end

function After.close(play, dt)
	if play.phaseTime == 0 then
		-- Reactor/Display makes the stand-ins a part's pieces are missing.
		for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
			if play.state[index] == GONE and not piece.retired then
				play.display.wake(index)
			end
		end
	end
	play.phaseTime += dt
	local progress = math.clamp(play.phaseTime / math.max(play.settings.AfterTime, TINY), 0, 1)
	local left = (1 - progress) * (1 - progress)
	local count = 0
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] == GONE and not piece.retired then
			local normal = UP
			if piece.strike then
				normal = piece.strike.normal
			end
			count += 1
			play.moveIndices[count] = index
			play.moveFrames[count] = piece.rest + normal * (-After.sinkDepth(piece.rest, piece.halfExt, normal) * left)
		end
	end
	play:_flush(Crack.returning(play, progress, count))
	if progress < 1 then
		return "active"
	end
	play:restore()
	return "done"
end

function After.back(play, dt)
	play.phaseTime += dt
	local progress = math.clamp(play.phaseTime / math.max(play.settings.AfterTime, TINY), 0, 1)
	local count = 0
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] == LANDED then
			local frame
			local track = play.track[index]
			local carried = 0
			if track then
				carried = track.times[#track.times]
			end
			if progress < RETURN_PATH_SHARE then
				-- Seconds of its way left to go back: the flight first, then what carried it.
				local left = (play.landedAfter[index] + carried) * (1 - progress / RETURN_PATH_SHARE)
				-- A piece that only lies (Reactor/Recarve) has no way to go back but its place.
				if not track or left > carried then
					frame = Trajectory.evaluate(play.path[index], left - carried, play.gravity[index])
				else
					frame = Driven.poseAt(track, left)
				end
			else
				local start
				if track then
					start = track.frames[1]
				else
					start = Trajectory.evaluate(play.path[index], 0, play.gravity[index])
				end
				frame = start:Lerp(piece.rest, (progress - RETURN_PATH_SHARE) / (1 - RETURN_PATH_SHARE))
			end
			count += 1
			play.moveIndices[count] = index
			play.moveFrames[count] = frame
		end
	end
	play:_flush(Crack.returning(play, progress, count))
	if progress < 1 then
		return "active"
	end
	if not play.placed then
		play:restore()
		return "done"
	end
	-- A placed Reactor stands where it was placed again: the stand-ins stay, back at rest.
	for index in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] == LANDED then
			play.state[index] = RESTING
		end
	end
	play.cracked = {}
	play.crackFrame = {}
	play.track = {}
	play.phase = "live"
	play.phaseTime = 0
	play.idleFor = 0
	return "dormant"
end

return After

--[[
	Batch: what one Force sets off breaks in one frame.

	The engine hands back about two cuts a frame however many are asked, so cuts made as a Force
	reaches things would break two a frame in turn. A pass is one telling: one Force told to the
	Reactors (Reactor/init), or the copies that Forces reach in one frame (Reactor/HandOver). Every cut
	asked for inside a pass takes a ticket, and what the cut owes when it is in (an entry and the
	Force's strike, a wound that shows) is held until the pass's last cut is in; then all of it is
	answered at once. What needs no cut waits with the rest (hold). A pass that cuts nothing answers as
	it ends. No batch holds an answer longer than LONGEST: then what is in is answered, and every cut
	still out as it comes.

	Batch.pass(work, ...)        runs work(...) as a pass; a pass begun inside it is part of it
	Batch.take() -> ticket       inside a pass: one cut the pass waits for; nil outside one
	Batch.give(ticket, answer)   the cut is in; with no ticket the answer runs at once
	Batch.hold(answer)           inside a pass: an answer that needs no cut; outside one it runs at once
	An answer is called with `late`: true when it waited for a cut, false when it runs as its pass
	ends. Each runs in its own thread: one that fails takes none of the others along.

	Logic only: no instance is read.
]]

local Batch = {}

-- Seconds a batch holds its answers at most, so a cut the engine never returns holds nothing up for good.
Batch.LONGEST = 3

-- How many passes run, one inside another, and the batch they share. It is made when the first
-- ticket or answer asks for it: a pass that sets nothing off makes none.
local depth = 0
local current = nil

-- Answers everything the batch holds; from here on it holds nothing and later arrivals run as they come.
local function release(batch, late)
	if batch.answered then
		return
	end
	batch.answered = true
	local held = batch.held
	batch.held = {}
	for _, answer in ipairs(held) do
		task.spawn(answer, late)
	end
end

local function inPass()
	if depth == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	if not current then
		current = { waits = 0, held = {}, closed = false, answered = false }
	end
	return current
end

function Batch.pass(work, ...)
	depth += 1
	local ok, problem = xpcall(work, debug.traceback, ...)
	depth -= 1
	if depth == 0 then
		local batch = current
		current = nil
		if batch then
			batch.closed = true
			if batch.waits == 0 then
				release(batch, false)
			else
				task.delay(Batch.LONGEST, release, batch, true)
			end
		end
	end
	if not ok then
		error(problem, 0)
	end
end

function Batch.take()
	local batch = inPass()
	if batch then
		batch.waits += 1
	end
	return batch
end

function Batch.give(ticket, answer)
	if not ticket then
		answer(false)
		return
	end
	if ticket.answered then
		answer(true)
		return
	end
	ticket.waits -= 1
	table.insert(ticket.held, answer)
	if ticket.waits == 0 and ticket.closed then
		release(ticket, true)
	end
end

function Batch.hold(answer)
	local batch = inPass()
	if not batch then
		answer(false)
		return
	end
	table.insert(batch.held, answer)
end

return Batch

--[[
	Blade: the cut of a Linear Force that has a Cut (Force/init: record.cut). Vector3 and CFrame
	maths only, no instances.

	The blade is the Force's box (Width x Height, from Inner to Range along its heading). The cut
	goes across the thinner of Width and Height; that thinner side is the kerf, and where the box
	ends inside a part the cut ends too (Reactor/Carve).

	Blade.of(field, cut) -> blade, or nil for a non-Linear shape or a blade with no length
	  blade = { frame, size, origin, heading, normal, across, kerf }
	    frame, size  the box in the world (X width, Y height, Z length)
	    origin       a point of the cut's plane
	    heading      unit way the Force heads, in the plane
	    normal       the plane's unit normal (the box's thinner side)
	    across       unit way across the blade, in the plane
	    kerf         the cut's width, never under LEAST_KERF
	  With cut.noise over 0 the cut is jagged: a zig-zag ribbon along one way of the blade
	  (Blade.ribbonFor picks lengthwise or crosswise), a joint every cut.noiseScale studs (at most
	  MOST_JOINTS), straying up to cut.noise but held to STEEPEST of the stretch between joints.
	  blade.size then holds either ribbon (wider by blade.stray) and blade.flat is the clean box.
	Blade.ribbon(blade, lengthwise) -> nil for a clean blade, else
	  { key, lengthwise, tool, frames, straight, length, stray, joints, step, flat }: a box of size
	  `tool` set at each of `frames` (in blade.frame space), joined up and stretched to `length`
	  along axis `straight`, is the cutter. key is the Force's cut table (Reactor/Ribbon caches by it).
	Blade.ribbonFor(blade, frame, size, toSpace) -> ribbon in `toSpace`, or nil for a clean blade
	  Lengthwise when the blade runs farther through the box along its heading than across it.
	  Asked with the whole part's box so all its pieces share one surface.
	Blade.touches(blade, frame, size) -> whether the blade's box meets the box `size` at `frame`
	Blade.side(blade, position) -> 1 where the normal points, -1 on the other side
	Blade.slope(blade) -> over, downhill, sine, cosine
	  over      side (1 or -1) lying on top of the cut, 0 for an upright cut
	  downhill  unit way down the cut's slope, in the plane; nil for an upright or level cut
	  sine, cosine  of the angle between the cut and level ground
	Blade.inPart(blade, frame) -> the blade's frame in the space of a part at `frame`
]]

local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)

local Blade = {}

-- A blade thinner than this is cut this wide: solid modelling needs some width.
local LEAST_KERF = 0.1
-- Noise under this many studs is a clean cut.
local LEAST_NOISE = 0.01
-- A jag is never shorter than this.
local LEAST_GRAIN = 0.5
local MOST_JOINTS = 96
-- The most a joint strays, as a share of the stretch between two joints.
local STEEPEST = 0.9
-- A ribbon is this much thicker than the kerf: its slopes take that off again.
local THICKER = 1.25
-- A joint strays by itself for this share of its stray, the rest is a slow wander of WANDER joints.
local OWN_SHARE = 0.65
local WANDER = 4
-- A ribbon's box is this thin along its path; Reactor/Ribbon stretches the swept result.
local TOOL_DEPTH = 0.05
local SWEPT_LENGTH = 8
local SIGNS = { -1, 1 }
-- A cut whose normal is this near level is upright: neither side lies on the other.
local UPRIGHT = 0.05
-- A cut whose normal is this near straight up is level: nothing slides on it.
local LEVEL = 0.02
local TINY = 1e-6

local UP = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)

local X_AXIS = Vector3.new(1, 0, 0)
local Y_AXIS = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
local Z_AXIS = Vector3.new(0, 0, 1)

-- How many joints a path of `length` gets, and how far apart they lie.
local function jointsOf(length, grain)
	local count = math.clamp(math.ceil(length / grain), 1, MOST_JOINTS)
	return count, length / count
end

-- The strays of a zig-zag of `count` stretches: every joint within `amount` of the plane.
local function straysOf(count, amount, random)
	local knots = {}
	for knot = 0, math.ceil(count / WANDER) + 1 do
		knots[knot] = random() * 2 - 1
	end
	local strays = table.create(count + 1)
	for joint = 0, count do
		local at = joint / WANDER
		local low = math.floor(at)
		local wander = knots[low] + (knots[low + 1] - knots[low]) * (at - low)
		strays[joint + 1] = (OWN_SHARE * (random() * 2 - 1) + (1 - OWN_SHARE) * wander) * amount
	end
	return strays
end

function Blade.of(field, cut)
	if field.shape ~= "Linear" then
		return nil
	end
	local length = field.range - field.inner
	if length <= 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local origin = field.origin
	local width = field.halfWidth * 2
	local height = field.halfHeight * 2
	local normal = origin.RightVector
	local across = origin.UpVector
	local thinIsWidth = true
	if height < width then
		thinIsWidth = false
		normal = origin.UpVector
		across = origin.RightVector
		height = math.max(height, LEAST_KERF)
		width = math.max(width, height)
	else
		width = math.max(width, LEAST_KERF)
		height = math.max(height, width)
	end
	local blade = {
		frame = origin * CFrame.new(0, 0, -(field.inner + field.range) / 2),
		size = Vector3.new(width, height, length),
		origin = origin.Position,
		heading = origin.LookVector,
		normal = normal,
		across = across,
		kerf = math.min(width, height),
		thinIsWidth = thinIsWidth,
	}
	if cut and (cut.noise or 0) > LEAST_NOISE then
		local grain = math.max(cut.noiseScale or 0, LEAST_GRAIN)
		local _, alongStep = jointsOf(length, grain)
		local _, acrossStep = jointsOf(math.max(width, height), grain)
		blade.key = cut
		blade.noise = cut.noise
		blade.grain = grain
		blade.flat = blade.size
		blade.ribbons = {}
		blade.stray = math.min(cut.noise, STEEPEST * math.max(alongStep, acrossStep))
		if blade.thinIsWidth then
			blade.size += Vector3.new(2 * blade.stray, 0, 0)
		else
			blade.size += Vector3.new(0, 2 * blade.stray, 0)
		end
	end
	return blade
end

function Blade.ribbon(blade, lengthwise)
	if not blade.noise then
		return nil
	end
	local kept = blade.ribbons[lengthwise]
	if kept then
		return kept
	end
	local flat = blade.flat
	local thin, across, acrossName, wide = Y_AXIS, X_AXIS, "X", flat.X
	if blade.thinIsWidth then
		thin, across, acrossName, wide = X_AXIS, Y_AXIS, "Y", flat.Y
	end
	-- The zig-zag runs along `way`; along `ruling` the ribbon is straight.
	local way, ruling, straight, pathLength, rulingLength = across, Z_AXIS, "Z", wide, flat.Z
	if lengthwise then
		way, ruling, straight, pathLength, rulingLength = Z_AXIS, across, acrossName, flat.Z, wide
	end
	local joints, step = jointsOf(pathLength, blade.grain)
	local stray = math.min(blade.noise, STEEPEST * step)
	local strays = straysOf(joints, stray, Sites.sequence(Sites.seedAt(blade.origin)))
	-- The box is only moved from joint to joint, never turned: boxes that stand alike join much faster.
	local depth = thin:Cross(ruling)
	local frames = table.create(joints + 1)
	for joint = 0, joints do
		frames[joint + 1] = CFrame.fromMatrix(way * (-pathLength / 2 + joint * step) + thin * strays[joint + 1], thin, ruling, depth)
	end
	local ribbon = {
		key = blade.key,
		lengthwise = lengthwise,
		tool = Vector3.new(blade.kerf * THICKER, math.min(rulingLength, SWEPT_LENGTH), TOOL_DEPTH),
		frames = frames,
		straight = straight,
		length = rulingLength,
		stray = stray,
		joints = joints,
		step = step,
		flat = flat,
	}
	blade.ribbons[lengthwise] = ribbon
	return ribbon
end

-- The three unit axes of a frame.
local function axesOf(frame)
	return { frame.XVector, frame.YVector, frame.ZVector }
end

-- How far a box of half-lengths `half` along `axes` reaches along `direction`.
local function reach(axes, half, direction)
	return math.abs(axes[1]:Dot(direction)) * half.X + math.abs(axes[2]:Dot(direction)) * half.Y + math.abs(axes[3]:Dot(direction)) * half.Z
end

-- Separating axis test: the six face normals and nine edge cross products.
function Blade.touches(blade, frame, size)
	local bladeAxes = axesOf(blade.frame)
	local partAxes = axesOf(frame)
	local bladeHalf = blade.size / 2
	local partHalf = size / 2
	local between = frame.Position - blade.frame.Position
	local function separates(axis)
		local length = axis.Magnitude
		if length < TINY then
			return false
		end
		local unit = axis / length
		return math.abs(between:Dot(unit)) > reach(bladeAxes, bladeHalf, unit) + reach(partAxes, partHalf, unit)
	end
	for index = 1, 3 do
		if separates(bladeAxes[index]) or separates(partAxes[index]) then
			return false
		end
	end
	for _, bladeAxis in ipairs(bladeAxes) do
		for _, partAxis in ipairs(partAxes) do
			if separates(bladeAxis:Cross(partAxis)) then
				return false
			end
		end
	end
	return true
end

function Blade.ribbonFor(blade, frame, size, toSpace)
	if not blade.noise then
		return nil, nil
	end
	-- The box's shadow on the blade's plane, in blade space.
	local own = blade.frame
	local half = size / 2
	local lowAlong, highAlong, lowAcross, highAcross = math.huge, -math.huge, math.huge, -math.huge
	for _, x in ipairs(SIGNS) do
		for _, y in ipairs(SIGNS) do
			for _, z in ipairs(SIGNS) do
				local corner = own:PointToObjectSpace(frame:PointToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(x * half.X, y * half.Y, z * half.Z)))
				local across = corner.X
				if blade.thinIsWidth then
					across = corner.Y
				end
				lowAlong = math.min(lowAlong, corner.Z)
				highAlong = math.max(highAlong, corner.Z)
				lowAcross = math.min(lowAcross, across)
				highAcross = math.max(highAcross, across)
			end
		end
	end
	local flat = blade.flat
	local wide = flat.X
	if blade.thinIsWidth then
		wide = flat.Y
	end
	local alongRun = math.min(highAlong, flat.Z / 2) - math.max(lowAlong, -flat.Z / 2)
	local acrossRun = math.min(highAcross, wide / 2) - math.max(lowAcross, -wide / 2)
	return Blade.ribbon(blade, alongRun >= acrossRun), toSpace * own
end

function Blade.side(blade, position)
	if (position - blade.origin):Dot(blade.normal) >= 0 then
		return 1
	end
	return -1
end

function Blade.slope(blade)
	local normal = blade.normal
	local rise = normal:Dot(UP)
	local cosine = math.abs(rise)
	local sine = math.sqrt(math.max(1 - cosine * cosine, 0))
	if cosine < UPRIGHT then
		return 0, nil, sine, cosine
	end
	local over = 1
	if rise < 0 then
		over = -1
	end
	if sine < LEVEL then
		return over, nil, sine, cosine
	end
	-- Straight down, laid onto the plane.
	local down = -UP + normal * rise
	return over, down.Unit, sine, cosine
end

function Blade.inPart(blade, frame)
	return frame:ToObjectSpace(blade.frame)
end

return Blade

--[[
	Carve  -  a part cut by a blade (Reactor/Blade): the engine's solid modelling
	(GeometryService:SubtractAsync) takes the blade's box out of the part. A blade that passes
	through leaves two or more sides with the kerf between them; one that ends inside leaves ONE
	side with a slot. The part is read and never changed: the sides are templates kept out of the
	world, as a part's shards are (Reactor/Shards), and Reactor/Display copies its stand-ins from them.

	The engine carries its source's colour into what it cuts, so the cut is made of a WHITE copy
	of the part, never parented, and a stand-in takes the part's colour. A union that shows its own
	parts' colours is cut as it is, and its results are marked baked, which Reactor/Display leaves.

	The cut's mode (the Force's Cut):
	  Halves   the sides stay whole
	  Pieces   every side breaks into the part's own pieces: its shards, or its blocks
	  Band     the sides stay whole, and what the blade took out flies off as debris

	Carve.key(part, bladeFrame, bladeSize, mode, count, seed, grid, grain) -> string
	    everything a cut depends on; bladeFrame is the blade's box in the part's own space,
	    grain a jagged blade's.
	Carve.cut(job, fragment, shardOf) -> shards or false. Yields.
	    job: { part, bladeFrame, bladeSize, slash, mode, count, seed, grid, stands }
	    (Reactor/CutPlan; Reactor/Footprint for a ground's patch, with stands = true: the ground's
	    side is fixed and never breaks).
	    slash = { origin, normal, heading, kerf } in the part's space: the cut's plane.
	    A piece cut AGAIN (Reactor/Recarve) comes with more:
	      frame      the space its boxes are told in, where the part itself is not what is cut
	      template   the piece's own shard, cut as it is (white already, or baked: job.baked)
	      blockSize  for a block of Reactor/Dice: a box of that size is made and cut
	      points     for mode Pieces, the points its sides break around, in that space
	    A jagged blade's job carries ribbon and ribbonFrame (Reactor/Blade.ribbonFor): a copy of
	    the ribbon's cutter (Reactor/Ribbon) is taken out in place of the box.
	    always = true (a ground's patch): the one side is given back even when nothing was taken.
	    fragment(part, points) and shardOf(template, frame, fixed, siteIndex) are Reactor/Shards'.
	    Each shard has one mark more:
	      side   1 or -1: the side of the cut it lies on (Reactor/Slash moves the sides)
	      bit    true for a piece of what the blade took out
	      baked  true when its colours are in its geometry
	    A lone side is fixed: it is the part, with a slot. shards.slash is the job's. false: the
	    engine refused, or the blade took nothing out (its box met the part's box, not its shape).
	    A refusal comes with the engine's reason as a second value, which Reactor/Shards keeps.
]]

local GeometryService = game:GetService("GeometryService")
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Dice = require(script.Parent.Dice)
local Ribbon = require(script.Parent.Ribbon)

-- A result whose longest edge is under this many studs is a sliver and is dropped.
local SLIVER = 0.35
-- Debris of the kerf: one bit per BIT_SIZE studs square of it, within LEAST_BITS and MOST_BITS.
local BIT_SIZE = 3
local LEAST_BITS = 3
local MOST_BITS = 24
-- A site keeps this far inside a box.
local INSET = 0.9

local Carve = {}

Carve.MOST_BITS = MOST_BITS

function Carve.key(part, bladeFrame, bladeSize, mode, count, seed, grid, grain)
	local shape = part.ClassName
	if part:IsA("MeshPart") then
		shape ..= part.MeshId
	elseif part:IsA("Part") then
		shape ..= part.Shape.Name
	elseif part:IsA("PartOperation") and not part.UsePartColor then
		-- Cut as it is: no white copy for one that uses its own colours.
		shape ..= ":baked"
	end
	local size = part.Size
	local place = bladeFrame.Position
	local look = bladeFrame.LookVector
	local up = bladeFrame.UpVector
	return string.format("carve|%s|%.3f,%.3f,%.3f|%.2f,%.2f,%.2f|%.3f,%.3f,%.3f|%.3f,%.3f,%.3f|%.2f,%.2f,%.2f|%s|%d|%d|%s|%.2f",
		shape, size.X, size.Y, size.Z, place.X, place.Y, place.Z, look.X, look.Y, look.Z, up.X, up.Y, up.Z,
		bladeSize.X, bladeSize.Y, bladeSize.Z, mode, count, seed, tostring(grid == true), grain or 0)
end

-- What the engine is given to cut for a job, and whether its results keep their own colours.
-- The third value is true for something made here, which the caller destroys.
local function sourceOf(job, frame)
	if job.template then
		return job.template, job.baked == true, false
	end
	if job.blockSize then
		local block = Instance.new("Part")
		block.Anchored = true
		block.Size = job.blockSize
		block.Color = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
		block.CFrame = frame
		return block, false, true
	end
	local part = job.part
	if part:IsA("PartOperation") and not part.UsePartColor then
		return part, true, false
	end
	local copy = Instance.fromExisting(part)
	copy.Anchored = true
	copy.Color = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
	-- A runtime copy is not Archivable, which the engine refuses to cut; this one stands where the cut was planned.
	copy.Archivable = true
	copy.CFrame = frame
	return copy, false, true
end

-- One of the engine's solid modelling calls on a part and its cutters, or nil and, when the
-- engine refused, its reason.
local function model(method, part, cutters, splitApart)
	local ok, results = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService[method](GeometryService, part, cutters, { SplitApart = splitApart })
	end)
	if ok and type(results) == "table" then
		return results
	end
	if not ok then
		return nil, tostring(results)
	end
	return nil
end

-- The results worth keeping; the slivers are destroyed.
local function withoutSlivers(results)
	local kept = {}
	for _, result in ipairs(results) do
		local size = result.ExtentsSize
		if math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z) < SLIVER then
			result:Destroy()
		else
			table.insert(kept, result)
		end
	end
	return kept
end

-- Random points in a template's own box, in the world.
local function sitesIn(template, count, random)
	local extents = template.ExtentsCFrame
	local size = template.ExtentsSize * INSET
	local points = table.create(count)
	for index = 1, count do
		points[index] = extents:PointToWorldSpace(Vector3.new((random() - 0.5) * size.X, (random() - 0.5) * size.Y, (random() - 0.5) * size.Z))
	end
	return points
end

-- The part's own pieces as points of the world: an even grid for blocks, anywhere for shards,
-- or the points a piece that is cut again was given.
local function ownSites(job, frame, random)
	local offsets
	if job.points then
		offsets = job.points
	elseif job.grid then
		offsets = Dice.centres(job.part.Size, job.count)
	else
		offsets = Sites.even(job.part.Size, job.count, random)
	end
	local points = table.create(#offsets)
	for index, offset in ipairs(offsets) do
		points[index] = frame:PointToWorldSpace(offset)
	end
	return points
end

-- Which side of the cut a template lies on.
local function sideOf(template, frame, slash)
	local middle = frame:PointToObjectSpace(template.ExtentsCFrame.Position)
	if (middle - slash.origin):Dot(slash.normal) >= 0 then
		return 1
	end
	return -1
end

-- The blade as the engine takes it: its box where the cut is, or a copy of a jagged blade's
-- ribbon. Yields while a Force's ribbon is made.
local function cuttersOf(job, frame)
	local ribbon = job.ribbon
	local template = ribbon and Ribbon.cutter(ribbon)
	if template then
		local cutter = template:Clone()
		cutter.CFrame = frame * job.ribbonFrame * template.CFrame
		return { cutter }
	end
	local cutter = Instance.new("Part")
	cutter.Anchored = true
	-- Without its ribbon a jagged blade cuts clean, with its own box and not the one that holds the ribbon.
	cutter.Size = ribbon and ribbon.flat or job.bladeSize
	cutter.CFrame = frame * job.bladeFrame
	return { cutter }
end

local function destroyAll(instances)
	for _, instance in ipairs(instances) do
		instance:Destroy()
	end
end

function Carve.cut(job, fragment, shardOf)
	local frame = job.frame or job.part.CFrame
	local slash = job.slash
	local random = Sites.sequence(job.seed)
	local cutters = cuttersOf(job, frame)

	local source, baked, copied = sourceOf(job, frame)
	local sides, refusal = model("SubtractAsync", source, cutters, true)
	if not sides and copied and not job.blockSize then
		-- The engine would not cut the copy: use the part itself, whose colours stay in the results.
		source:Destroy()
		source, baked, copied = job.part, true, false
		sides = model("SubtractAsync", source, cutters, true)
		if sides then
			refusal = nil
		end
	end
	if sides then
		sides = withoutSlivers(sides)
	end
	-- A lone side may be the part untouched: what the blade took out of it says.
	local taken = nil
	if sides and #sides == 1 and not job.always then
		taken = model("IntersectAsync", source, cutters, false)
		if not taken or #taken == 0 then
			sides[1]:Destroy()
			sides = nil
		end
	end
	if not sides or #sides == 0 then
		destroyAll(cutters)
		if copied then
			source:Destroy()
		end
		return false, refusal
	end

	local shards = {}
	-- A lone side is the part with a slot, whatever the mode; so is every side of a ground's patch.
	local slotted = #sides == 1 or job.stands == true
	for _, side in ipairs(sides) do
		local mark = sideOf(side, frame, slash)
		local broken = nil
		if job.mode == "Pieces" and job.count >= 2 and not slotted then
			-- Around points of the whole part: one whose cell does not touch this side gives it nothing.
			broken = fragment(side, ownSites(job, frame, random))
		end
		if broken and #broken >= 2 then
			for _, entry in ipairs(broken) do
				local shard = shardOf(entry.Instance, frame, false, nil)
				shard.side = mark
				shard.baked = baked
				table.insert(shards, shard)
			end
			side:Destroy()
		else
			local shard = shardOf(side, frame, slotted, nil)
			shard.side = mark
			shard.baked = baked
			table.insert(shards, shard)
		end
	end

	if taken and job.mode ~= "Band" then
		destroyAll(taken)
	end
	if job.mode == "Band" then
		local slabs = taken or model("IntersectAsync", source, cutters, false)
		local slab = slabs and slabs[1]
		if slab then
			local size = slab.ExtentsSize
			local longest = math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z)
			local middling = size.X + size.Y + size.Z - longest - math.min(size.X, size.Y, size.Z)
			local count = math.clamp(math.round(longest * middling / (BIT_SIZE * BIT_SIZE)), LEAST_BITS, MOST_BITS)
			local bits = fragment(slab, sitesIn(slab, count, random))
			for _, entry in ipairs(bits or {}) do
				local shard = shardOf(entry.Instance, frame, false, nil)
				shard.bit = true
				shard.baked = baked
				table.insert(shards, shard)
			end
			slab:Destroy()
		end
	end
	destroyAll(cutters)
	if copied then
		source:Destroy()
	end
	shards.slash = slash
	return shards
end

return Carve

--[[
	Crack  -  cracked ground: what a part cut with the "Cracks" pattern does when struck. Part of
	Reactor/Play (its functions read and write a play's tables). Maths only.
	A crust of pieces in rings around the hit over a fixed base. A crust piece carries piece.strike =
	{ origin, normal, reach, crust } (world; one table per crack), with .path for a Linear Force's
	split (measured from the path, narrowing to its ends) and .by, the Force it was made for.
	By distance from the hit over the reach: in the crater (under CRATER) a piece is thrown if the Force
	beats its Hold, else sunk and tipped toward the hit; on the rim (under RIM) heaved a little; beyond,
	moved by a hair so the crack shows. Each rolls its own sink, tip and twist. A joined piece wider
	than the crater counts as beyond the rim.
	  Crack.share(piece), Crack.shareAt(strike, position), Crack.outsizes(piece, strike)
	  Crack.reached(piece, record, pulls) -> direction, distance, distance01, or nil
	  Crack.holds(piece), Crack.buried(piece, position) -> studs under its struck face (floors only)
	  Crack.power(strike, strength) -> 0..1 (a crater sinks STRENGTH_DEPTH of the Strength at most)
	  Crack.pose(piece, random, from, power) -> CFrame (within its crust, tilted at most MOST_TILT)
	  Crack.strike(play, index, strength), Crack.settle(play, count) -> count,
	  Crack.returning(play, progress, count) -> count
	A cracked piece stays RESTING: play.cracked, play.crackPower, play.crackFrame (a later throw
	starts from that pose, Play:_surfaced).
]]

local Fissure = require(script.Parent.Fissure)
local Fields = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Fields)

local RESTING = 0

local CRATER = Fissure.CRATER
local RIM = Fissure.RIM
-- How far the piece at the hit sinks, as a share of the crust: its top stays over the base.
local DEPTH_SHARE = 0.7
-- The studs a crater sinks for each stud of the Force's Strength, up to that depth.
local STRENGTH_DEPTH = 0.2
-- The least of that depth a crater piece sinks, at the crater's edge.
local EDGE_SINK = 0.19
-- Degrees a crater piece is tipped toward the hit, at the crater's edge and at the hit.
local EDGE_TIP = 8
local HIT_TIP = 24
local CRATER_TWIST = 26
-- The rim: how far out of the part it is heaved (share of the depth), and its tip and twist.
local RIM_LIFT = 0.17
local RIM_TIP = 9
local RIM_TWIST = 9
-- Beyond the rim: a hair.
local HAIR_LIFT = 0.027
local HAIR_TIP = 1.2
-- However many cracks it took, a piece is at most this share of its crust under or over its rest.
local MOST_SINK = 0.95
local MOST_LIFT = 0.6
-- And its struck face leans at most this many degrees (one crack alone stays under it).
local MOST_TILT = 40
-- A struck face whose normal points up at least this much is a floor.
local FLOOR_LIKE = 0.7
local TINY = 1e-4

local Crack = {}

-- Degrees between two unit vectors.
local function between(first, second)
	return math.deg(math.acos(math.clamp(first:Dot(second), -1, 1)))
end

-- A place seen from the hit: its distance over the reach and the unit direction out along the
-- face; for a split, seen from its path, with the share of the way along it third.
local function fromStrike(strike, position)
	if strike.path then
		local away, along, outward = Fissure.from(strike.path, position)
		return away / (strike.reach * Fissure.leaf(along)), outward, along
	end
	local normal = strike.normal
	local offset = position - strike.origin
	local flat = offset - normal * offset:Dot(normal)
	local distance = flat.Magnitude
	if distance > TINY then
		return distance / strike.reach, flat / distance
	end
	-- Right at the hit there is no way out: any direction along the face serves.
	local along = normal:Cross(Vector3.new(1, 0, 0))
	if along.Magnitude < TINY then
		along = normal:Cross(Vector3.new(0, 0, 1))
	end
	return 0, along.Unit
end

-- Whether a piece reaches farther toward `outward` than the crater is wide there (`along`: the
-- share along a split, nil for a round crack).
local function widerThanCrater(piece, strike, outward, along)
	local own = piece.rest:VectorToObjectSpace(outward)
	local half = piece.halfExt
	local reaches = math.abs(own.X) * half.X + math.abs(own.Y) * half.Y + math.abs(own.Z) * half.Z
	local crater = strike.reach * CRATER
	if along then
		crater *= Fissure.leaf(along)
	end
	return reaches > crater
end

local function fromHit(piece)
	local strike = piece.strike
	local share, outward, along = fromStrike(strike, piece.rest.Position)
	if piece.joined and share < RIM and widerThanCrater(piece, strike, outward, along) then
		share = RIM
	end
	return share, outward, along
end

function Crack.share(piece)
	local share = fromHit(piece)
	return share
end

function Crack.shareAt(strike, position)
	local share = fromStrike(strike, position)
	return share
end

function Crack.outsizes(piece, strike)
	local _, outward, along = fromStrike(strike, piece.rest.Position)
	return widerThanCrater(piece, strike, outward, along)
end

function Crack.holds(piece)
	return piece.strike ~= nil and Crack.share(piece) >= CRATER
end

function Crack.buried(piece, position)
	local strike = piece.strike
	if not strike or strike.normal.Y < FLOOR_LIKE then
		return 0
	end
	local under = (strike.origin - (position or piece.rest.Position)):Dot(strike.normal)
	return math.max(under, 0) / strike.normal.Y
end

function Crack.reached(piece, record, pulls)
	local strike = piece.strike
	if not strike or not strike.path or strike.by ~= record then
		return nil
	end
	local share, _, along = fromHit(piece)
	if share > 1 then
		return nil
	end
	local field = record.field
	local distance = field.inner + along * (field.range - field.inner)
	return Fields.heading(field, pulls), distance, distance / field.range
end

function Crack.power(strike, strength)
	return math.clamp(math.abs(strength) * STRENGTH_DEPTH / (strike.crust * DEPTH_SHARE), 0, 1)
end

function Crack.pose(piece, random, from, power)
	local strike = piece.strike
	local normal = strike.normal
	local share, outward = fromHit(piece)
	local depth = strike.crust * DEPTH_SHARE
	local felt = 1
	if power ~= nil then
		felt = power
	end
	local lift, tip, twist
	if share < CRATER then
		local near = 1 - share / CRATER
		lift = -depth * (EDGE_SINK + (1 - EDGE_SINK) * near ^ 1.3) * (0.7 + 0.6 * random()) * felt
		tip = (EDGE_TIP + (HIT_TIP - EDGE_TIP) * near) * (0.5 + random()) * felt
		twist = (random() - 0.5) * CRATER_TWIST * felt
	elseif share < RIM then
		local rim = 1 - (share - CRATER) / (RIM - CRATER)
		lift = depth * RIM_LIFT * rim * (0.5 + random()) * felt
		tip = -RIM_TIP * rim * (0.4 + random()) * felt
		twist = (random() - 0.5) * RIM_TWIST * rim * felt
	else
		lift = depth * HAIR_LIFT * (random() - 0.5)
		tip = (random() - 0.5) * HAIR_TIP
		twist = 0
	end
	-- About this axis a positive turn raises the piece's outer edge and lowers its inner one.
	local axis = outward:Cross(normal)
	local turn = CFrame.fromAxisAngle(axis, math.rad(tip)) * CFrame.fromAxisAngle(outward, math.rad(twist))
	local rest = from or piece.rest
	local moved = (rest.Position - piece.rest.Position):Dot(normal)
	local facing = rest.Rotation
	if share < CRATER then
		-- A piece cut out of a tipped one is handed its place in it, which may lie over the face.
		facing = piece.rest.Rotation
		lift += math.min(moved, 0) - moved
	end
	lift = math.clamp(lift, -strike.crust * MOST_SINK - moved, strike.crust * MOST_LIFT - moved)
	-- Of a turn that would lean the piece too far, only the share that stays within is given.
	local turned = turn * facing
	local faceOut = piece.rest:VectorToObjectSpace(normal)
	local leans = between(facing:VectorToWorldSpace(faceOut), normal)
	local wouldLean = between(turned:VectorToWorldSpace(faceOut), normal)
	if wouldLean > MOST_TILT and wouldLean > leans then
		local share = math.clamp((MOST_TILT - leans) / (wouldLean - leans), 0, 1)
		turned = facing:Lerp(turned, share)
	end
	return CFrame.new(rest.Position + normal * lift) * turned
end

function Crack.strike(play, index, strength)
	if play.cracked[index] or play.state[index] ~= RESTING or play.pendingPush[index] then
		return
	end
	-- Along its patch's side and beyond the rim a piece stays at rest (Reactor/Pieces.ofSet).
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	if piece.atEdge and Crack.share(piece) >= RIM then
		return
	end
	play.cracked[index] = true
	play.crackPower[index] = Crack.power(piece.strike, strength)
	table.insert(play.pendingCrack, index)
end

function Crack.settle(play, count)
	local pending = play.pendingCrack
	if #pending == 0 then
		return count
	end
	local budget = play.settings.wakeBudget
	local taken = 0
	local made = 0
	while taken < #pending and made < budget do
		taken += 1
		local index = pending[taken]
		-- One thrown since it was queued flies from where it stood.
		if play.state[index] == RESTING and not play.pendingPush[index] then
			made += play.display.wake(index) or 1
			play.hidden += 1
			local frame = Crack.pose(play.pieces[index], play.settings.random, play.crackFrame[index], play.crackPower[index])
			play.crackFrame[index] = frame
			count += 1
			play.moveIndices[count] = index
			play.moveFrames[count] = frame
		end
	end
	local remaining = {}
	for position = taken + 1, #pending do
		table.insert(remaining, pending[position])
	end
	play.pendingCrack = remaining
	return count
end

function Crack.returning(play, progress, count)
	for index, frame in pairs(play.crackFrame) do
		if play.state[index] == RESTING then
			count += 1
			play.moveIndices[count] = index
			play.moveFrames[count] = frame:Lerp(play.pieces[index].rest, progress)
		end
	end
	return count
end

return Crack

--[[
	CutPlan: what the engine is asked to cut of a Reactor at rest, and what is kept of it already.
	Part of the Reactor mixin's entry-making (Reactor/Entries).

	The engine cuts a Reactor's parts with Break = "Shards" or "Blocks" (a plain box with Blocks is
	left to Reactor/Dice). A part touched by the blade of a Force that has a Cut (Reactor/Blade,
	Reactor/Carve) is carved instead; every other part keeps the cut of its Break.

	CutPlan.byEngine(data) -> whether the Reactor's Break is cut by the engine at all
	CutPlan.waitsForHit(data) -> whether its Shard Pattern is cut around a Force, so only once one arrives
	CutPlan.strike(data, record) -> strike or nil (nil when the arriving Force means nothing for the cut)
	  strike = { hit, reach, field, blade, mode }
	    hit           where the Force is, for patterns cut around it
	    reach, field  with Shard Pattern "Cracks": the Force's Range and field (a Linear one splits
	                  the ground along its line, Reactor/Fissure)
	    blade, mode   for a Force with a Cut: its blade and what becomes of the part. Such a Force
	                  cracks no ground; a part its blade misses is cut around the hit
	CutPlan.grounds(reactor) -> grounds, isGround
	  The Reactor's grounds (Reactor/Layers) and the set of their parts: plain blocks, and each mesh
	  part or union lying on one as its skin.
	CutPlan.of(reactor, data, grounds, strike) -> sets, jobs
	  sets: part -> its kept shards (a part without moves whole). jobs: parts still to be cut
	  (Reactor/Shards.prepare). A part the rings of cracked ground do not reach moves whole.
	  grounds = true: the plain boxes are grounds, left to Reactor/Wounds. A part whose mesh the engine
	  refuses gets no job and moves whole; the Output says why, once per mesh a session (Shards.explain).
]]

local Shards = require(script.Parent.Shards)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Fissure = require(script.Parent.Fissure)
local Pieces = require(script.Parent.Pieces)
local Blade = require(script.Parent.Blade)
local Carve = require(script.Parent.Carve)
local Layers = require(script.Parent.Layers)

local CutPlan = {}

function CutPlan.byEngine(data)
	return data.Break == "Shards" or data.Break == "Blocks"
end

function CutPlan.waitsForHit(data)
	return data.Break == "Shards" and (data.ShardPattern == "Around hit" or data.ShardPattern == "Cracks")
end

function CutPlan.strike(data, record)
	if not record then
		return nil
	end
	local strike = {}
	if CutPlan.waitsForHit(data) then
		strike.hit = record.field.origin.Position
	end
	if record.cut then
		strike.blade = Blade.of(record.field, record.cut)
		strike.mode = record.cut.mode
	elseif strike.hit and data.ShardPattern == "Cracks" then
		strike.reach = record.field.range
		strike.field = record.field
	end
	if not strike.hit and not strike.blade then
		return nil
	end
	return strike
end

-- The split a Linear Force makes of a part cut whole: its line in the part's space with the face it
-- lies on, or nil for any other Force (Reactor/Fissure.of). Drawn from the Force's place alone, as
-- Reactor/Footprint and Reactor/Recut draw it.
local function splitOf(part, hit, hitInPart, field)
	local axis, side = Sites.face(part.Size, hitInPart)
	local normal = Sites.alongFace(axis, 0, 0, side)
	local seed = Sites.seedAt(hit)
	local line = Fissure.of(field, part.CFrame, normal * (part.Size[axis] / 2), normal, Sites.sequence(seed))
	if line then
		line.seed = seed
		line.face = { axis = axis, side = side }
	end
	return line
end

-- The cut of one part by a Force's blade; nil for a part the blade misses, one the engine cannot cut, or a ground.
local function carveJob(part, data, seed, strike, grounds)
	local blade = strike.blade
	if not Shards.cuttable(part) or (grounds and grounds[part]) then
		if Shards.refused(part) and Blade.touches(blade, part.ExtentsCFrame, part.ExtentsSize) then
			Shards.explain(part)
		end
		return nil
	end
	local frame = part.CFrame
	-- Where the part's shape is, which need not be around its CFrame (Reactor/Pieces).
	if not Blade.touches(blade, part.ExtentsCFrame, part.ExtentsSize) then
		return nil
	end
	-- Pieces splits the sides into the part's own pieces; a part with no Break has none.
	local count = 0
	if strike.mode == "Pieces" and CutPlan.byEngine(data) then
		count = Sites.count(part.Size, data.Pieces)
	end
	local grid = data.Break == "Blocks"
	local bladeFrame = Blade.inPart(blade, frame)
	local ribbon, ribbonFrame = Blade.ribbonFor(blade, frame, part.Size, frame:Inverse())
	return {
		part = part,
		key = Carve.key(part, bladeFrame, blade.size, strike.mode, count, seed, grid, blade.grain),
		bladeFrame = bladeFrame,
		bladeSize = blade.size,
		ribbon = ribbon,
		ribbonFrame = ribbonFrame,
		slash = {
			origin = frame:PointToObjectSpace(blade.origin),
			normal = frame:VectorToObjectSpace(blade.normal),
			heading = frame:VectorToObjectSpace(blade.heading),
			kerf = blade.kerf,
		},
		mode = strike.mode,
		count = count,
		seed = seed,
		grid = grid,
	}
end

-- The cut of one part by its Reactor's Break, or nil for a part that moves whole.
local function breakJob(part, data, seed, strike, grounds)
	local blocks = data.Break == "Blocks"
	local count = Sites.count(part.Size, data.Pieces)
	-- A plain box is cut by arithmetic with Blocks; a ground is not cut whole.
	if (blocks and Pieces.isPlainBlock(part)) or (grounds and grounds[part]) then
		count = 0
	end
	local hit = strike and strike.hit
	local reach = strike and strike.reach
	local hitInPart = nil
	if hit then
		hitInPart = part.CFrame:PointToObjectSpace(hit)
		local nearest = Sites.hitIn(part.Size, hitInPart)
		if not reach then
			hitInPart = nearest
		elseif (hitInPart - nearest).Magnitude > reach * Sites.RUN_ON then
			count = 0
		end
	end
	if count < 2 or not Shards.cuttable(part) then
		if count >= 2 then
			Shards.explain(part)
		end
		return nil
	end
	local line = nil
	if reach and strike.field then
		line = splitOf(part, hit, hitInPart, strike.field)
	end
	return {
		part = part,
		key = Shards.key(part, count, seed, hitInPart, reach, blocks, line),
		count = count,
		seed = seed,
		hit = hitInPart,
		reach = reach,
		grid = blocks,
		line = line,
		face = line and line.face,
	}
end

-- A Reactor's grounds and the set of their parts: plain blocks, and mesh parts and unions lying on one as its skin.
function CutPlan.grounds(reactor)
	local blocks = {}
	local others = {}
	local isGround = {}
	for _, part in ipairs(Pieces.parts(reactor)) do
		if Pieces.isPlainBlock(part) then
			isGround[part] = true
			table.insert(blocks, part)
		elseif (part:IsA("MeshPart") or part:IsA("PartOperation")) and Shards.cuttable(part) then
			table.insert(others, part)
		end
	end
	local grounds, skins = Layers.grounds(blocks, others)
	for part in pairs(skins) do
		isGround[part] = true
	end
	return grounds, isGround
end

function CutPlan.of(reactor, data, grounds, strike)
	local sets = {}
	local jobs = {}
	-- The parts Reactor/Wounds cracks where struck are never cut whole.
	if grounds then
		local _
		_, grounds = CutPlan.grounds(reactor)
	end
	local engine = CutPlan.byEngine(data)
	for order, part in ipairs(Pieces.parts(reactor)) do
		local seed = order * 7919 + 13
		local job = nil
		if strike and strike.blade then
			job = carveJob(part, data, seed, strike, grounds)
		end
		if not job and engine then
			job = breakJob(part, data, seed, strike, grounds)
		end
		if job then
			local shards = Shards.get(part, job.key)
			if shards == nil then
				table.insert(jobs, job)
			elseif shards then
				sets[part] = shards
			end
		end
	end
	return sets, jobs
end

return CutPlan

--[[
	Dice  -  a box as a grid of blocks: what a part of a Reactor breaks into with Break =
	"Blocks". Numbers only, no instances.

	Dice.grid(size, pieces) -> countX, countY, countZ
	    how many blocks along each axis: the grid whose blocks are nearest to cubes and whose
	    number is nearest to `pieces`. A count can rarely be met exactly (50 in a cube is
	    3 x 4 x 4 = 48). An axis too short for a cube of its own is not cut, and the others are
	    cut the finer for it. Never more than Dice.MAX_BLOCKS.
	Dice.cut(size, pieces, random) -> { { offset = Vector3, size = Vector3 }, ... }
	    that grid as blocks that fill the box exactly, for a part that is a plain box. Each
	    axis is cut by planes that run through the whole box, spaced evenly and then shifted a
	    little, so the blocks are an uneven grid: every block touches its neighbours face to
	    face and nothing overlaps or is left out. offset is a block's centre in the box's own
	    space. random gives 0 to 1; the same sequence gives the same blocks.
	Dice.centres(size, pieces) -> { Vector3 }
	    the middles of that grid's cells, evenly spaced: the points the engine cuts a part that
	    is NOT a plain box around (Reactor/Shards). Each fragment is the part of the shape nearest
	    its point, which for an even grid is a cube.
]]

local Dice = {}

-- A part is never cut into more blocks than this.
Dice.MAX_BLOCKS = 240
-- How far a cut may be shifted from its even place, as a share of a block's length.
local SHIFT = 0.22
-- An axis shorter than this share of a cube's edge is not cut.
local UNCUT_UNDER = 0.75
-- grid: how much a block's being off a cube weighs against the count's being off `pieces`.
local SHAPE_WEIGHT = 0.25

local AXES = { "X", "Y", "Z" }

-- The cut planes along one axis of `length`, from -length / 2 to length / 2, both ends included.
local function planes(length, count, random)
	local edges = table.create(count + 1)
	local step = length / count
	edges[1] = -length / 2
	for cut = 1, count - 1 do
		edges[cut + 1] = -length / 2 + step * (cut + (random() * 2 - 1) * SHIFT)
	end
	edges[count + 1] = length / 2
	return edges
end

-- The edge of a cube when `pieces` of them fill the box, and which axes are cut at all: an axis
-- too short for such a cube is left whole and the cube worked out again over the others.
local function cubeEdge(size, pieces)
	local cut = { X = true, Y = true, Z = true }
	local edge = 0
	for _ = 1, #AXES do
		local measure = 1
		local axes = 0
		for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
			if cut[axis] then
				measure *= size[axis]
				axes += 1
			end
		end
		if axes == 0 then
			break
		end
		edge = (measure / pieces) ^ (1 / axes)
		local dropped = false
		for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
			if cut[axis] and size[axis] < edge * UNCUT_UNDER then
				cut[axis] = false
				dropped = true
			end
		end
		if not dropped then
			break
		end
	end
	return edge, cut
end

-- The counts worth trying along one axis: the nearest to a cube, one fewer and one more.
local function choices(length, edge, isCut)
	if not isCut then
		return { 1 }
	end
	local nearest = math.max(math.round(length / edge), 1)
	local list = {}
	for count = math.max(nearest - 1, 1), nearest + 1 do
		table.insert(list, count)
	end
	return list
end

function Dice.grid(size, pieces)
	pieces = math.clamp(math.floor(pieces), 1, Dice.MAX_BLOCKS)
	local edge, cut = cubeEdge(size, pieces)
	local bestX, bestY, bestZ = 1, 1, 1
	local bestScore = math.huge
	for _, countX in ipairs(choices(size.X, edge, cut.X)) do
		for _, countY in ipairs(choices(size.Y, edge, cut.Y)) do
			for _, countZ in ipairs(choices(size.Z, edge, cut.Z)) do
				local total = countX * countY * countZ
				if total <= Dice.MAX_BLOCKS then
					-- How far the longest edge of a block is from its shortest, over the cut axes.
					local longest, shortest = 0, math.huge
					local counts = { X = countX, Y = countY, Z = countZ }
					for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
						if cut[axis] then
							local length = size[axis] / counts[axis]
							longest = math.max(longest, length)
							shortest = math.min(shortest, length)
						end
					end
					local offCube = 0
					if longest > 0 then
						offCube = longest / shortest - 1
					end
					local score = math.abs(total - pieces) / pieces + SHAPE_WEIGHT * offCube
					if score < bestScore then
						bestX, bestY, bestZ = countX, countY, countZ
						bestScore = score
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return bestX, bestY, bestZ
end

function Dice.cut(size, pieces, random)
	local countX, countY, countZ = Dice.grid(size, pieces)
	local edgesX = planes(size.X, countX, random)
	local edgesY = planes(size.Y, countY, random)
	local edgesZ = planes(size.Z, countZ, random)
	local blocks = table.create(countX * countY * countZ)
	for x = 1, countX do
		for y = 1, countY do
			for z = 1, countZ do
				table.insert(blocks, {
					offset = Vector3.new((edgesX[x] + edgesX[x + 1]) / 2, (edgesY[y] + edgesY[y + 1]) / 2, (edgesZ[z] + edgesZ[z + 1]) / 2),
					size = Vector3.new(edgesX[x + 1] - edgesX[x], edgesY[y + 1] - edgesY[y], edgesZ[z + 1] - edgesZ[z]),
				})
			end
		end
	end
	return blocks
end

function Dice.centres(size, pieces)
	local countX, countY, countZ = Dice.grid(size, pieces)
	local centres = table.create(countX * countY * countZ)
	for x = 1, countX do
		for y = 1, countY do
			for z = 1, countZ do
				table.insert(centres, Vector3.new(
					((x - 0.5) / countX - 0.5) * size.X,
					((y - 0.5) / countY - 0.5) * size.Y,
					((z - 0.5) / countZ - 0.5) * size.Z
				))
			end
		end
	end
	return centres
end

return Dice
