--[[
	Display  -  what a Reactor's play looks like: a stand-in for every piece out of place, its
	original hidden meanwhile. Reactor/Play calls wake, move, drop and restore.
	A block (Break = "Blocks") gets a stand-in its size, and the first block of a part to wake brings
	its siblings (the part hides whole). A shard gets a copy of its template in the part's look now,
	placed at frame * standOffset; a layered piece (Reactor/Layers) has one per fragment, moved
	together. The base under cracked ground is drawn darker.
	Only stand-ins move: unsaved copies marked _PartIcleEmit. An original is LIVE content, written one
	way only: hidden by LocalTransparencyModifier (never saved or replicated); on a server, where that
	does not exist, its Transparency, CanCollide, CanQuery and its Decals' Transparency are set and
	put back from values kept here. A piece marked own (Reactor/Owned) is a runtime copy and is its
	own stand-in.
	  Display.hide(part, onServer, staysSolid) -> kept; Display.show(part, onServer, kept)
	  Display.serverOnly(), Display.ownTransparency(instance), Display.unhidden(copy, original)
	  Display.new(pieces, folder, onServer, keepOriginals) -> display; display.clear()
]]

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local EngineAttr = require(script.Parent.Parent.EngineAttr)
local Index = require(script.Parent.Index)

local CONFIG_NAME = "PartIcleProperties"
-- How bright the base under cracked ground is, against the part's own colour.
local BASE_SHADE = 0.6
-- A fragment whose top lies this near its piece's top is at the piece's surface.
local FACE_SLACK = 0.05

local Display = {}

-- What a server's hide wrote over, by instance; kept here, not per display, since a ground is
-- hidden by Reactor/GroundDisplay while its wounds' displays make its pieces.
local serverKept = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

-- A server and nothing else (Studio's edit mode counts as a client, as in VisualHost).
function Display.serverOnly()
	return RunService:IsServer() and not RunService:IsClient()
end

function Display.ownTransparency(instance)
	local kept = serverKept[instance]
	if kept then
		return kept.Transparency
	end
	return instance.Transparency
end

function Display.unhidden(copy, original)
	EngineAttr.writeProp(copy, "LocalTransparencyModifier", 0)
	copy.Transparency = Display.ownTransparency(original)
end

-- Whether a stand-in takes a child of its original along: what draws on the part does; parts,
-- joints, values, code and the plugin's own children do not.
function Display.travels(child)
	if child:IsA("BasePart") or child:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("BasePart", true) then
		return false
	end
	if child:IsA("JointInstance") or child:IsA("Constraint") or child:IsA("WeldConstraint") or child:IsA("NoCollisionConstraint") then
		return false
	end
	if child:IsA("LuaSourceContainer") or child:IsA("ValueBase") then
		return false
	end
	if child.Name == CONFIG_NAME or child:GetAttribute("Transformed") then
		return false
	end
	return true
end

-- A part that stands on while hidden: cracked ground, or a part a blade left a slot in.
function Display.cracked(piece)
	return piece.strike ~= nil or piece.fixed == true or piece.partStands == true
end

-- A ground patch's piece carries the ground's Textures, so a patch at rest matches the ground:
-- on a Part a Texture runs from the +X and +Z edges, on a MeshPart (what FragmentAsync cuts) from
-- the middle of its box. Top face only. fragment: one of a layered piece's.
local function carryTextures(copy, piece, fragment)
	local cut = piece.cut
	-- Only a piece that reaches the struck face shows any of it; the base under cracked ground does not.
	local hiddenBase = piece.fixed and not piece.slash
	if not cut or hiddenBase or not piece.atFace or cut.face.axis ~= "Y" or cut.face.side ~= 1 then
		return
	end
	local part = piece.part
	local middle = piece.rest.Position
	local halfExt = piece.halfExt
	local plain = piece.plain
	if fragment then
		part = fragment.part
		middle = (piece.rest * fragment.offset).Position
		halfExt = fragment.halfExt
		plain = fragment.plain
		-- Of a piece's fragments only the one that comes up to the struck face is its surface.
		if fragment.offset.Position.Y + halfExt.Y < piece.halfExt.Y - FACE_SLACK then
			return
		end
	end
	-- A layer turned otherwise than its ground has its own Top elsewhere.
	if plain then
		return
	end
	local centre = part.CFrame:PointToObjectSpace(middle)
	local start = halfExt
	if copy:IsA("MeshPart") then
		start = Vector3.zero
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("Texture") and child.Face == Enum.NormalId.Top then
			local texture = child:Clone()
			texture.OffsetStudsU = child.OffsetStudsU + part.Size.X / 2 - (centre.X + start.X)
			texture.OffsetStudsV = child.OffsetStudsV + part.Size.Z / 2 - (centre.Z + start.Z)
			-- The ground's own Texture is hidden while a wound is open: the copy is not.
			Display.unhidden(texture, child)
			texture.Parent = copy
		end
	end
end

-- A shard's stand-in: a copy of its template, looking as the part does now. fragment: one of
-- a stacked ground's piece, whose template and part are its own.
local function makeShard(piece, fragment)
	local part = piece.part
	local template = piece.shard
	if fragment then
		part = fragment.part
		template = fragment.shard
	end
	local copy = template:Clone()
	-- A baked shard keeps the Color it came with (its colours are in its geometry); a blade's union
	-- shows the part's colour only when told to.
	local own = copy.Color
	if not piece.baked then
		if copy:IsA("PartOperation") then
			copy.UsePartColor = true
		end
		own = part.Color
	end
	if piece.fixed and not piece.slash then
		own = Color3.new(own.R * BASE_SHADE, own.G * BASE_SHADE, own.B * BASE_SHADE)
	end
	copy.Color = own
	-- A mesh part's SurfaceAppearance is its look, and cutting leaves it off; under any other part it
	-- draws nothing.
	local appearance = part:IsA("MeshPart") and copy:IsA("MeshPart") and part:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("SurfaceAppearance")
	-- A skin's fragment (Reactor/Layers) is cut out of a box, so it has none of the mesh's mapping.
	local skinned = piece.skin
	if fragment then
		skinned = fragment.skin
	end
	if appearance and not skinned then
		appearance:Clone().Parent = copy
	end
	copy.Material = part.Material
	copy.MaterialVariant = part.MaterialVariant
	copy.Transparency = Display.ownTransparency(part)
	copy.Reflectance = part.Reflectance
	copy.Archivable = false
	copy.Anchored = true
	copy.CanCollide = false
	copy.CanQuery = false
	copy.CanTouch = false
	copy.Locked = true
	copy:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	carryTextures(copy, piece, fragment)
	return copy
end

local function makeStandIn(piece)
	if piece.shard then
		return makeShard(piece)
	end
	local part = piece.part
	local copy = Instance.fromExisting(part)
	-- A copy of a part a server has hidden has taken the hide with it.
	copy.Transparency = Display.ownTransparency(part)
	copy.Archivable = false
	copy.Anchored = true
	copy.CanCollide = false
	copy.CanQuery = false
	copy.CanTouch = false
	copy.Locked = true
	-- A Reactor that is one part would hand its own marks to its stand-in.
	Index.unmark(copy)
	copy:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	if piece.blockSize then
		-- A block carries nothing over from the whole part's faces.
		copy.Size = piece.blockSize
		return copy
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if Display.travels(child) then
			local childCopy = child:Clone()
			if childCopy then
				if childCopy:IsA("Decal") then
					Display.unhidden(childCopy, child)
				end
				childCopy.Parent = copy
			end
		end
	end
	return copy
end

-- Hides or shows a LIVE original and the Decals and Textures directly on it.
local function setLocalHidden(part, hidden)
	local modifier = 0
	if hidden then
		modifier = 1
	end
	EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "LocalTransparencyModifier", modifier)
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("Decal") then
			EngineAttr.writeProp(child, "LocalTransparencyModifier", modifier)
		end
	end
end

-- Hides a LIVE original; returns what Display.show needs. staysSolid: cracked ground, which goes
-- on carrying what lands on it. A server reads the part's own values once.
function Display.hide(part, onServer, staysSolid)
	if not onServer then
		setLocalHidden(part, true)
		return true
	end
	local kept = serverKept[part]
	if not kept then
		kept = { Transparency = part.Transparency, CanCollide = part.CanCollide, CanQuery = part.CanQuery, decals = {} }
		serverKept[part] = kept
		EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "Transparency", 1)
		for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
			if child:IsA("Decal") then
				table.insert(kept.decals, child)
				serverKept[child] = { Transparency = child.Transparency }
				EngineAttr.writeProp(child, "Transparency", 1)
			end
		end
	end
	if staysSolid then
		return kept
	end
	EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "CanCollide", false)
	EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "CanQuery", false)
	return kept
end

-- Shows a LIVE original Display.hide hid, also one that has left the world.
function Display.show(part, onServer, kept)
	if not onServer then
		if part.Parent then
			setLocalHidden(part, false)
		end
		return
	end
	serverKept[part] = nil
	for _, decal in ipairs(kept.decals) do
		local own = serverKept[decal]
		serverKept[decal] = nil
		if own then
			EngineAttr.writeProp(decal, "Transparency", own.Transparency)
		end
	end
	EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "Transparency", kept.Transparency)
	EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "CanCollide", kept.CanCollide)
	EngineAttr.writeProp(part, "CanQuery", kept.CanQuery)
end

-- Switches off what draws on and under a runtime COPY. Never on a user's part.
function Display.quiet(copy)
	for _, descendant in ipairs(copy:GetDescendants()) do
		if descendant:IsA("ParticleEmitter") or descendant:IsA("Trail") or descendant:IsA("Beam")
			or descendant:IsA("Light") or descendant:IsA("Highlight") then
			descendant.Enabled = false
		end
	end
end

-- Shows a LIVE part found hidden with no play to answer for it (ShowStrandedReactors). Undoes the
-- local hide only.
function Display.unhide(part)
	setLocalHidden(part, false)
end

-- onServer: no local hide here, the part's own properties are used. keepOriginals: someone else
-- hides and shows the originals.
function Display.new(pieces, folder, onServer, keepOriginals)
	local standIns = {}
	-- index -> the stand-ins of a layered piece's other fragments; nil until one is placed.
	local extras = nil
	local extraFrames = {}
	-- index -> true once its stand-in was removed: a sibling's wake does not bring it back.
	local dropped = {}
	-- part -> true while it is hidden, or (on a server) the values to put back.
	local hidden = {}
	local moveParts = {}
	local moveCount = 0
	local display = {}
	-- Made when the first shard is placed: only then are frames rewritten.
	local offsetFrames = nil

	-- Hides a LIVE original once, however many of its blocks ask.
	local function hideOriginal(part, staysSolid)
		if keepOriginals or hidden[part] then
			return
		end
		hidden[part] = Display.hide(part, onServer, staysSolid)
	end

	local function showOriginal(part)
		local kept = hidden[part]
		if not kept then
			return
		end
		hidden[part] = nil
		Display.show(part, onServer, kept)
	end

	local function place(index)
		local piece = pieces[index]
		if piece.own then
			-- Moved by its box as any other piece: one whose shape lies off its CFrame has an offset.
			if piece.standOffset then
				offsetFrames = offsetFrames or {}
			end
			standIns[index] = piece.part
			dropped[index] = nil
			return 1
		end
		local layered = piece.layered
		if layered then
			extras = extras or {}
			local more = table.create(#layered - 1)
			for position, fragment in ipairs(layered) do
				local copy = makeShard(piece, fragment)
				copy.CFrame = piece.rest * fragment.standOffset
				copy.Parent = folder
				if position == 1 then
					standIns[index] = copy
				else
					more[position - 1] = copy
				end
			end
			extras[index] = more
			dropped[index] = nil
			return #layered
		end
		local copy = makeStandIn(piece)
		if piece.standOffset then
			offsetFrames = offsetFrames or {}
			copy.CFrame = piece.rest * piece.standOffset
		else
			copy.CFrame = piece.rest
		end
		copy.Parent = folder
		standIns[index] = copy
		dropped[index] = nil
		return 1
	end

	-- Removes the stand-ins of a layered piece's other fragments.
	local function dropExtras(index)
		local more = extras and extras[index]
		if more then
			for _, copy in ipairs(more) do
				copy:Destroy()
			end
			extras[index] = nil
		end
	end

	-- Returns how many stand-ins it made (the wake budget counts them).
	function display.wake(index)
		local piece = pieces[index]
		local made = 0
		if piece.siblings then
			for _, sibling in ipairs(piece.siblings) do
				if not standIns[sibling] and (sibling == index or not dropped[sibling]) then
					made += place(sibling)
				end
			end
		elseif not standIns[index] then
			made = place(index)
		end
		if not piece.own then
			hideOriginal(piece.part, Display.cracked(piece))
		end
		return made
	end

	-- Every index must have its stand-in: BulkMoveTo stops at a missing one.
	function display.move(indices, frames, count)
		if extras then
			-- A layered piece moves all its stand-ins: the list is longer than the pieces'.
			local total = 0
			for position = 1, count do
				local index = indices[position]
				local piece = pieces[index]
				local frame = frames[position]
				total += 1
				moveParts[total] = standIns[index]
				if piece.standOffset then
					extraFrames[total] = frame * piece.standOffset
				else
					extraFrames[total] = frame
				end
				local more = extras[index]
				if more then
					local layered = piece.layered
					for place = 1, #more do
						total += 1
						moveParts[total] = more[place]
						extraFrames[total] = frame * layered[place + 1].standOffset
					end
				end
			end
			for position = total + 1, moveCount do
				moveParts[position] = nil
				extraFrames[position] = nil
			end
			moveCount = total
			workspace:BulkMoveTo(moveParts, extraFrames, Enum.BulkMoveMode.FireCFrameChanged)
			return
		end
		for position = 1, count do
			moveParts[position] = standIns[indices[position]]
		end
		for position = count + 1, moveCount do
			moveParts[position] = nil
		end
		if offsetFrames then
			for position = 1, count do
				local standOffset = pieces[indices[position]].standOffset
				if standOffset then
					offsetFrames[position] = frames[position] * standOffset
				else
					offsetFrames[position] = frames[position]
				end
			end
			for position = count + 1, moveCount do
				offsetFrames[position] = nil
			end
			frames = offsetFrames
		end
		moveCount = count
		workspace:BulkMoveTo(moveParts, frames, Enum.BulkMoveMode.FireCFrameChanged)
	end

	function display.drop(index)
		local copy = standIns[index]
		if copy then
			if pieces[index].own then
				-- The part itself: hidden for good; its owner destroys it.
				Display.hide(copy, onServer, false)
				Display.quiet(copy)
			else
				copy:Destroy()
			end
			dropExtras(index)
			standIns[index] = nil
			dropped[index] = true
		end
	end

	-- A block takes its siblings with it: the part comes back whole or not at all.
	function display.restore(index)
		local piece = pieces[index]
		if piece.own then
			standIns[index] = nil
			dropped[index] = nil
			return
		end
		if piece.siblings then
			for _, sibling in ipairs(piece.siblings) do
				display.drop(sibling)
				dropped[sibling] = nil
			end
		else
			display.drop(index)
			dropped[index] = nil
		end
		showOriginal(piece.part)
	end

	function display.clear()
		for index, copy in pairs(standIns) do
			if not pieces[index].own then
				copy:Destroy()
			end
			dropExtras(index)
			standIns[index] = nil
		end
		for part in pairs(table.clone(hidden)) do
			showOriginal(part)
		end
	end

	-- The original of a piece, for whoever must leave it out of a ray.
	function display.original(index)
		return pieces[index].part
	end

	return display
end

return Display

--[[
	Driven: the pieces of a play that a Continuous Force is carrying (wind, a tornado, a pull).
	Part of Reactor/Play; reads and writes the play's own tables.

	A Continuous Force's Strength is the speed in studs per second it carries a piece at, along the
	direction Force/Fields gives. A carried piece takes up that speed within a fraction of a second
	(GRIP). Gravity still holds it down unless the flow rises, in which case it carries the piece up
	at the flow's speed until the piece leaves the shape and falls. Each piece is stepped live (one
	floor ray and one wall ray a step) only while a Force holds it; afterwards it is put back on a
	built path (Play:_launch) and lands like any other.

	A carried piece's way is kept (play.track[index] = { frames, times }: a pose every TRACK_EVERY
	seconds from when a Force took hold, thinned when long) so Reactor/After's Return can take it back
	the way it came. A piece a Force lets go and retakes from the same flight keeps one way.
	Play:_launch drops the way of a piece launched from anywhere but where a Force let it go.

	capture(play, record) takes in the pieces a Continuous record has reached.
	poseAt(track, seconds) -> the pose `seconds` after the Force took hold.
	step(play, dt, count) advances every driven piece, adds its pose to the play's move lists from
	position count + 1, and returns the new count.
]]

local Fields = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Fields)
local Trajectory = require(script.Parent.Parent.Rocks.Trajectory)

local RESTING = 0
local FLYING = 1
local LANDED = 2
local GONE = 3
local DRIVEN = 4

local ZERO = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)
local TINY = 1e-4
-- A pose this often per carried piece; a long way keeps every other pose.
local TRACK_EVERY = 0.05
local TRACK_MOST = 160
-- Steps at most this long, a few a frame.
local STEP_SECONDS = 1 / 60
local MAX_STEPS = 3
-- How fast a piece takes up the Force's speed, per second.
local GRIP = 6
-- How far below a piece the floor ray looks beyond the piece's own half height.
local FLOOR_MARGIN = 0.1
-- A flow whose upward part is at least this share of its speed spares a piece gravity; a level flow spares none.
local LIFTING_SHARE = 0.25
-- Turbulence: how fast gusts change, and how far apart two pieces' gusts are.
local GUST_RATE = 1.7
local GUST_SPREAD = 0.37

local Driven = {}

Driven.STATE = DRIVEN

-- How far a turned box reaches along a unit direction.
local function support(rotation, halfExt, direction)
	return math.abs(rotation.XVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.X
		+ math.abs(rotation.YVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.Y
		+ math.abs(rotation.ZVector:Dot(direction)) * halfExt.Z
end

-- What the Continuous Forces ask of a piece at `position`: the velocity to carry it at, the share
-- of gravity it is spared (0 level, 1 rising), and whether any Force holds it.
local function flowAt(play, index, position)
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	local velocity = ZERO
	local held = false
	for record in pairs(play.kicks) do
		if record.actsAs == "Continuous" and not record.ended then
			local strength = record.strength
			local direction, distance, distance01 = Fields.sample(record.field, position, strength < 0)
			if direction and distance <= record.front then
				local share = Fields.kept(record.falloff, distance01) * Fields.sizeShare(piece.size, record.sizeResponse)
				local gust = 1
				if record.turbulence > 0 then
					gust = 1 + record.turbulence * 2 * math.noise(play.clock * GUST_RATE, index * GUST_SPREAD, record.seed * 10)
				end
				velocity += direction * (math.abs(strength) * share * gust)
				held = true
			end
		end
	end
	local speed = velocity.Magnitude
	local rising = 0
	if speed > TINY then
		rising = math.clamp(velocity.Y / (speed * LIFTING_SHARE), 0, 1)
	end
	return velocity, rising, held
end

-- Adds a pose to a way, `seconds` after its start.
local function note(track, seconds, frame)
	table.insert(track.frames, frame)
	table.insert(track.times, seconds)
	track.due = seconds + track.every
	if #track.frames <= TRACK_MOST then
		return
	end
	local frames, times = {}, {}
	for place = 1, #track.frames, 2 do
		table.insert(frames, track.frames[place])
		table.insert(times, track.times[place])
	end
	if times[#times] ~= seconds then
		table.insert(frames, frame)
		table.insert(times, seconds)
	end
	track.frames = frames
	track.times = times
	track.every *= 2
end

function Driven.poseAt(track, seconds)
	local frames, times = track.frames, track.times
	local last = #times
	if seconds <= times[1] then
		return frames[1]
	elseif seconds >= times[last] then
		return frames[last]
	end
	local low, high = 1, last
	while high - low > 1 do
		local middle = (low + high) // 2
		if times[middle] <= seconds then
			low = middle
		else
			high = middle
		end
	end
	return frames[low]:Lerp(frames[high], (seconds - times[low]) / (times[high] - times[low]))
end

-- The way of a piece a Force takes hold of at `frame`; after a flight the last Force let it go
-- into, it continues the way it has.
local function wayFrom(play, index, frame, elapsed)
	local track = play.track[index]
	if not track or track.releasedAt ~= play.pathStart[index] then
		play.track[index] = { frames = { frame }, times = { 0 }, every = TRACK_EVERY, due = TRACK_EVERY, started = play.clock }
		return
	end
	local released = track.releasedAt - track.started
	local flown = track.every
	while flown < elapsed do
		note(track, released + flown, Trajectory.evaluate(play.path[index], flown, play.gravity[index]))
		flown += track.every
	end
	note(track, released + elapsed, frame)
	track.releasedAt = nil
end

local function enter(play, index)
	-- Read place and speed off the whole flight path, not the arc that knows no ground.
	play:_buildPath(index)
	local elapsed = play.clock - play.pathStart[index]
	local gravity = play.gravity[index]
	local frame = Trajectory.evaluate(play.path[index], elapsed, gravity)
	wayFrom(play, index, frame, elapsed)
	local velocity, spin = Trajectory.velocity(play.path[index], elapsed, gravity)
	if spin.Magnitude < TINY then
		spin = play.path[index].segs[1].w
	end
	play.drivePosition[index] = frame.Position
	play.driveRotation[index] = frame.Rotation
	play.driveVelocity[index] = velocity
	play.driveSpin[index] = spin
	play.state[index] = DRIVEN
	table.insert(play.driven, index)
end

-- Whether a Continuous record would carry a piece at `position` (faster than its Hold) and
-- whether its front is still on its way there.
local function reaches(play, record, index, position, pulls)
	local direction, distance, distance01 = Fields.sample(record.field, position, pulls)
	if not direction then
		return false, false
	end
	if distance > record.front then
		return false, true
	end
	local speed = math.abs(record.strength) * Fields.kept(record.falloff, distance01) * Fields.sizeShare(play.pieces[index].size, record.sizeResponse)
	return speed > play:_holdOf(index), false
end

-- Takes in the pieces a record has reached: a resting one is woken (joins the flow once it has its
-- stand-in), one out of place joins now. A Force no faster than Hold leaves a piece be.
-- Cross-file: the play's wait is held (play.held, Reactor/Follow) by a piece inside the shape the
-- front has yet to reach, and by one outside the flow whose own place is inside (it would be carried off again).
function Driven.capture(play, record)
	local pulls = record.strength < 0
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		local state = play.state[index]
		if state ~= DRIVEN and state ~= GONE then
			local carried, awaited = reaches(play, record, index, play:_position(index), pulls)
			if carried then
				if state == RESTING then
					play:_push(index, ZERO)
				elseif state == FLYING or state == LANDED then
					enter(play, index)
				end
				play:_takeTime(record)
			elseif awaited then
				play.held = true
			elseif state ~= RESTING and reaches(play, record, index, piece.rest.Position, pulls) then
				play.held = true
			end
		end
	end
end

-- One step of one piece; returns its new position, velocity and rotation.
local function advance(play, index, position, velocity, rotation, flow, spared, stepSeconds)
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	local gravity = play.gravity[index]
	velocity += (flow - velocity) * math.min(GRIP * stepSeconds, 1)
	velocity += Vector3.new(0, -gravity * (1 - spared) * stepSeconds, 0)
	local move = velocity * stepSeconds

	-- Walls: what lies ahead along the level part of the move.
	local level = Vector3.new(move.X, 0, move.Z)
	local levelDistance = level.Magnitude
	if levelDistance > TINY then
		local ahead = level / levelDistance
		local wall = play.castRay(position, ahead * (levelDistance + support(rotation, piece.halfExt, ahead)))
		if wall then
			local into = move:Dot(wall.Normal)
			if into < 0 then
				move -= wall.Normal * into
			end
			local speedInto = velocity:Dot(wall.Normal)
			if speedInto < 0 then
				velocity -= wall.Normal * speedInto
			end
		end
	end

	-- Floor: the piece stays at least its half height above what is under it.
	local halfHeight = support(rotation, piece.halfExt, Vector3.new(0, 1, 0))
	local floor = play.castRay(position, Vector3.new(0, -(halfHeight + math.max(-move.Y, 0) + FLOOR_MARGIN), 0))
	if floor then
		local lowest = floor.Position.Y + halfHeight
		if position.Y + move.Y < lowest then
			move = Vector3.new(move.X, lowest - position.Y, move.Z)
			if velocity.Y < 0 then
				velocity = Vector3.new(velocity.X, 0, velocity.Z)
			end
		end
	end

	local spin = play.driveSpin[index]
	local turn = spin.Magnitude
	if turn * stepSeconds > TINY then
		rotation = CFrame.fromAxisAngle(spin / turn, turn * stepSeconds) * rotation
	end
	return position + move, velocity, rotation
end

function Driven.step(play, dt, count)
	local driven = play.driven
	if #driven == 0 or dt <= 0 then
		return count
	end
	local steps = math.clamp(math.ceil(dt / STEP_SECONDS), 1, MAX_STEPS)
	local stepSeconds = dt / steps
	local place = 1
	while place <= #driven do
		local index = driven[place]
		local position = play.drivePosition[index]
		local velocity = play.driveVelocity[index]
		local rotation = play.driveRotation[index]
		local held = true
		for _ = 1, steps do
			local flow, spared, inside = flowAt(play, index, position)
			if not inside then
				held = false
				break
			end
			position, velocity, rotation = advance(play, index, position, velocity, rotation, flow, spared, stepSeconds)
		end

		local frame = rotation + position
		play.lastFrame[index] = frame
		local track = play.track[index]
		local carried = play.clock - track.started
		if held then
			if carried >= track.due then
				note(track, carried, frame)
			end
			play.drivePosition[index] = position
			play.driveVelocity[index] = velocity
			play.driveRotation[index] = rotation
			count += 1
			play.moveIndices[count] = index
			play.moveFrames[count] = frame
			place += 1
		else
			-- No Force holds it: back onto a built path from here at this speed.
			local last = #driven
			driven[place] = driven[last]
			driven[last] = nil
			play.state[index] = LANDED
			-- Its way ends where its flight begins (Play:_launch keeps a way marked so).
			note(track, carried, frame)
			track.kept = true
			track.releasedAt = play.clock
			play:_launch(index, frame, velocity, play.driveSpin[index])
		end
	end
	return count
end

return Driven

--[[
	Entries  -  the entry of a Reactor that is not at rest: its play, display and place on the engine's
	list. Part of the Reactor mixin: functions take the Particle table as `self` and use its
	_reactorPlays (reactor -> entry) and _reactorCutting (reactor -> cutting state).
	An entry: { reactor, group, play, pData?, cracksAgain, pieceCount, breaks, cracks, wounds, cutBy }.
	The play covers every part but the grounds, whose cracks are wounds (Reactor/Wounds). A cutting
	state: { records, place, emitCtx, owner, ticket }. An owned entry (Reactor/Owned) is the emitted
	copy of a mesh part-icle a Force reached; ending it ends the copy.
	  Entries.entryFor(self, reactor, emitCtx, record, owner) -> entry | nil, cutting state (shards first)
	  Entries.resume(self, entry) -> false when the particle cap refused it
	  Entries.putBack(entry), Entries.discard(self, entry, natural)
	  Entries.follow(self, entry, record, late), Entries.owe(cutting, record), Entries.forget(cutting)
	  Entries.step(entry, step, dt, override, frozen) -> "active" | "dormant" | "done"
	  Entries.crackAgain(self, entry, record, kicked)   Recrack or Recarve
	  Entries.emitOrigin(emitCtx) -> origin, fullPose | nil
	  Entries.prepare(self, item)   cuts a Reactor's shards ahead (PrepareReactor)
]]

local RangeMod = require(script.Parent.Parent.Range)
local Play = require(script.Parent.Play)
local Pieces = require(script.Parent.Pieces)
local Support = require(script.Parent.Support)
local Display = require(script.Parent.Display)
local Shards = require(script.Parent.Shards)
local CutPlan = require(script.Parent.CutPlan)
local Recrack = require(script.Parent.Recrack)
local Recarve = require(script.Parent.Recarve)
local Wounds = require(script.Parent.Wounds)
local Owned = require(script.Parent.Owned)
local Patches = require(script.Parent.Patches)
local GroundDisplay = require(script.Parent.GroundDisplay)
local Batch = require(script.Parent.Batch)

-- Pieces given a stand-in, and paths built, per Reactor per frame.
local WAKE_BUDGET = 100
local BUILD_BUDGET = 150
-- A piece is carried by the world when something that is not its Reactor lies this close under it.
local ANCHOR_REACH = 0.3
-- No strip of a ground between two wounds, or a wound and its edge, is thinner than this.
local GROUND_SNAP = 2

local Entries = {}

local function playSettings(data, isAnchored)
	return {
		Hold = data.Hold,
		HoldSpread = data.HoldSpread,
		Collapse = data.Collapse,
		isAnchored = isAnchored,
		After = data.After,
		AfterDelay = data.AfterDelay,
		AfterTime = data.AfterTime,
		MaxPieces = data.MaxPieces,
		MaxAirTime = data.MaxAirTime,
		wakeBudget = WAKE_BUDGET,
		buildBudget = BUILD_BUDGET,
		random = math.random,
		rollGravity = function()
			return RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Gravity)
		end,
		rollBounciness = function()
			return RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Bounciness)
		end,
		rollFriction = function()
			return RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.Friction)
		end,
		rollTumble = function()
			return math.rad(RangeMod.RandomValueFromRange(data.TumbleSpeed))
		end,
	}
end

-- A Reactor's own frame, which an origin stands in for.
local function hostFrame(reactor)
	if reactor:IsA("Model") then
		return reactor:GetPivot()
	end
	return reactor.CFrame
end

-- Where an emit puts the Reactor: an origin and whether its rotation counts, or nil in place.
function Entries.emitOrigin(emitCtx)
	if not emitCtx then
		return nil
	end
	local origin = nil
	if emitCtx.EventOriginResolver then
		origin = emitCtx.EventOriginResolver()
	end
	origin = origin or emitCtx.EventOriginCF
	if not origin then
		return nil
	end
	return origin, emitCtx.UseFullOrigin == true
end

-- Whether a Reactor's plain blocks are grounds (cracked where struck, never cut whole); never for a
-- reacting copy.
local function hasGrounds(data, emitCtx)
	return data.Break == "Shards" and data.ShardPattern == "Cracks" and Entries.emitOrigin(emitCtx) == nil and not data.NoGrounds
end

-- The Hit Filter: every ray of a play meets only what its collision group collides with, and never
-- what it excludes.
local function applyHitFilter(params, data)
	if data.HitGroup and data.HitGroup ~= "" then
		-- The group may have been deleted since.
		pcall(function()
			params.CollisionGroup = data.HitGroup
		end)
	end
	for _, instance in ipairs(data.HitExcludes or {}) do
		params:AddToFilter(instance)
	end
end

-- A play over some of a Reactor's pieces, and its display. Rays skip the runtime's folders and the
-- hidden originals; standing pieces stay solid to flying ones. keepOriginals: a wound's pieces.
local function makePlay(self, reactor, data, pieces, keepOriginals)
	local params = RaycastParams.new()
	params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	params.RespectCanCollide = true
	params.FilterDescendantsInstances = { self:GetFolder(), self:GetPoolFolder() }
	applyHitFilter(params, data)

	local display = Display.new(pieces, self:GetFolder(), Display.serverOnly(), keepOriginals)
	local showStandIn = display.wake
	local filtered = {}
	display.wake = function(index)
		local made = showStandIn(index)
		local original = display.original(index)
		-- Cracked ground is left in the rays' way: its base stands, and its pieces land on it.
		if not filtered[original] and not Display.cracked(pieces[index]) then
			filtered[original] = true
			params:AddToFilter(original)
		end
		return made
	end
	local function castRay(origin, displacement)
		return workspace:Raycast(origin, displacement, params)
	end

	-- What carries a piece is the world under it, the Reactor itself left out of the ray.
	local worldParams = RaycastParams.new()
	worldParams.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
	worldParams.RespectCanCollide = true
	worldParams.FilterDescendantsInstances = { reactor, self:GetFolder(), self:GetPoolFolder() }
	applyHitFilter(worldParams, data)
	local function isAnchored(index)
		local piece = pieces[index]
		if piece.fixed then
			return true
		end
		local drop = Support.worldHalf(piece).Y + ANCHOR_REACH
		return workspace:Raycast(piece.rest.Position, Vector3.new(0, -drop, 0), worldParams) ~= nil
	end

	local settings = playSettings(data, isAnchored)
	-- A wound gives its ground back when done (Reactor/After.close).
	settings.closes = keepOriginals == true
	-- A part cut whole into cracked ground mends as a wound does, with its cracking Force's After.
	if not keepOriginals then
		for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
			if piece.strike then
				settings.closes = true
				settings.takesAfter = true
				break
			end
		end
	end
	return Play.new(pieces, settings, display, castRay), display
end

-- The wounds of a Reactor's grounds, or nil when it has none.
local function woundsOf(self, entry, reactor, data, grounds)
	if #grounds == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local groundDisplay = GroundDisplay.new(self:GetFolder(), Display.serverOnly(), Shards.without)
	return Wounds.new({
		grounds = grounds,
		pieceCount = data.Pieces,
		maxPieces = data.MaxPieces,
		after = data.After,
		afterDelay = data.AfterDelay,
		snap = GROUND_SNAP,
		-- A wound asked for in a pass shows with the rest of the pass (Reactor/Batch).
		cut = function(jobs, done)
			local ticket = Batch.take()
			Patches.cut(jobs, function(sets)
				Batch.give(ticket, function()
					done(sets)
				end)
			end)
		end,
		play = function(pieces)
			return makePlay(self, reactor, data, pieces, true)
		end,
		draw = groundDisplay.draw,
		isCurrent = function()
			return self._reactorPlays[reactor] == entry
		end,
		revive = function()
			if not Entries.resume(self, entry) then
				Entries.discard(self, entry)
			end
		end,
	})
end

-- The entry of a Reactor at rest, or nil with neither pieces nor grounds. With an origin, the
-- stand-ins start there.
local function newEntry(self, reactor, data, emitCtx, shardSets, owner)
	local grounds = {}
	local isGround = {}
	if hasGrounds(data, emitCtx) then
		-- Blocks lying on each other are one ground, a skin on them a layer (Reactor/Layers).
		grounds, isGround = CutPlan.grounds(reactor)
	end
	local pieces = Pieces.collect(reactor, data.Break, data.Pieces, shardSets and function(part)
		return shardSets[part]
	end, function(part)
		return isGround[part] == true
	end)
	if #pieces == 0 and #grounds == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	if owner then
		Owned.mark(pieces, owner)
	end
	local origin, fullPose = Entries.emitOrigin(emitCtx)
	if origin then
		Pieces.carry(pieces, hostFrame(reactor), origin, fullPose)
	end

	local entry = {
		reactor = reactor,
		group = data.Group,
		play = makePlay(self, reactor, data, pieces, false),
		pData = nil,
		-- Whether later Impulses crack this ground again (Reactor/Recrack).
		cracksAgain = data.Break == "Shards" and data.ShardPattern == "Cracks",
		pieceCount = data.Pieces,
		breaks = CutPlan.byEngine(data),
		cracks = {},
	}
	entry.wounds = woundsOf(self, entry, reactor, data, grounds)
	if owner then
		Owned.adopt(entry, owner)
	end
	return entry
end

function Entries.resume(self, entry)
	if entry.pData then
		return true
	end
	-- An owned play is listed under its part-icle, so Disable, SetTimescale and a PlayHandle find it.
	local owner = entry.owner
	local source = owner and owner.source or entry.reactor
	local pData = {
		Type = "Reactor",
		VisualPart = nil,
		StartTime = os.clock(),
		TotalKeyFrames = 1,
		CurrentStep = -1,
		LifeTime = math.huge,
		PartLife = 0,
		Graphs = {},
		Seeds = {},
		_effectiveElapsed = 0,
		_sourceItem = source,
		_entry = entry,
	}
	pData._onReclaim = function()
		if entry.pData == pData then
			entry.pData = nil
		end
	end
	self._seedTsOverride(pData, source)
	entry.pData = pData
	self:_registerEmit(pData, owner and owner.context)
	return entry.pData == pData
end

function Entries.putBack(entry)
	entry.play:restore()
	if entry.wounds then
		entry.wounds:restore()
	end
end

function Entries.discard(self, entry, natural)
	Entries.putBack(entry)
	self._reactorPlays[entry.reactor] = nil
	Owned.gone(self, entry.owner, natural == true)
end

-- `kicked` is the record's list of the pieces it has kicked in the play.
function Entries.crackAgain(self, entry, record, kicked)
	if record.actsAs ~= "Impulse" then
		return
	end
	local function isCurrent()
		return self._reactorPlays[entry.reactor] == entry
	end
	local function revive()
		if not Entries.resume(self, entry) then
			Entries.discard(self, entry)
		end
	end
	-- A Force with a Cut carves and cracks nothing; its own first cut needs no second.
	if record.cut then
		if entry.cutBy ~= record then
			Recarve.request(entry, record, kicked, isCurrent, revive)
		end
		return
	end
	if entry.cracksAgain then
		Recrack.request(entry, record, kicked, isCurrent, revive)
	end
end

function Entries.follow(self, entry, record, late)
	local play = entry.play
	local follows, kicked
	if late then
		follows, kicked = play:answer(record, record.cut ~= nil and entry.cutBy ~= record)
		-- A copy's pieces were let go when its entry was made.
		follows = follows or entry.owner ~= nil
	else
		follows = play:watch(record)
	end
	local wounds = entry.wounds
	if wounds then
		-- The grounds crack whatever the other parts' play is doing.
		wounds:strike(record)
		if wounds:watch(record) or wounds:busy() then
			follows = true
		end
	end
	if not follows then
		return
	end
	if not Entries.resume(self, entry) then
		Entries.discard(self, entry)
		return
	end
	Entries.crackAgain(self, entry, record, kicked or play.kicks[record])
end

function Entries.step(entry, step, dt, override, frozen)
	local status = entry.play:step(step)
	if not entry.wounds then
		return status
	end
	local woundStatus = entry.wounds:step(dt, override, frozen)
	if status == "active" or woundStatus == "active" then
		return "active"
	end
	if status == "done" and woundStatus == "done" then
		return "done"
	end
	return "dormant"
end

-- A first cut is its Force's: Reactor/Crack and Reactor/Slash tell by it what that Force reaches.
local function cutFor(entry, record)
	entry.cutBy = record
	for _, piece in ipairs(entry.play.pieces) do
		if piece.strike and not piece.strike.by then
			piece.strike.by = record
		end
		if piece.slash and not piece.slash.by then
			piece.slash.by = record
		end
	end
end

-- Has a Reactor's shards cut and then gives it the entry it was owed: placed if an emit asked,
-- following live Forces, struck once by ended Impulses. A restore empties the state. A refusal may
-- come at once, so the answer waits until the caller has said what it wanted.
local function startCutting(self, reactor, data, sets, jobs, hit, record, owner)
	local state = { records = {}, place = false, emitCtx = nil, owner = owner }
	self._reactorCutting[reactor] = state
	local asked = false
	local function answer()
		if self._reactorCutting[reactor] ~= state then
			return
		end
		self._reactorCutting[reactor] = nil
		local wanted = state.place or #state.records > 0
		if not wanted or not self.Connection or not reactor.Parent or self._reactorPlays[reactor] then
			-- A copy with no entry is ended; nothing else would remove it.
			Owned.gone(self, owner, false)
			return
		end
		for _, job in ipairs(jobs) do
			sets[job.part] = Shards.get(job.part, job.key) or nil
		end
		local entry = newEntry(self, reactor, data, state.emitCtx, sets, owner)
		if not entry then
			Owned.gone(self, owner, false)
			return
		end
		self._reactorPlays[reactor] = entry
		if record then
			cutFor(entry, record)
		end
		-- A copy's pieces were let go as its entry was made (Reactor/Owned.adopt).
		local live = state.place or owner ~= nil
		if state.place then
			entry.play:place()
		end
		local kickedBy = {}
		for _, record in ipairs(state.records) do
			local struck, kicked = entry.play:answer(record, record.cut ~= nil and entry.cutBy ~= record)
			live = struck or live
			kickedBy[record] = kicked
		end
		if not live or not Entries.resume(self, entry) then
			Entries.discard(self, entry)
			return
		end
		-- The cut was around the first hit; other Impulses meanwhile crack again at their own places.
		if hit then
			Recrack.opened(entry, state.records, hit)
		end
		for _, record in ipairs(state.records) do
			Entries.crackAgain(self, entry, record, kickedBy[record])
			if entry.wounds then
				entry.wounds:strike(record)
			end
		end
	end
	-- The answer waits for the other cuts of its pass.
	local function kept()
		if not asked then
			asked = true
			task.defer(kept)
			return
		end
		Batch.give(state.ticket, answer)
	end
	Shards.prepare(jobs, kept)
	asked = true
	return state
end

-- A Reactor being cut owes this Force an entry; inside a pass it waits for the others.
function Entries.owe(cutting, record)
	if not table.find(cutting.records, record) then
		table.insert(cutting.records, record)
	end
	if not cutting.ticket then
		cutting.ticket = Batch.take()
	end
end

-- The Reactor is being put back as built: nobody is owed an entry any more.
function Entries.forget(cutting)
	if cutting then
		table.clear(cutting.records)
		cutting.place = false
		cutting.emitCtx = nil
	end
end

function Entries.entryFor(self, reactor, emitCtx, record, owner)
	local entry = self._reactorPlays[reactor]
	if entry then
		return entry
	end
	local cutting = self._reactorCutting[reactor]
	if cutting then
		return nil, cutting
	end
	local data = owner and owner.settings or self:GetData(reactor)
	if not data then
		return nil
	end
	local sets = nil
	local strike = CutPlan.strike(data, record)
	local hit = strike and strike.hit
	if CutPlan.byEngine(data) or (strike and strike.blade) then
		local jobs
		sets, jobs = CutPlan.of(reactor, data, hasGrounds(data, emitCtx), strike)
		if #jobs > 0 then
			return nil, startCutting(self, reactor, data, sets, jobs, hit, strike and record, owner)
		end
	end
	entry = newEntry(self, reactor, data, emitCtx, sets, owner)
	self._reactorPlays[reactor] = entry
	if entry and strike then
		cutFor(entry, record)
	end
	-- The cut is around this Force's hit: it asks for no later crack at that place.
	if entry and hit then
		Recrack.opened(entry, { record }, hit)
	end
	return entry
end

-- Returns at once; the cut takes frames. Its meshes are asked about whatever its Break: a blade
-- cuts any part.
function Entries.prepare(self, item)
	if self._reactorPlays[item] or self._reactorCutting[item] then
		return
	end
	for _, part in ipairs(Pieces.parts(item)) do
		Shards.judge(part)
	end
	local data = self:GetData(item)
	-- A skin's first cut is slow: warmed ahead (Reactor/Shards).
	if data and hasGrounds(data, nil) then
		local _, isGround = CutPlan.grounds(item)
		for part in pairs(isGround) do
			if not Pieces.isPlainBlock(part) then
				Shards.warm(part)
			end
		end
	end
	if not data or not CutPlan.byEngine(data) or CutPlan.waitsForHit(data) then
		return
	end
	local sets, jobs = CutPlan.of(item, data, false, nil)
	if #jobs > 0 then
		startCutting(self, item, data, sets, jobs)
	end
end

return Entries

--[[
	Fissure  -  a crack that runs along a line: what a Linear Force splits cracked ground into
	(Shard Pattern "Cracks"). Maths on Vector3 and CFrame values only, no instances.

	A round crack is rings of pieces around its hit. A split is the same rings drawn out along
	a path: a strip of pieces that sinks, lips beside it that are heaved, hairlines beyond.
	The path is the Force's line laid on the struck face and roughened, so a split wanders as a
	crack does; and it is a leaf, narrow where it starts, widest before its middle, a point at
	its end.

	Fissure.CRATER, Fissure.RIM
	    The shares of a crack's reach that are its crater and its rim. A round crack's reach is
	    its radius, a split's is how far its hairlines lie to either side of its path.
	    Reactor/Crack poses a piece by them; the rows of a split are laid by them.
	Fissure.reach(width, length) -> the reach of a split whose strip is `width` studs across at
	    its widest; never a thinner strip than LEAST_WIDTH of the split's length
	Fissure.of(field, frame, faceAt, normal, random) -> line or nil
	    field: Force/Fields'. frame: the part's. faceAt: any point of the struck face, normal:
	    that face's outward unit normal, both in the part's space. nil for any shape but Linear,
	    and for a line that points into the face more than along it: that is a round crack.
	    line = { path, reach, probes }: probes are places just under the face along the
	    Force's own straight line, to ask its field at.
	Fissure.path(start, along, normal, length, random) -> path
	    path = { points, run, length, normal }: points on one plane, run[index] the length up
	    to points[index]. Roughened by midpoint displacement: WANDER of the length at most.
	Fissure.moved(path, frame, toObject) -> the same path in another space: through `frame`
	    into the world, or with toObject out of the world into the frame's own space
	Fissure.at(path, share) -> position, direction     share 0 at the start, 1 at the end
	Fissure.from(path, position) -> away, share, outward
	    how far the position (laid onto the path's plane) is from the path, the share of the
	    way along its nearest place is, and the unit direction from that place out to it
	Fissure.leaf(share) -> 0 to 1: how wide the split is there, of its widest
	Fissure.places(count, path, reach, runOn, random, inside) -> { Vector3 }
	    about `count` places for the points of a split: rows along both sides of the path (the
	    strip, the lips, the hairlines, long pieces out to runOn times the reach), rubble in
	    the strip, a few round both ends so the strip stops there. inside(position) keeps one.
	Fissure.bounds(path) -> least, most: the corners of the box the path lies in
]]

local Fissure = {}

Fissure.CRATER = 0.42
Fissure.RIM = 0.71

-- The strip is never thinner than this share of the split's length, whatever the Force's Width.
local LEAST_WIDTH = 0.03
-- How far the path strays from the Force's line, as a share of its length, and in how many
-- halvings it is roughened.
local WANDER = 0.045
local LEVELS = 4
-- A line whose share along the face is under this points into it.
local FLAT_LEAST = 0.3
local PROBE_DEPTH = 0.5
local PROBE_SHARES = { 0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95 }
-- The share of the points that are rubble in the strip, and where along the path it lies.
local RUBBLE_SHARE = 0.1
local RUBBLE_FROM = 0.1
local RUBBLE_SPAN = 0.7
-- A strip wider than this many studs gets more than one row of pieces a side, three at most.
local ROW_WIDTH = 5
-- How many places a row gets against a strip row: fewer and longer pieces farther out.
local LIP_WEIGHT = 0.75
local HAIR_WEIGHT = 0.5
local FAR_WEIGHT = 0.3
-- Places round each end: { distance as a share of the width there, angle off the path }.
local CAPS = { { 0.6, 0 }, { 1.0, -0.9 }, { 1.0, 0.9 }, { 1.7, -0.5 }, { 1.7, 0.5 } }
local TINY = 1e-4

function Fissure.reach(width, length)
	return math.max(width / 2, length * LEAST_WIDTH) / Fissure.CRATER
end

function Fissure.path(start, along, normal, length, random)
	local side = normal:Cross(along)
	local points = { start, start + along * length }
	local sway = length * WANDER
	for _ = 1, LEVELS do
		local finer = {}
		for index = 1, #points - 1 do
			table.insert(finer, points[index])
			table.insert(finer, (points[index] + points[index + 1]) / 2 + side * ((random() * 2 - 1) * sway))
		end
		table.insert(finer, points[#points])
		points = finer
		sway /= 2
	end
	local run = { 0 }
	for index = 2, #points do
		run[index] = run[index - 1] + (points[index] - points[index - 1]).Magnitude
	end
	return { points = points, run = run, length = run[#run], normal = normal }
end

function Fissure.moved(path, frame, toObject)
	local points = table.create(#path.points)
	for index, point in ipairs(path.points) do
		if toObject then
			points[index] = frame:PointToObjectSpace(point)
		else
			points[index] = frame:PointToWorldSpace(point)
		end
	end
	local normal = path.normal
	if toObject then
		normal = frame:VectorToObjectSpace(normal)
	else
		normal = frame:VectorToWorldSpace(normal)
	end
	return { points = points, run = path.run, length = path.length, normal = normal }
end

function Fissure.at(path, share)
	local target = math.clamp(share, 0, 1) * path.length
	local points, run = path.points, path.run
	local index = 2
	while index < #points and run[index] < target do
		index += 1
	end
	local first, second = points[index - 1], points[index]
	local span = run[index] - run[index - 1]
	local direction = (second - first) / span
	return first + direction * (target - run[index - 1]), direction
end

function Fissure.from(path, position)
	local normal = path.normal
	local points, run = path.points, path.run
	local flat = position - normal * (position - points[1]):Dot(normal)
	local least, share, outward = math.huge, 0, nil
	for index = 2, #points do
		local first = points[index - 1]
		local step = points[index] - first
		local span = step.Magnitude
		local along = math.clamp((flat - first):Dot(step) / (span * span), 0, 1)
		local off = flat - (first + step * along)
		local away = off.Magnitude
		if away < least then
			least = away
			share = (run[index - 1] + span * along) / path.length
			if away > TINY then
				outward = off / away
			else
				outward = normal:Cross(step / span)
			end
		end
	end
	return least, share, outward
end

function Fissure.leaf(share)
	local rise = math.clamp(share / 0.4, 0, 1)
	local fall = math.clamp((1 - share) / 0.6, 0, 1)
	return 0.3 + 0.7 * math.sin(rise * math.pi / 2) * math.sin(fall * math.pi / 2) ^ 0.8
end

function Fissure.places(count, path, reach, runOn, random, inside)
	local normal = path.normal
	local places = {}
	local function add(position)
		if inside(position) then
			table.insert(places, position)
		end
	end

	local rubble = math.floor(count * RUBBLE_SHARE)
	for _ = 1, rubble do
		local share = RUBBLE_FROM + random() * RUBBLE_SPAN
		local position, direction = Fissure.at(path, share)
		local off = (random() * 2 - 1) * reach * Fissure.CRATER * Fissure.leaf(share) * 0.8
		add(position + normal:Cross(direction) * off)
	end

	-- Every row: how far from the path it lies, as a share of the reach, and its weight.
	local rows = {}
	local stripRows = math.clamp(math.ceil(reach * Fissure.CRATER / ROW_WIDTH), 1, 3)
	for row = 1, stripRows do
		table.insert(rows, { offset = (row - 0.5) / stripRows * Fissure.CRATER, weight = 1 })
	end
	table.insert(rows, { offset = (Fissure.CRATER + Fissure.RIM) / 2, weight = LIP_WEIGHT })
	table.insert(rows, { offset = (Fissure.RIM + 1) / 2, weight = HAIR_WEIGHT })
	-- The long pieces beyond keep to the path's line: they are no part of the leaf.
	table.insert(rows, { offset = (1 + runOn) / 2, weight = FAR_WEIGHT, straight = true })
	local weights = 0
	for _, row in ipairs(rows) do
		weights += row.weight * 2
	end
	local left = math.max(count - rubble - #CAPS * 2, #rows * 4)
	for _, row in ipairs(rows) do
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			local along = math.max(2, math.round(left * row.weight / weights))
			local phase = random()
			for step = 1, along do
				local share = (step - 1 + 0.1 + phase * 0.8) / along
				local position, direction = Fissure.at(path, share)
				local width = reach
				if not row.straight then
					width *= Fissure.leaf(share)
				end
				local off = side * row.offset * width * (1 + (random() - 0.5) * 0.3)
				add(position + normal:Cross(direction) * off)
			end
		end
	end

	for _, ending in ipairs({ { share = 0, turned = -1 }, { share = 1, turned = 1 } }) do
		local position, direction = Fissure.at(path, ending.share)
		local ahead = direction * ending.turned
		local across = normal:Cross(ahead)
		local width = math.max(reach * Fissure.leaf(ending.share), reach * 0.5)
		for _, cap in ipairs(CAPS) do
			local angle = cap[2] + (random() - 0.5) * 0.3
			add(position + (ahead * math.cos(angle) + across * math.sin(angle)) * (cap[1] * width))
		end
	end
	return places
end

function Fissure.bounds(path)
	local least, most = path.points[1], path.points[1]
	for _, point in ipairs(path.points) do
		least = Vector3.new(math.min(least.X, point.X), math.min(least.Y, point.Y), math.min(least.Z, point.Z))
		most = Vector3.new(math.max(most.X, point.X), math.max(most.Y, point.Y), math.max(most.Z, point.Z))
	end
	return least, most
end

function Fissure.of(field, frame, faceAt, normal, random)
	if field.shape ~= "Linear" then
		return nil
	end
	local heading = frame:VectorToObjectSpace(field.origin.LookVector)
	local flat = heading - normal * heading:Dot(normal)
	local share = flat.Magnitude
	if share < FLAT_LEAST then
		return nil
	end
	local along = flat / share
	local origin = frame:PointToObjectSpace(field.origin.Position)
	local onFace = origin - normal * (origin - faceAt):Dot(normal)
	local length = (field.range - field.inner) * share
	if length <= 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local start = onFace + along * (field.inner * share)
	local probes = {}
	for _, at in ipairs(PROBE_SHARES) do
		table.insert(probes, start + along * (length * at) - normal * PROBE_DEPTH)
	end
	return {
		path = Fissure.path(start, along, normal, length, random),
		reach = Fissure.reach(field.halfWidth * 2, length),
		probes = probes,
	}
end

return Fissure

--[[
	Follow  -  what Forces do to a play. Follow.methods are mixed into Reactor/Play, so each
	takes the play as `self` and reads and writes its own tables.

	A play follows the Forces it was told of for as long as each is alive (play.kicks: record ->
	the pieces that record has kicked). An Impulse kicks each piece once, when its front reaches
	it; a Continuous Force carries what lies in it (Reactor/Driven).

	Following is not waiting. A play's Delay runs from the moment its pieces lie still, and a
	Force that is still alive holds it up (play.held) only while it may yet move a piece here:
	a piece inside its shape that its front has not reached, a Force that is on its way
	somewhere (record.moving, Force/init) and has not kicked every piece, or a flow that still
	covers the place a piece was carried from (Reactor/Driven.capture). An Impulse that stands
	still, and any Force that reaches nothing of the play, holds nothing up.
	Cross-file: Play:step reads play.held, which _followForces works out afresh every step.

	methods: watch(record), strike(record), answer(record, cutsFirst),
	kickAgain(record, kicked, indices), _takeTime(record), _applyImpulse(record, kicked),
	_followForces()
]]

local Fields = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Fields)
local Driven = require(script.Parent.Driven)
local Crack = require(script.Parent.Crack)
local Slash = require(script.Parent.Slash)

local RESTING = 0
local GONE = 3

local Follow = {}
local methods = {}
Follow.methods = methods

-- Starts following a Force. False while the play is fading or returning: those finish first.
function methods:watch(record)
	if self.phase ~= "live" then
		return false
	end
	if not self.kicks[record] then
		self.kicks[record] = {}
	end
	return true
end

-- The kick of an Impulse that arrived before this play existed, given NOW: a Reactor whose
-- shards were still being cut (Reactor/init) answers late, and a short Impulse can be over
-- before this play's first step. One still alive is followed as well and remembers the
-- pieces it has kicked here. Returns true and the list of the pieces it kicked, which a
-- later crack asks for (kickAgain).
function methods:strike(record)
	if self.phase ~= "live" then
		return false
	end
	local kicked = {}
	if not record.ended and self:watch(record) then
		kicked = self.kicks[record]
	end
	self:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
	self.idleFor = 0
	return true, kicked
end

-- What a play does with a Force that reached its Reactor before the play could answer: an
-- Impulse strikes now, a flow that is still alive is followed. cutsFirst: the Force's blade
-- has a cut of its own to make first (Reactor/Recarve), which holds its kick until then.
-- Returns whether the play answers, and the record's list of the pieces it has kicked.
function methods:answer(record, cutsFirst)
	if record.actsAs == "Impulse" and not cutsFirst then
		return self:strike(record)
	end
	if record.actsAs ~= "Impulse" and record.ended then
		return false, nil
	end
	return self:watch(record), self.kicks[record]
end

-- The kick of an Impulse, given to pieces it has passed by: a later crack (Reactor/Recut) made
-- them or took them over after the Impulse arrived. `kicked` is that Impulse's own list of the
-- pieces it has kicked here; no other piece is kicked twice.
function methods:kickAgain(record, kicked, indices)
	if self.phase ~= "live" then
		return
	end
	for _, index in ipairs(indices) do
		kicked[index] = nil
	end
	self:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
	self.idleFor = 0
end

-- A Force that moves a piece of this play lends the play its time. Following one is not
-- enough: a play out of place follows every Force of its Group, however far away.
function methods:_takeTime(record)
	local times = self.times
	local carried = record.time
	if carried and not table.find(times, carried) then
		table.insert(times, carried)
	end
	local own = record.ownTime
	if own and not table.find(times, own) then
		table.insert(times, own)
	end
end

-- One kick for every piece the front of an Impulse has reached since the last frame.
function methods:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
	local settings = self.settings
	local field = record.field
	local front = record.front
	local strength = record.strength
	local pulls = strength < 0
	local waits = self.recracking[record]
	local moving = record.moving == true
	Slash.kick(self, record, kicked)
	for index, piece in ipairs(self.pieces) do
		local standsBy = waits and (waits == "all" or (piece.strike ~= nil and self.state[index] == RESTING))
		if not kicked[index] and self.state[index] ~= GONE and not piece.fixed and not standsBy then
			local direction, distance, distance01 = Fields.sample(field, self:_position(index), pulls)
			if not direction then
				direction, distance, distance01 = Crack.reached(piece, record, pulls)
			end
			if direction and distance <= front then
				kicked[index] = true
								-- Cracked ground that is no wound's: the last Force with an After of its own decides.
				if piece.strike and settings.takesAfter and record.after then
					settings.After = record.after
					settings.AfterDelay = record.afterDelay or settings.AfterDelay
				end
				local share = Fields.sizeShare(piece.size, record.sizeResponse)
				local spread = 1 + record.variation * (settings.random() * 2 - 1)
				local throw = strength * Fields.kept(record.falloff, distance01) * share * spread
				if math.abs(throw) > self:_holdOf(index) and not Crack.holds(piece) then
					self:_push(index, direction * Fields.throwSpeed(throw, self:_rolled(index)))
					self:_takeTime(record)
				elseif piece.strike then
					Crack.strike(self, index, strength)
				end
			elseif direction or moving then
				self.held = true
			end
		end
	end
end

function methods:_followForces()
	self.held = false
	for record, kicked in pairs(self.kicks) do
		if record.ended then
			self.kicks[record] = nil
		elseif record.actsAs == "Impulse" then
			self:_applyImpulse(record, kicked)
		else
			Driven.capture(self, record)
			if record.moving then
				self.held = true
			end
		end
	end
end

return Follow

--[[
	Footprint  -  what one Impulse cracks of a ground's struck face (Reactor/Wounds), and the
	template each rectangle of it is cut from (Reactor/Patches). Numbers only, no instances.

	A round Force opens a square around its hit, PATCH_REACH Ranges to each side: a little past
	what it can move, so the pieces along the square's sides stay at rest, and two Forces
	farther apart than twice that along one axis of the face never share ground. A Linear Force
	that lies along the face opens a strip around its split's path (Reactor/Fissure).

	Footprint.of(ground, field, hitInPart, reach, seed) -> footprint
	    ground: { frame, size, face = { axis, side }, uAxis, vAxis } (Reactor/Wounds).
	    field: Force/Fields'. hitInPart: where the Force is, in the ground's space. reach: its
	    Range. seed: the split's path is drawn from it, the same for every ground and every
	    later crack of one Force at one place.
	    footprint = { minU, minV, maxU, maxV, area, reach, probes, line }: the rectangle of the
	    face, how far the crack's hairlines go, places just under the face to ask the field
	    at, and for a split its line (Reactor/Fissure.of), nil for a round crack.
	Footprint.reaches(footprint, rectangle) -> whether the crack moves any of that rectangle
	Footprint.job(ground, rectangle, footprint, hitInPart, seed, alone, pieces) -> job
	    The template one rectangle is cut from: { size, frame, hit, reach, count, seed, face,
	    line, whole, variant }. hit and line are in the template's own space. A rectangle that
	    is all of a round crack's square (alone = it is the footprint's only one) is whole: its
	    cut depends on nothing but its size, the Range, the count and `variant`, so
	    Reactor/Patches keeps it. A split is never whole: its path turns with its Force.
	    A rectangle of a blade's wound is carved, not cracked: its job has bladeFrame,
	    bladeSize and slash in the template's space, the cut's mode, and stands = true, since
	    what a blade leaves of the ground never moves (Reactor/Carve).
	    A round crack's rectangle gets its share of `pieces` by its area. A split's rectangles
	    all carry the whole count and the line's seed: its places are laid once along the
	    path, and each rectangle keeps those that fall in it (Reactor/Sites.cracks).
	Footprint.pieces(footprint, jobs) -> the pieces those jobs are expected to bring: every
	    place gives Sites.LAYERS of them, every job a base; a carved rectangle its one side
	    and, with Band, the most bits a cut gives
	Footprint.ofBlade(ground, blade, mode, room) -> footprint or nil
	    The wound of a Force with a Cut (Reactor/Blade): the rectangle of the face its blade
	    stands over, BLADE_MARGIN studs more to every side, so the blade ends inside the patch
	    and the patch stays in one piece with a gash in it. nil when there is no blade or it
	    does not come down into the ground. room: the pieces the budget still has room for;
	    with too little for a Band's debris the gash is cut as Halves. footprint = { minU,
	    minV, maxU, maxV, area, reach = 0, blade, mode, under }, under the blade's own rectangle.
	Footprint.bladePieces(mode) -> the pieces one cut of a blade may bring
]]

local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Fissure = require(script.Parent.Fissure)
local Blade = require(script.Parent.Blade)
local Carve = require(script.Parent.Carve)
local Layers = require(script.Parent.Layers)

local Footprint = {}

Footprint.PATCH_REACH = 1.3
-- A split's strip of ground lies this many times its reach to either side of its path.
local STRIP_REACH = 2.2
-- The different cuts kept of one whole square (Reactor/Patches).
local VARIANTS = 3
local SAME_LENGTH = 1e-3
-- A blade's wound reaches this many studs past the blade to every side.
local BLADE_MARGIN = 2
-- A blade that comes less than this far under the face cuts nothing worth a wound.
local LEAST_DEPTH = 0.05
local SIGNS = { -1, 1 }

function Footprint.ofBlade(ground, blade, mode, room)
	local size = ground.size
	if not blade or not Blade.touches(blade, ground.frame, size) then
		return nil
	end
	-- Debris is made only while the budget has room for it: the cut itself always shows.
	if mode == "Band" and room and room < 2 * Footprint.bladePieces(mode) then
		mode = "Halves"
	end
	local axis, side = ground.face.axis, ground.face.side
	local uAxis, vAxis = ground.uAxis, ground.vAxis
	local own = Blade.inPart(blade, ground.frame)
	local half = blade.size / 2
	local minU, minV, maxU, maxV = math.huge, math.huge, -math.huge, -math.huge
	local deepest = -math.huge
	for _, x in ipairs(SIGNS) do
		for _, y in ipairs(SIGNS) do
			for _, z in ipairs(SIGNS) do
				local corner = own:PointToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(x * half.X, y * half.Y, z * half.Z))
				minU = math.min(minU, corner[uAxis])
				maxU = math.max(maxU, corner[uAxis])
				minV = math.min(minV, corner[vAxis])
				maxV = math.max(maxV, corner[vAxis])
				deepest = math.max(deepest, size[axis] / 2 - corner[axis] * side)
			end
		end
	end
	if deepest < LEAST_DEPTH then
		return nil
	end
	return {
		minU = minU - BLADE_MARGIN, minV = minV - BLADE_MARGIN, maxU = maxU + BLADE_MARGIN, maxV = maxV + BLADE_MARGIN,
		area = (maxU - minU + 2 * BLADE_MARGIN) * (maxV - minV + 2 * BLADE_MARGIN),
		reach = 0,
		blade = blade,
		mode = mode,
		under = { minU = minU, minV = minV, maxU = maxU, maxV = maxV },
	}
end

function Footprint.of(ground, field, hitInPart, reach, seed)
	local size = ground.size
	local axis, side = ground.face.axis, ground.face.side
	local uAxis, vAxis = ground.uAxis, ground.vAxis
	local normal = Sites.alongFace(axis, 0, 0, side)
	local faceAt = normal * (size[axis] / 2)
	local line = Fissure.of(field, ground.frame, faceAt, normal, Sites.sequence(seed))
	if line then
		local least, most = Fissure.bounds(line.path)
		local margin = line.reach * STRIP_REACH
		local minU, maxU = least[uAxis] - margin, most[uAxis] + margin
		local minV, maxV = least[vAxis] - margin, most[vAxis] + margin
		line.seed = seed
		return {
			minU = minU, minV = minV, maxU = maxU, maxV = maxV,
			area = (maxU - minU) * (maxV - minV),
			reach = line.reach,
			probes = line.probes,
			line = line,
			uAxis = uAxis, vAxis = vAxis,
		}
	end
	local u, v = hitInPart[uAxis], hitInPart[vAxis]
	local half = reach * Footprint.PATCH_REACH
	return {
		minU = u - half, minV = v - half, maxU = u + half, maxV = v + half,
		area = 4 * half * half,
		reach = reach,
		probes = Sites.probes(size, axis, side, u, v, reach),
		u = u, v = v, half = half,
	}
end

-- How far (u, v) lies from a rectangle of the face.
local function awayFrom(rectangle, u, v)
	local awayU = math.max(rectangle.minU - u, 0, u - rectangle.maxU)
	local awayV = math.max(rectangle.minV - v, 0, v - rectangle.maxV)
	return math.sqrt(awayU * awayU + awayV * awayV)
end

function Footprint.reaches(footprint, rectangle)
	local under = footprint.under
	if under then
		return rectangle.minU < under.maxU and rectangle.maxU > under.minU and rectangle.minV < under.maxV and rectangle.maxV > under.minV
	end
	local line = footprint.line
	if not line then
		return awayFrom(rectangle, footprint.u, footprint.v) <= footprint.reach
	end
	for _, point in ipairs(line.path.points) do
		if awayFrom(rectangle, point[footprint.uAxis], point[footprint.vAxis]) <= line.reach then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

function Footprint.job(ground, rectangle, footprint, hitInPart, seed, alone, pieces)
	local width = rectangle.maxU - rectangle.minU
	local height = rectangle.maxV - rectangle.minV
	local axis = ground.face.axis
	local centre = Sites.alongFace(axis, (rectangle.minU + rectangle.maxU) / 2, (rectangle.minV + rectangle.maxV) / 2, 0)
	local size = Sites.alongFace(axis, width, height, ground.size[axis])
	local layers = nil
	if ground.layers then
		layers = Layers.inPatch(ground, centre, size)
	end
	local blade = footprint.blade
	if blade then
		local patch = ground.frame * CFrame.new(centre.X, centre.Y, centre.Z)
		-- Asked with the whole ground: every patch of it is cut by the same ribbon.
		local ribbon, ribbonFrame = Blade.ribbonFor(blade, ground.frame, ground.size, patch:Inverse())
		return {
			size = size,
			frame = patch,
			layers = layers,
			face = ground.face,
			seed = seed,
			-- Reactor/Patches cuts no job that asks for fewer than two pieces.
			count = 2,
			bladeFrame = Blade.inPart(blade, patch),
			bladeSize = blade.size,
			ribbon = ribbon,
			ribbonFrame = ribbonFrame,
			always = true,
			slash = {
				origin = patch:PointToObjectSpace(blade.origin),
				normal = patch:VectorToObjectSpace(blade.normal),
				heading = patch:VectorToObjectSpace(blade.heading),
				kerf = blade.kerf,
			},
			mode = footprint.mode,
			stands = true,
		}
	end
	-- A rectangle that is a part of the footprint gets that share of the points.
	local wanted = math.max(math.floor(pieces * width * height / footprint.area + 0.5), 2)
	local job = {
		size = size,
		frame = ground.frame * CFrame.new(centre.X, centre.Y, centre.Z),
		hit = hitInPart - centre,
		reach = footprint.reach,
		count = Sites.count(size, wanted),
		seed = seed,
		face = ground.face,
		layers = layers,
	}
	local line = footprint.line
	if line then
		job.count = Sites.count(size, pieces)
		job.line = { path = Fissure.moved(line.path, CFrame.new(centre.X, centre.Y, centre.Z), true), reach = line.reach, seed = line.seed }
		return job
	end
	local side = 2 * footprint.half
	local skinned = false
	for _, share in ipairs(layers or {}) do
		skinned = skinned or share.skin ~= nil
	end
	-- Under a skin a square is no cut of its size alone: the skin's outline differs from place to place.
	if alone and not skinned and math.abs(width - side) < SAME_LENGTH and math.abs(height - side) < SAME_LENGTH then
		job.whole = true
		job.variant = math.floor(seed / 4) % VARIANTS
		job.hit = Sites.alongFace(axis, 0, 0, ground.face.side * ground.size[axis] / 2)
	end
	return job
end

-- The pieces one cut of a blade may bring: a side, and with Band the most debris a cut gives.
function Footprint.bladePieces(mode)
	if mode == "Band" then
		return 1 + Carve.MOST_BITS
	end
	return 1
end

function Footprint.pieces(footprint, jobs)
	if footprint.blade then
		local carved = 0
		for _, job in ipairs(jobs) do
			if job.layers then
				carved += #job.layers
			else
				carved += 1
			end
		end
		return carved * Footprint.bladePieces(footprint.mode)
	end
	local bases = #jobs
	local places = 0
	for _, job in ipairs(jobs) do
		if footprint.line then
			places = math.max(places, job.count)
		else
			places += job.count
		end
	end
	return places * Sites.LAYERS + bases
end

return Footprint

--[[

	(Reactor/Wounds) and what is left intact. Numbers only, no instances.

	A place is (u, v) on the face, in studs from its middle. A rectangle is
	{ minU, minV, maxU, maxV }.

	Ground.new(halfU, halfV, snap) -> ground
	    snap: the least width of anything this makes. An edge nearer than that to an edge
	    already there is laid onto it, so no strip thinner than `snap` is ever left.
	ground:claim(owner, centreU, centreV, half) -> { rectangle }
	    The square of half-side `half` around the centre, cut to the face, less what is held
	    already. The rectangles returned are intact ground no longer: they are `owner`'s until
	    released. Empty when the square holds nothing intact.
	ground:claimArea(owner, minU, minV, maxU, maxV) -> { rectangle }
	    The same for any rectangle of the face: a split along a line needs a strip, not a square.
	ground:release(owner)
	ground:held(owner) -> { rectangle }: what `owner` holds, or nil
	ground:touching(minU, minV, maxU, maxV) -> { owner }: whose rectangles overlap that area,
	    in the order they claimed
	ground:remainder(unshown) -> { rectangle }: the intact ground, as few large rectangles
	    unshown: nil, or a set of owners (owner -> true) whose rectangles still count as
	    intact: a crack that holds its ground while its pieces are being cut.

local Ground = {}
Ground.__index = Ground

function Ground.new(halfU, halfV, snap)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Ground)
	self.halfU = halfU
	self.halfV = halfV
	self.snap = snap
	self.rectangles = {}
	self.owners = {}
	return self
end

-- Every edge on one axis: the face's two and those of every held rectangle.
local function edgesOf(self, minKey, maxKey, half)
	local edges = { -half, half }
	for _, owner in ipairs(self.owners) do
		for _, rectangle in ipairs(self.rectangles[owner]) do
			table.insert(edges, rectangle[minKey])
			table.insert(edges, rectangle[maxKey])
		end
	end
	return edges
end

-- `value`, laid onto the nearest of `edges` when one is nearer than `snap`.
local function snapped(value, edges, snap)
	local best = value
	local least = snap
	for _, edge in ipairs(edges) do
		local distance = math.abs(edge - value)
		if distance < least then
			least = distance
			best = edge
		end
	end
	return best
end

-- The distinct values of `edges` from `low` to `high`, both ends among them, in order, and the
-- place of each value in that list.
local function cuts(edges, low, high)
	local within = { low, high }
	for _, edge in ipairs(edges) do
		if edge > low and edge < high then
			table.insert(within, edge)
		end
	end
	table.sort(within)
	local distinct = {}
	local placeOf = {}
	for _, edge in ipairs(within) do
		if distinct[#distinct] ~= edge then
			table.insert(distinct, edge)
			placeOf[edge] = #distinct
		end
	end
	return distinct, placeOf
end

-- The part of an area that nobody holds, as rectangles. The held rectangles' edges make a grid
-- of cells over the area; the free cells are merged, row by row, into the largest rectangles
-- they give. `unshown`: owners whose rectangles count as free.
local function freeIn(self, minU, minV, maxU, maxV, unshown)
	local us, columnOf = cuts(edgesOf(self, "minU", "maxU", self.halfU), minU, maxU)
	local vs, rowOf = cuts(edgesOf(self, "minV", "maxV", self.halfV), minV, maxV)
	local columns = #us - 1
	local rows = #vs - 1

	local taken = {}
	for _, owner in ipairs(self.owners) do
		local counted = self.rectangles[owner]
		if unshown and unshown[owner] then
			counted = {}
		end
		for _, rectangle in ipairs(counted) do
			local overlaps = rectangle.minU < maxU and rectangle.maxU > minU and rectangle.minV < maxV and rectangle.maxV > minV
			if overlaps then
				local firstColumn = columnOf[math.max(rectangle.minU, minU)]
				local lastColumn = columnOf[math.min(rectangle.maxU, maxU)] - 1
				local firstRow = rowOf[math.max(rectangle.minV, minV)]
				local lastRow = rowOf[math.min(rectangle.maxV, maxV)] - 1
				for row = firstRow, lastRow do
					for column = firstColumn, lastColumn do
						taken[(row - 1) * columns + column] = true
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end

	local rectangles = {}
	for row = 1, rows do
		for column = 1, columns do
			if not taken[(row - 1) * columns + column] then
				local lastColumn = column
				while lastColumn < columns and not taken[(row - 1) * columns + lastColumn + 1] do
					lastColumn += 1
				end
				local lastRow = row
				local grows = true
				while grows and lastRow < rows do
					for across = column, lastColumn do
						if taken[lastRow * columns + across] then
							grows = false
							break
						end
					end
					if grows then
						lastRow += 1
					end
				end
				for filled = row, lastRow do
					for across = column, lastColumn do
						taken[(filled - 1) * columns + across] = true
					end
				end
				table.insert(rectangles, { minU = us[column], minV = vs[row], maxU = us[lastColumn + 1], maxV = vs[lastRow + 1] })
			end
		end
	end
	return rectangles
end

function Ground:claim(owner, centreU, centreV, half)
	return self:claimArea(owner, centreU - half, centreV - half, centreU + half, centreV + half)
end

function Ground:claimArea(owner, lowU, lowV, highU, highV)
	local snap = self.snap
	local uEdges = edgesOf(self, "minU", "maxU", self.halfU)
	local vEdges = edgesOf(self, "minV", "maxV", self.halfV)
	local minU = snapped(math.max(lowU, -self.halfU), uEdges, snap)
	local maxU = snapped(math.min(highU, self.halfU), uEdges, snap)
	local minV = snapped(math.max(lowV, -self.halfV), vEdges, snap)
	local maxV = snapped(math.min(highV, self.halfV), vEdges, snap)
	if maxU - minU < snap or maxV - minV < snap then
		return {}
	end
	local rectangles = freeIn(self, minU, minV, maxU, maxV)
	if #rectangles == 0 then
		return rectangles
	end
	local own = self.rectangles[owner]
	if not own then
		self.rectangles[owner] = rectangles
		table.insert(self.owners, owner)
		return rectangles
	end
	for _, rectangle in ipairs(rectangles) do
		table.insert(own, rectangle)
	end
	return rectangles
end

function Ground:release(owner)
	if not self.rectangles[owner] then
		return
	end
	self.rectangles[owner] = nil
	table.remove(self.owners, table.find(self.owners, owner))
end

function Ground:held(owner)
	return self.rectangles[owner]
end

function Ground:touching(minU, minV, maxU, maxV)
	local found = {}
	for _, owner in ipairs(self.owners) do
		for _, rectangle in ipairs(self.rectangles[owner]) do
			if rectangle.minU < maxU and rectangle.maxU > minU and rectangle.minV < maxV and rectangle.maxV > minV then
				table.insert(found, owner)
				break
			end
		end
	end
	return found
end

function Ground:remainder(unshown)
	return freeIn(self, -self.halfU, -self.halfV, self.halfU, self.halfV, unshown)
end

function Ground:isWhole()
	return #self.owners == 0
end

return Ground
