--[[
	GroundDisplay: what is left intact of a ground that has open cracks (Reactor/Wounds): plain boxes
	around the wounds in the ground's look, while the ground itself is hidden.

	The ground is LIVE user content. It is written one way only, by Reactor/Display's hide and show,
	once per ground however many wounds are open, and it stays solid so thrown debris lands on it. The
	boxes are COPY parts that are not saved (Archivable off, under the runtime's folder, marked
	_PartIcleEmit) and that nothing collides with.

	A tiling Texture on the struck face is carried onto the boxes with its offset moved so the pattern
	runs on across them. This works for the top face only (a Texture is laid from the face's +X and +Z
	edges); on another face the boxes carry no Texture. A Decal is stretched over its face and cannot be carried.

	GroundDisplay.new(folder, onServer, without) -> display
	  without: Reactor/Shards.without, for the skins (Reactor/SkinDisplay).
	display.draw(ground, rectangles, face)
	  ground: { part, frame, size } (Reactor/Wounds). rectangles: the intact rest of its face `face`
	  ({ axis, side }), each { minU, minV, maxU, maxV } (Reactor/Ground); the boxes are those
	  rectangles through the ground. nil: the ground is whole again, its boxes go and it is shown.
	  A stacked ground (Reactor/Layers) is drawn layer by layer, each as a ground of its own (its slice).
	display.clear()   every ground whole again
]]

local Display = require(script.Parent.Display)
local Index = require(script.Parent.Index)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Layers = require(script.Parent.Layers)
local SkinDisplay = require(script.Parent.SkinDisplay)

local GroundDisplay = {}

-- A bare copy of the ground, to be sized as one box.
local function makeBox(part, folder)
	local box = Instance.fromExisting(part)
	box.Name = "GroundBox"
	box.Archivable = false
	box.Anchored = true
	box.CanCollide = false
	box.CanQuery = false
	box.CanTouch = false
	box.Locked = true
	-- On a server the ground is hidden through its own Transparency, which the copy took.
	box.Transparency = Display.ownTransparency(part)
	Index.unmark(box)
	box:SetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit", true)
	box.Parent = folder
	return box
end

-- The ground's Textures that tile its struck face, when they can be carried on that face.
local function carried(ground, face)
	local part = ground.part
	local textures = {}
	-- plain: a layer turned otherwise than its stack has its own Top elsewhere.
	if ground.plain or face.axis ~= "Y" or face.side ~= 1 then
		return textures
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("Texture") and child.Face == Enum.NormalId.Top then
			table.insert(textures, child)
		end
	end
	return textures
end

function GroundDisplay.new(folder, onServer, without)
	-- part -> { boxes, kept (what Display.show puts back), textures }
	local drawn = {}
	local display = {}
	-- A skin (Reactor/Layers) is no box: what is intact of it is the skin with holes in it.
	local skins = SkinDisplay.new(folder, onServer, without)

	local function whole(part)
		local state = drawn[part]
		if not state then
			return
		end
		drawn[part] = nil
		for _, box in ipairs(state.boxes) do
			box:Destroy()
		end
		Display.show(part, onServer, state.kept)
	end

	function display.draw(ground, rectangles, face)
		if ground.layers then
			for _, layer in ipairs(ground.layers) do
				if layer.skin then
					skins.draw(ground, layer, rectangles, face)
				else
					local own = rectangles
					if own then
						own = Layers.clip(ground, layer, rectangles, face)
					end
					display.draw(layer.slice, own, face)
				end
			end
			return
		end
		local part = ground.part
		if not rectangles then
			whole(part)
			return
		end
		local state = drawn[part]
		if not state then
			-- Textures are read before the ground is hidden: hiding writes them too.
			state = { boxes = {}, textures = carried(ground, face) }
			drawn[part] = state
		end
		local boxes = state.boxes
		for position = #boxes, #rectangles + 1, -1 do
			boxes[position]:Destroy()
			boxes[position] = nil
		end
		local thickness = ground.size[face.axis]
		for position, rectangle in ipairs(rectangles) do
			local box = boxes[position]
			if not box then
				box = makeBox(part, folder)
				for _, texture in ipairs(state.textures) do
					local copy = texture:Clone()
					-- The ground's own Texture is hidden with it; the copy is not.
					Display.unhidden(copy, texture)
					copy.Parent = box
				end
				boxes[position] = box
			end
			local centre = Sites.alongFace(face.axis, (rectangle.minU + rectangle.maxU) / 2, (rectangle.minV + rectangle.maxV) / 2, 0)
			box.Size = Sites.alongFace(face.axis, rectangle.maxU - rectangle.minU, rectangle.maxV - rectangle.minV, thickness)
			box.CFrame = ground.frame * CFrame.new(centre.X, centre.Y, centre.Z)
			if #state.textures > 0 then
				local copies = {}
				for _, child in ipairs(box:GetChildren()) do
					if child:IsA("Texture") then
						table.insert(copies, child)
					end
				end
				for place, texture in ipairs(state.textures) do
					copies[place].OffsetStudsU = texture.OffsetStudsU + ground.size.X / 2 - rectangle.maxU
					copies[place].OffsetStudsV = texture.OffsetStudsV + ground.size.Z / 2 - rectangle.maxV
				end
			end
		end
		-- Hidden last, so the boxes are there in the frame the ground goes.
		if not state.kept then
			state.kept = Display.hide(part, onServer, true)
		end
	end

	function display.clear()
		for part in pairs(table.clone(drawn)) do
			whole(part)
		end
		skins.clear()
	end

	return display
end

return GroundDisplay

--[[
	HandOver Mixin  -  a mesh part-icle that becomes a Reactor. A mesh whose config says Reacts plays
	as authored until a Force of its Group reaches its emitted copy. In that frame its own play ends
	and the copy is handed to the Reactor code: an entry is made around it (Reactor/Entries, owner:
	Reactor/Owned), and Play, After and the rest run it from there.

	_watchForForces(pData, settings, whole)
	    EmitPart calls it for a play whose data has Reactor settings, before it registers the play.
	    The play is listed in Particle._watched; pData._onReclaim (run by every removal route,
	    LifecycleRelease._reclaimPData) takes it off. `whole`: a Matte carries the copy, which then
	    reacts in one piece and is never cut. Asks the engine now whether it cuts the copy's mesh
	    at all (Shards.judge, once a mesh a session), since a refusal is slow.
	_handOverReached(now)
	    Engine's step calls it before it walks ActiveEmits. Does nothing while no play is watched or
	    no Force is alive. Else reads each record's place and reach once, then for each watched play
	    checks the record's Group, the copy's place and size and a distance, and only then
	    Reactor/Reach. Makes no table, but for a Force with a Cut whose box the copy is in
	    (Reactor/Blade.touches).
	_followReacted(record)
	    Reactor/init's _reactToForce calls it: a reacted copy follows a later Force of its Group
	    that could reach one of its pieces. Copies carry no tag and may be hundreds, so one out of
	    reach stays off the engine's list.
	_endReacted(item, token)
	    Releases at once every reacted copy of an item (item given) or of one play (token given).
	    Lifecycle.Disable and PlayHandle:Disable call it.

	The hand-over: the copy's velocity is measured (Reactor/Momentum); its play leaves ActiveEmits
	without dying and is kept by the owner, which ends it when the copy is gone; the entry lets every
	piece go at that velocity (Owned.adopt) and the Force strikes. A copy the engine has to cut first
	hangs where it was reached until the cut is in. Copies reached in one frame are one pass
	(Reactor/Batch) and answer together. Max Pieces is the most reacted pieces of one item out at
	once; a hand-over past it sends the oldest away, sunk where they lie.

	Mutates: the copy and its play (both the runtime's own).
	Cross-file: sets _onReclaim on a Part play; another user of it must chain.
	Flipbook.luau and MeshFrames.luau stop a play's tasks on pData._handedOver.
]]

local ForceRegistry = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Registry)
local Index = require(script.Parent.Index)
local Entries = require(script.Parent.Entries)
local Play = require(script.Parent.Play)
local Owned = require(script.Parent.Owned)
local Reach = require(script.Parent.Reach)
local Momentum = require(script.Parent.Momentum)
local Blade = require(script.Parent.Blade)
local Shards = require(script.Parent.Shards)
local Batch = require(script.Parent.Batch)

-- Seconds a copy the cap sends away takes to sink where it lies.
local LEAVE_SECONDS = 0.25

return function(Particle)

-- The plays that may react, in no order; pData._watchIndex is a play's place in it.
Particle._watched = {}
-- The owners of the copies that have reacted, oldest first (Reactor/Owned).
Particle._reacted = {}

-- record -> { at, blade }: a cutting Force's blade where the Force stands this frame.
local blades = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
-- One pass's scratch: where each live record stands and how far its shape reaches.
local origins = {}
local reaches = {}

local function unwatch(pData)
	local watched = Particle._watched
	local place = pData._watchIndex
	if not place or watched[place] ~= pData then
		return
	end
	local last = #watched
	local moved = watched[last]
	watched[place] = moved
	moved._watchIndex = place
	watched[last] = nil
	pData._watchIndex = nil
end

function Particle:_watchForForces(pData, settings, whole)
	if whole and settings.Break ~= "None" then
		settings = table.clone(settings)
		settings.Break = "None"
	end
	pData._reacts = settings
	pData._reactWhole = whole == true
	local visual = pData.VisualPart
	if visual and not whole then
		Shards.judge(visual)
	end
	-- Its own Hold, rolled once: asked again every frame, a roll would let it through in the end.
	pData._reactHold = settings.Hold * (1 + settings.HoldSpread * (math.random() * 2 - 1))
	local watched = self._watched
	pData._watchIndex = #watched + 1
	watched[pData._watchIndex] = pData
	pData._onReclaim = unwatch
end

local function cutBy(record, visual, position, radius, age)
	if not Reach.inBlade(record, position, radius, age) then
		return false
	end
	local origin = record.field.origin
	local kept = blades[record]
	if not kept then
		kept = {}
		blades[record] = kept
	end
	if kept.at ~= origin then
		kept.at = origin
		kept.blade = Blade.of(record.field, record.cut)
	end
	return kept.blade ~= nil and Blade.touches(kept.blade, visual.ExtentsCFrame, visual.ExtentsSize)
end

-- The first of the `live` records that reaches a watched play, or nil. The copy is read only
-- for a record of its Group, and the record's shape only inside a ball round it.
local function reachedBy(pData, visual, records, live, now)
	local group = pData._reacts.Group
	local position, extent, radius = nil, nil, 0
	for place = 1, live do
		local record = records[place]
		if Index.groupMatches(record.group, group) then
			if not position then
				position = visual.CFrame.Position
				extent = visual.Size
				radius = extent.Magnitude / 2
			end
			if (position - origins[place]).Magnitude <= radius + reaches[place] then
				local age = now - pData.StartTime
				if Reach.moved(record, position, extent, pData._reactHold, age) then
					return record
				end
				if record.cut and not pData._reactWhole and cutBy(record, visual, position, radius, age) then
					return record
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return nil
end

-- Ends an owner at once, from outside: what waits for its cut is dropped, its entry discarded.
local function release(self, owner)
	Entries.forget(self._reactorCutting[owner.copy])
	if owner.entry and self._reactorPlays[owner.copy] == owner.entry then
		Entries.discard(self, owner.entry)
	end
	Owned.gone(self, owner, false)
end

local function piecesOf(owner)
	local entry = owner.entry
	if entry then
		return math.max(entry.play.awake, 1)
	end
	return 1
end

-- Sends an owner away for the cap: one that lies where it fell sinks there and is then gone
-- by itself; one still in flight, or still being cut, goes at once.
local function leave(self, owner)
	owner.leaving = true
	local entry = owner.entry
	if not entry or entry.pData or entry.play.phase ~= "live" then
		release(self, owner)
		return
	end
	local settings = entry.play.settings
	settings.After = "Fade"
	settings.AfterDelay = 0
	settings.AfterTime = LEAVE_SECONDS
	entry.play.idleFor = 0
	if not Entries.resume(self, entry) then
		release(self, owner)
	end
end

-- Keeps the reacted pieces of the newest owner's item within its Max Pieces: the oldest go.
local function keepWithin(self, newest)
	local source = newest.source
	local most = math.max(newest.settings.MaxPieces, 1)
	local reacted = self._reacted
	local out = 0
	for _, owner in ipairs(reacted) do
		if owner.source == source and not owner.leaving then
			out += piecesOf(owner)
		end
	end
	local place = 1
	while out > most and place <= #reacted do
		local owner = reacted[place]
		if owner ~= newest and owner.source == source and not owner.leaving then
			out -= piecesOf(owner)
			leave(self, owner)
		end
		-- An owner that went at once has left the list: the next one stands in its place.
		if reacted[place] == owner then
			place += 1
		end
	end
end

local function handOver(self, pData, record, now)
	local copy = pData.VisualPart
	local emits = self.ActiveEmits
	local listed = table.find(emits, pData)
	unwatch(pData)
	if not listed then
		return
	end
	local velocity = Momentum.of(self, pData, now)
	-- The play leaves the engine's list without dying: its owner keeps it and ends it.
	local last = #emits
	emits[listed] = emits[last]
	emits[last] = nil
	pData._onReclaim = nil
	pData._handedOver = true
	pData._noPool = true

	local token = pData._playToken
	local owner = {
		copy = copy,
		particle = pData,
		source = pData._sourceItem,
		settings = pData._reacts,
		velocity = velocity,
		whole = pData._reactWhole,
		context = token and { _playToken = token } or nil,
	}
	table.insert(self._reacted, owner)
	keepWithin(self, owner)

	-- A Matte's shape is never cut: its entry is made without the Force's blade.
	local asking = record
	if owner.whole then
		asking = nil
	end
	local entry, cutting = Entries.entryFor(self, copy, nil, asking, owner)
	if cutting then
		Entries.owe(cutting, record)
		return
	end
	if not entry then
		release(self, owner)
		return
	end
	-- The Force that reached the copy is given to its entry with the rest of this frame's
	-- pass (Reactor/init's _tellEntry): an Impulse strikes, a later blade cuts before it kicks.
	self:_tellEntry(entry, record, true)
end

-- One frame's pass over the watched plays (Reactor/Batch.pass runs it).
-- Backwards: a play handed over leaves the list, and the last one takes its place.
local function handOverAll(self, watched, count, records, live, now)
	for place = count, 1, -1 do
		local pData = watched[place]
		local visual = pData.VisualPart
		if visual and visual.Parent then
			local record = reachedBy(pData, visual, records, live, now)
			if record then
				handOver(self, pData, record, now)
			end
		end
	end
end

function Particle:_handOverReached(now)
	local watched = self._watched
	local count = #watched
	if count == 0 then
		return
	end
	local records = ForceRegistry.list()
	local live = #records
	if live == 0 then
		return
	end
	for place = 1, live do
		local field = records[place].field
		origins[place] = field.origin.Position
		reaches[place] = Index.reachOf(field)
	end
	Batch.pass(handOverAll, self, watched, count, records, live, now)
end

-- Whether a Force could reach a piece of an owned entry that is still there: a ball round the
-- piece against a ball round the Force's shape.
local function couldReach(record, entry)
	local play = entry.play
	local field = record.field
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] ~= Play.GONE and Index.reaches(field, play:_position(index), piece.reach) then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

function Particle:_followReacted(record)
	local reacted = self._reacted
	for place = #reacted, 1, -1 do
		local owner = reacted[place]
		local entry = owner.entry
		if not owner.copy.Parent then
			release(self, owner)
		elseif entry and not owner.leaving and Index.groupMatches(record.group, entry.group) and couldReach(record, entry) then
			self:_tellEntry(entry, record, false)
		end
	end
end

function Particle:_endReacted(item, token)
	local reacted = self._reacted
	for place = #reacted, 1, -1 do
		local owner = reacted[place]
		if owner and ((item ~= nil and owner.source == item) or (token ~= nil and owner.particle._playToken == token)) then
			release(self, owner)
		end
	end
end

end

--[[
	Index  -  which Reactors a Force could reach. A Reactor is found by its tag (set by
	TransformReactor), so nothing is scanned: a place with no Reactors costs one empty list.
	Index.reaches is a first, generous test (a ball around the Reactor against a ball around
	the Force's shape); Reactor/Play decides piece by piece.
	Index.unmark makes a copy of a Reactor an ordinary instance again (Reactor/Display's
	stand-ins, the plugin's Modules/Scatter).

local CollectionService = game:GetService("CollectionService")

local Index = {}

Index.TAG = "PartIcleReactor"
-- The item attributes TransformReactor (Reactor/init.luau) stamps; one added there is added here.
Index.MARKS = { "Transformed", "Qwinkle", "IsReactor", "IsEmitter", "EmitCount", "EmitDuration", "EmitDelay", "EmissionMode", "AnimateLoop" }

-- Every tagged Reactor that is in the world right now.
function Index.reactors()
	local found = {}
	for _, reactor in ipairs(CollectionService:GetTagged(Index.TAG)) do
		if reactor:IsDescendantOf(workspace) and not reactor:GetAttribute("_PartIcleEmit") then
			table.insert(found, reactor)
		end
	end
	return found
end

-- The farthest any point of a field's shape is from its origin.
function Index.reachOf(field)
	if field.shape == "Linear" then
		return math.sqrt(field.range * field.range + field.halfWidth * field.halfWidth + field.halfHeight * field.halfHeight)
	elseif field.shape == "Vortex" then
		return math.sqrt(field.range * field.range + field.height * field.height)
	end
	return field.range
end

function Index.reaches(field, centre, radius)
	return (centre - field.origin.Position).Magnitude <= radius + Index.reachOf(field)
end

-- Takes a Reactor's attributes and tag off a COPY of one. Never called on the Reactor itself.
function Index.unmark(copy)
	for _, mark in ipairs(Index.MARKS) do
		copy:SetAttribute(mark, nil)
	end
	copy:RemoveTag(Index.TAG)
end

-- A Force's Group reaches a Reactor when it is empty or the same.
function Index.groupMatches(forceGroup, reactorGroup)
	return forceGroup == "" or forceGroup == reactorGroup
end

return Index

--[[
	LayerCuts: the engine's cut of a patch of a stacked ground (Reactor/Layers). Every layer is cut
	around the same points and the fragments of one point are joined into one shard. Called by
	Reactor/Shards, which passes `fragment` (the engine's cut of one part around world points, or nil)
	and `shardOf` (a fragment as a shard record).

	A patch's template is first cut into layer slabs (a plane a border), so every slab has the patch's
	own frame, the frame a cut's points are given in. The layers' cuts of one step are asked of the
	engine at once. Yields wherever the engine cuts; mutates nothing of the place.

	LayerCuts.cut(job, whole, frame, points, split) -> shards | false
	  For a job with more than one share (job.layers): `whole` the patch's template, `frame` its frame,
	  `points` the cut's world points, `split` Sites.cracks' crust and base points or nil. A shard of
	  several layers has `parts`: for each fragment { template, layer, standOffset, offset, size }, the
	  last two its box in the shard's. Every shard has `layer`, that of its first fragment. The base
	  under the crust is one shard of every layer's share of it.
	LayerCuts.carve(job, frame, carve) -> shards | false
	  A blade through such a patch: each layer is carved by itself (Reactor/Carve.cut, passed in).
	LayerCuts.cutAgain(job) -> shards | false
	  Reactor/Shards.recut for a piece of several fragments (job.layered): each is cut around the
	  job's points and the results joined by point again.
	LayerCuts.stamp(shards, share)   marks the shards of a patch that lies in one layer
	LayerCuts.use(fragment, shardOf, clip)   gives the Reactor/Shards functions once. clip(template,
	  part, into) is what of the template's box lies inside a part, `into` taking the part to where the
	  template stands (job.place is where the patch stands). A skin's share (share.skin) is its slab
	  clipped to the skin; a patch the skin does not reach has no such layer.
]]

local AXES = { "X", "Y", "Z" }
-- A share's offset shorter than this along an axis is none.
local THIN = 0.01

local LayerCuts = {}

local fragment = nil
local shardOf = nil
local clip = nil

function LayerCuts.use(fragmentOf, shardFrom, clipTo)
	fragment = fragmentOf
	shardOf = shardFrom
	clip = clipTo
end

local function along(axis, value)
	if axis == "X" then
		return Vector3.new(value, 0, 0)
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return Vector3.new(0, value, 0)
	end
	return Vector3.new(0, 0, value)
end

function LayerCuts.stamp(shards, share)
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
		shard.layer = share.index
	end
end

-- The fragments of one point as one shard. Fragments keep the patch template's frame, so their
-- boxes lie along `frame`'s axes.
local function joined(frame, group, fixed, siteIndex)
	local first = group[1]
	if #group == 1 then
		local shard = shardOf(first.instance, frame, fixed, siteIndex)
		shard.layer = first.layer
		return shard
	end
	local low, high = nil, nil
	for _, member in ipairs(group) do
		local middle = frame:PointToObjectSpace(member.instance.ExtentsCFrame.Position)
		local half = member.instance.ExtentsSize / 2
		local from = middle - half
		local to = middle + half
		if low then
			low = Vector3.new(math.min(low.X, from.X), math.min(low.Y, from.Y), math.min(low.Z, from.Z))
			high = Vector3.new(math.max(high.X, to.X), math.max(high.Y, to.Y), math.max(high.Z, to.Z))
		else
			low, high = from, to
		end
	end
	local box = CFrame.new((low + high) / 2)
	local world = frame * box
	local parts = table.create(#group)
	for position, member in ipairs(group) do
		local template = member.instance
		parts[position] = {
			template = template,
			layer = member.layer,
			standOffset = world:ToObjectSpace(template.CFrame),
			offset = world:ToObjectSpace(template.ExtentsCFrame),
			size = template.ExtentsSize,
		}
	end
	return {
		template = first.instance,
		box = box,
		size = high - low,
		standOffset = parts[1].standOffset,
		fixed = fixed,
		siteIndex = siteIndex,
		layer = first.layer,
		parts = parts,
	}
end

local function gather(bySite, order, entries, layer)
	for _, entry in ipairs(entries) do
		local group = bySite[entry.Index]
		if not group then
			group = {}
			bySite[entry.Index] = group
			table.insert(order, entry.Index)
		end
		table.insert(group, { instance = entry.Instance, layer = layer })
	end
end

local function destroyGroups(bySite, bases)
	for _, group in pairs(bySite) do
		for _, member in ipairs(group) do
			member.instance:Destroy()
		end
	end
	for _, member in ipairs(bases or {}) do
		member.instance:Destroy()
	end
end

-- Shards of the points that gave any, in the points' order, or false for fewer than two.
local function shardsOf(frame, bySite, order, bases)
	if #order < 2 then
		destroyGroups(bySite, bases)
		return false
	end
	table.sort(order)
	local shards = table.create(#order + 1)
	for _, site in ipairs(order) do
		table.insert(shards, joined(frame, bySite[site], false, site))
	end
	if bases and #bases > 0 then
		table.insert(shards, joined(frame, bases, true, nil))
	end
	return shards
end

-- The stack's axis in the patch: the one its shares are offset along.
local function axisOf(shares)
	local offset = shares[2].offset - shares[1].offset
	for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
		if math.abs(offset[axis]) > THIN then
			return axis
		end
	end
	return "Y"
end

-- A patch's template cut into layer slabs in the shares' order (a plane a border, by two points a
-- stud either side). An entry is false where the engine gave none; nil when it would not cut. Yields.
local function slabsOf(whole, frame, shares, place)
	local axis = axisOf(shares)
	local slabs = table.create(#shares, false)
	local rest = whole
	for position = 1, #shares - 1 do
		local share = shares[position]
		local border = share.offset[axis] + share.size[axis] / 2
		local halves = fragment(rest, {
			frame:PointToWorldSpace(along(axis, border - 1)),
			frame:PointToWorldSpace(along(axis, border + 1)),
		})
		if rest ~= whole then
			rest:Destroy()
		end
		rest = nil
		if not halves then
			for _, slab in ipairs(slabs) do
				if slab then
					slab:Destroy()
				end
			end
			return nil
		end
		for _, entry in ipairs(halves) do
			-- White, as every cut source is: a blade's cut keeps the slab's colour in its geometry.
			entry.Instance.Color = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
			if entry.Index == 1 then
				slabs[position] = entry.Instance
			else
				rest = entry.Instance
			end
		end
		if not rest then
			break
		end
	end
	if rest then
		slabs[#shares] = rest
	end
	-- A skin's slab is the template's box cut to the skin, white and in the patch's frame. The template
	-- may stand elsewhere (job.place): the skin is taken to it.
	local into = place and frame * place:Inverse() or nil
	for position, share in ipairs(shares) do
		local slab = slabs[position]
		if slab and share.skin then
			slabs[position] = clip(whole, share.skin, into) or false
			slab:Destroy()
		end
	end
	return slabs
end

-- The engine's cut of several sources at once around the same points, in the sources' order; false
-- where a source is none or gave nothing. Yields until the last is in.
local function together(sources, points)
	local results = table.create(#sources, false)
	local waiting = coroutine.running()
	local pending = #sources
	local parked = false
	for position, source in ipairs(sources) do
		task.spawn(function()
			if source then
				results[position] = fragment(source, points) or false
			end
			pending -= 1
			if pending == 0 and parked then
				task.spawn(waiting)
			end
		end)
	end
	if pending > 0 then
		parked = true
		coroutine.yield()
	end
	return results
end

function LayerCuts.cut(job, whole, frame, points, split)
	local shares = job.layers
	local slabs = slabsOf(whole, frame, shares, job.place)
	if not slabs then
		return false
	end
	local crustPoint, basePoint = nil, nil
	if split then
		crustPoint = frame:PointToWorldSpace(split.inCrust)
		basePoint = frame:PointToWorldSpace(split.inBase)
	end
	local bySite, order, bases = {}, {}, {}
	-- The crust off its base in every layer: a layer may be all of one or the other.
	local crusts = slabs
	if split then
		local halves = together(slabs, { crustPoint, basePoint })
		crusts = table.create(#shares, false)
		for position, share in ipairs(shares) do
			local slab = slabs[position]
			local halved = halves[position]
			if halved then
				for _, entry in ipairs(halved) do
					if entry.Index == 1 then
						crusts[position] = entry.Instance
					else
						table.insert(bases, { instance = entry.Instance, layer = share.index })
					end
				end
				slab:Destroy()
			else
				crusts[position] = slab
			end
		end
	end
	local rings = together(crusts, points)
	for position, share in ipairs(shares) do
		local crust = crusts[position]
		local fragments = rings[position]
		if fragments and #fragments > 0 then
			gather(bySite, order, fragments, share.index)
			crust:Destroy()
		elseif crust then
			-- No cut of this layer's crust: it stands with the base.
			table.insert(bases, { instance = crust, layer = share.index })
		end
	end
	return shardsOf(frame, bySite, order, bases)
end

function LayerCuts.carve(job, frame, carve)
	local shares = job.layers
	local slabs = slabsOf(job.part, frame, shares, job.place)
	if not slabs then
		return false
	end
	local shards = {}
	for position, share in ipairs(shares) do
		local slab = slabs[position]
		if slab then
			local own = table.clone(job)
			own.template = slab
			own.frame = frame
			own.layers = nil
			local carved = carve(own, fragment, shardOf)
			if carved then
				for _, shard in ipairs(carved) do
					shard.layer = share.index
					table.insert(shards, shard)
				end
				slab:Destroy()
			else
				-- The engine would not carve this layer: its slab stands.
				local shard = shardOf(slab, frame, true, nil)
				shard.layer = share.index
				table.insert(shards, shard)
			end
		end
	end
	if #shards == 0 then
		return false
	end
	shards.slash = job.slash
	return shards
end

function LayerCuts.cutAgain(job)
	local frame = job.template.CFrame
	local points = table.create(#job.points)
	for index, offset in ipairs(job.points) do
		points[index] = frame:PointToWorldSpace(offset)
	end
	local templates = table.create(#job.layered)
	for position, part in ipairs(job.layered) do
		templates[position] = part.shard
	end
	local cuts = together(templates, points)
	local bySite, order = {}, {}
	for position, part in ipairs(job.layered) do
		if cuts[position] then
			gather(bySite, order, cuts[position], part.layer)
		end
	end
	return shardsOf(frame, bySite, order, nil)
end

return LayerCuts

--[[
	Layers: plain blocks of a Reactor that lie on each other crack as ONE ground (a grass slab on
	the earth under it). Every piece is all that lies nearest one point of the crack: a fragment of
	each layer the point's cell passes through, moved as one piece.

	The engine cuts a part by the cells of all the points given, outside points included, so each
	layer is cut around the same points and the fragments of one point (told by Index) form one
	piece. A patch's template is first cut into layer slabs (a plane a border); a fragment keeps the
	CFrame of what it was cut from, so every slab has the patch's own frame.

	A stacked ground is { part, frame, size, axis, layers }: frame and size are the box around all
	layers in the first block's turn; axis is the box axis the layers lie along; layers, in order
	along it, are { part, low, high, aligned, slice }: low and high from the box's middle, aligned
	when the part is turned as the box is (a Texture is carried from such a part alone), slice the
	layer's share as a ground of its own for Reactor/GroundDisplay ({ part, frame, size, plain }).
	Stacked means one footprint, face on face, turned alike but for quarter turns. Blocks that only
	overlap in part crack each on its own.

	A skin is a thin non-block part (mesh, union: grass over a baseplate) lying flush on an end of a
	block or stack. Its layer has `skin = true`; the ground keeps the blocks' footprint, so what
	overhangs is never opened. A skin's share of a patch is what the engine finds of it inside that
	share (Reactor/LayerCuts); intact skin is drawn by Reactor/SkinDisplay.

	Layers.grounds(parts, others) -> grounds, skins
	  The Reactor's plain blocks as grounds: a block in no stack and under no skin is
	  { part, frame, size }. others: parts that may be skins, or nil; skins: those that are, as a set.
	Layers.inPatch(ground, centre, size) -> shares
	  The layers' shares of a patch box (centre, size in the ground's space):
	  { { index, offset, size, skin } }, offset from the patch middle, skin the part when a skin.
	Layers.clip(ground, layer, rectangles, face) -> rectangles
	  Rectangles of the ground's face `face` as rectangles of that layer's slice.
	The cut itself is Reactor/LayerCuts. Maths only: reads each part's CFrame and Size.
]]

local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)

-- Two faces this near lie on each other; two lengths this near are the same.
local FLUSH = 0.05
-- An axis counts as another's when it lies along it this nearly (about a degree).
local SQUARE = 0.9998
-- A share of a patch thinner than this is none.
local THIN = 0.01
-- Stacks are looked for among this many blocks at most: every pair is tried.
local MOST_BLOCKS = 400
-- A skin is no thicker than this share of its narrower side and covers at least this share of its face.
local SKIN_THIN = 0.2
local SKIN_COVER = 0.25
local AXES = { "X", "Y", "Z" }

local Layers = {}

local function along(axis, value)
	if axis == "X" then
		return Vector3.new(value, 0, 0)
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return Vector3.new(0, value, 0)
	end
	return Vector3.new(0, 0, value)
end

local function withAxis(vector, axis, value)
	if axis == "X" then
		return Vector3.new(value, vector.Y, vector.Z)
	elseif axis == "Y" then
		return Vector3.new(vector.X, value, vector.Z)
	end
	return Vector3.new(vector.X, vector.Y, value)
end

-- Size of a block along another's axes when its axes match in some order (`relative` is its frame
-- in the other's space); nil when turned otherwise.
local function sizeAlong(relative, size)
	local turned = { relative.XVector, relative.YVector, relative.ZVector }
	local lengths = {}
	for position, vector in ipairs(turned) do
		local found = nil
		for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
			if math.abs(vector[axis]) >= SQUARE then
				found = axis
			end
		end
		if not found or lengths[found] then
			return nil
		end
		lengths[found] = size[AXES[position]]
	end
	return Vector3.new(lengths.X, lengths.Y, lengths.Z)
end

-- Blocks on `root`'s line along one of its axes with its footprint, by axis:
-- { part, low, high, aligned }, low and high from root's middle.
local function inLine(root, parts, taken)
	local byAxis = {}
	local frame = root.CFrame
	local own = root.Size
	for _, other in ipairs(parts) do
		if other ~= root and not taken[other] then
			local relative = frame:ToObjectSpace(other.CFrame)
			local offset = relative.Position
			local axis = nil
			local apart = 0
			for _, name in ipairs(AXES) do
				if math.abs(offset[name]) > FLUSH then
					axis = name
					apart += 1
				end
			end
			local size = apart == 1 and sizeAlong(relative, other.Size)
			if size then
				local same = true
				for _, name in ipairs(AXES) do
					if name ~= axis and math.abs(own[name] - size[name]) > FLUSH then
						same = false
					end
				end
				if same then
					local list = byAxis[axis]
					if not list then
						list = {}
						byAxis[axis] = list
					end
					table.insert(list, {
						part = other,
						low = offset[axis] - size[axis] / 2,
						high = offset[axis] + size[axis] / 2,
						aligned = relative.XVector.X >= SQUARE and relative.YVector.Y >= SQUARE and relative.ZVector.Z >= SQUARE,
					})
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return byAxis
end

-- The stack through `root` along one axis: candidates face on face with what is stacked so far.
-- Returns members in order and the ends, or nil.
local function stackOf(root, axis, candidates)
	local half = root.Size[axis] / 2
	local members = { { part = root, low = -half, high = half, aligned = true } }
	local low, high = -half, half
	local grew = true
	while grew do
		grew = false
		for position = #candidates, 1, -1 do
			local candidate = candidates[position]
			if math.abs(candidate.low - high) <= FLUSH then
				high = candidate.high
				table.insert(members, candidate)
				table.remove(candidates, position)
				grew = true
			elseif math.abs(candidate.high - low) <= FLUSH then
				low = candidate.low
				table.insert(members, candidate)
				table.remove(candidates, position)
				grew = true
			end
		end
	end
	if #members < 2 then
		return nil
	end
	table.sort(members, function(first, second)
		return first.low < second.low
	end)
	return members, low, high
end

-- A part of `others` lying on an end of the stack as its skin: { part, low, high, aligned, skin }, or nil.
local function skinOn(root, axis, low, high, others, taken)
	local frame = root.CFrame
	local own = root.Size
	for _, other in ipairs(others) do
		if not taken[other] then
			local relative = frame:ToObjectSpace(other.CFrame)
			local size = sizeAlong(relative, other.Size)
			if size then
				local offset = relative.Position
				local from = offset[axis] - size[axis] / 2
				local to = offset[axis] + size[axis] / 2
				if math.abs(from - high) <= FLUSH or math.abs(to - low) <= FLUSH then
					local cover = 1
					local narrow = math.huge
					for _, name in ipairs(AXES) do
						if name ~= axis then
							local shared = math.min(offset[name] + size[name] / 2, own[name] / 2) - math.max(offset[name] - size[name] / 2, -own[name] / 2)
							cover *= math.max(shared, 0) / own[name]
							narrow = math.min(narrow, size[name])
						end
					end
					if cover >= SKIN_COVER and size[axis] <= narrow * SKIN_THIN then
						return { part = other, low = from, high = to, aligned = false, skin = true }
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return nil
end

local function stacked(root, axis, members, low, high)
	local middle = (low + high) / 2
	local frame = root.CFrame * CFrame.new(along(axis, middle))
	local size = withAxis(root.Size, axis, high - low)
	local layers = table.create(#members)
	for position, member in ipairs(members) do
		local from = member.low - middle
		local to = member.high - middle
		layers[position] = {
			part = member.part,
			low = from,
			high = to,
			aligned = member.aligned,
			skin = member.skin,
			slice = {
				part = member.part,
				frame = frame * CFrame.new(along(axis, (from + to) / 2)),
				size = withAxis(size, axis, to - from),
				plain = not member.aligned,
			},
		}
	end
	return { part = root, frame = frame, size = size, axis = axis, layers = layers }
end

-- Adds the skin lying on the stack, if any; returns the stack's ends with it.
local function withSkin(root, axis, members, low, high, others, skins)
	local skin = skinOn(root, axis, low, high, others, skins)
	if not skin then
		return false, low, high
	end
	skins[skin.part] = true
	table.insert(members, skin)
	table.sort(members, function(first, second)
		return first.low < second.low
	end)
	return true, math.min(low, skin.low), math.max(high, skin.high)
end

function Layers.grounds(parts, others)
	local grounds = table.create(#parts)
	local taken = {}
	local skins = {}
	local looks = #parts > 1 and #parts <= MOST_BLOCKS
	local skinned = others ~= nil and #others > 0 and #parts <= MOST_BLOCKS
	for _, root in ipairs(parts) do
		if not taken[root] then
			taken[root] = true
			local ground = nil
			if looks then
				local byAxis = inLine(root, parts, taken)
				for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
					local candidates = byAxis[axis]
					if candidates and not ground then
						local members, low, high = stackOf(root, axis, candidates)
						if members then
							for _, member in ipairs(members) do
								taken[member.part] = true
							end
							if skinned then
								local _
								_, low, high = withSkin(root, axis, members, low, high, others, skins)
							end
							ground = stacked(root, axis, members, low, high)
						end
					end
				end
			end
			-- A lone block may still lie under a skin along any of its axes.
			if not ground and skinned then
				for _, axis in ipairs(AXES) do
					if not ground then
						local half = root.Size[axis] / 2
						local members = { { part = root, low = -half, high = half, aligned = true } }
						local found, low, high = withSkin(root, axis, members, -half, half, others, skins)
						if found then
							ground = stacked(root, axis, members, low, high)
						end
					end
				end
			end
			table.insert(grounds, ground or { part = root, frame = root.CFrame, size = root.Size })
		end
	end
	return grounds, skins
end

function Layers.inPatch(ground, centre, size)
	local axis = ground.axis
	local low = centre[axis] - size[axis] / 2
	local high = centre[axis] + size[axis] / 2
	local shares = {}
	for index, layer in ipairs(ground.layers) do
		local from = math.max(low, layer.low)
		local to = math.min(high, layer.high)
		if to - from > THIN then
			table.insert(shares, {
				index = index,
				offset = along(axis, (from + to) / 2 - centre[axis]),
				size = withAxis(size, axis, to - from),
				skin = layer.skin and layer.part or nil,
			})
		end
	end
	return shares
end

function Layers.clip(ground, layer, rectangles, face)
	if face.axis == ground.axis then
		return rectangles
	end
	local uAxis = Sites.faceAxes(face.axis)
	local middle = (layer.low + layer.high) / 2
	local clipped = {}
	for _, rectangle in ipairs(rectangles) do
		local minU, minV, maxU, maxV = rectangle.minU, rectangle.minV, rectangle.maxU, rectangle.maxV
		if uAxis == ground.axis then
			minU = math.max(minU, layer.low) - middle
			maxU = math.min(maxU, layer.high) - middle
		else
			minV = math.max(minV, layer.low) - middle
			maxV = math.min(maxV, layer.high) - middle
		end
		if maxU - minU > THIN and maxV - minV > THIN then
			table.insert(clipped, { minU = minU, minV = minV, maxU = maxU, maxV = maxV })
		end
	end
	return clipped
end

return Layers

--[[
	Momentum: the velocity a mesh part-icle's own motion gives its copy at this moment, for the moment
	the copy is handed to the Reactor code (Reactor/HandOver).

	A play moves its copy in keyframe steps and keeps no velocity (its motion is Speed along a direction,
	Acceleration, Drag, Displacement graphs, a Timescale), so the velocity is measured with the play's own
	update. One step tells how fast the play's time runs against real time. The play is then set exactly
	on its keyframe and stepped exactly one keyframe on: the way its copy goes over the real time that
	keyframe stands for is its velocity. The copy is put back where it stood.

	Momentum.of(particle, pData, now) -> Vector3, studs per second of real time
	  particle: the engine, whose UpdatePart is called. Zero for a play whose time stands still, is at
	  the end of its life, or was stopped by a collision.
	Mutates: the play (stepped on, its clock set on a keyframe) and its copy's look (up to two steps of
	its graphs); the copy's CFrame is as it was afterwards. Only for a play whose own motion ends here.
	Cross-file: reads and writes what UpdatePart keeps (Update.luau): _effectiveElapsed, AccumulatedDT,
	CurrentStep and _lastEffectiveDt. A keyframe that starts and ends on a keyframe is the one stretch
	both of UpdatePart's ways of moving agree on (closed forms move by keyframes, loops by gathered
	time). _postUpdateCF (Engine.luau) is the last keyframe's pose without the later overlays (Orientation, Z-Offset).
]]

local Momentum = {}

local ZERO = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)
local TINY = 1e-6
-- How far past a keyframe the measuring step ends, as a share of it: on the keyframe itself a
-- rounding could leave the play one short.
local PAST = 1e-6

function Momentum.of(particle, pData, now)
	local visual = pData.VisualPart
	local shown = visual.CFrame
	local keyframeSeconds = pData.LifeTime / math.max(pData.TotalKeyFrames, 1)
	local velocity = ZERO

	local step = pData.CurrentStep
	particle:UpdatePart(pData, keyframeSeconds, now)
	local timescale = (pData._lastEffectiveDt or 0) / keyframeSeconds
	if math.abs(timescale) > TINY then
		local from = visual.CFrame.Position
		if pData.CurrentStep == step then
			from = (pData._postUpdateCF or shown).Position
		end
		-- A play in reverse steps back: floor() needs the step to end short of the keyframe.
		local direction = math.sign(timescale)
		step = pData.CurrentStep
		pData._effectiveElapsed = step * keyframeSeconds
		pData.AccumulatedDT = 0
		local wanted = direction * keyframeSeconds * (1 + direction * PAST)
		particle:UpdatePart(pData, wanted / timescale, now)
		local took = pData._lastEffectiveDt or 0
		if pData.CurrentStep ~= step and math.abs(took) > TINY then
			velocity = (visual.CFrame.Position - from) * (timescale / took)
		end
	end
	visual.CFrame = shown
	return velocity
end

return Momentum

	made: the emitted copy of a mesh part-icle that a Force has reached (Reactor/HandOver). Such an
	entry has an owner:
	  { copy, particle, source, settings, velocity, whole, context, entry, leaving, released }
	  copy       the emitted copy: the entry's reactor. The runtime's own; never pooled again.
	  particle   the copy's own play (its pData): off the engine's list since the hand-over,
	             and ended here when the owner is gone
	  source     the transformed item the copy was emitted from
	  settings   the Reactor settings read from that item's config at the emit
	  velocity   the copy's own velocity at the hand-over
	  whole      true for a copy that is never cut (a Matte's shape: a window, not a thing)
	  context    what the entry's play is registered with: the part-icle's own play token
	  entry      nil while the engine cuts the copy
	  leaving    true once the cap has sent it away (Reactor/HandOver)

	A piece that is a whole part of the copy is marked own: Reactor/Display then moves that part
	itself, so what is linked to the copy goes along (nested part-icles, emitters, trails, a Matte's
	twin). A copy in pieces is hidden where it was reached and what drew on it is switched off.
	Nothing carries a copy, so when its entry is made every piece is let go at the copy's own
	velocity; what a Force throws is thrown on top.

	Owned.mark(pieces, owner)        before the play is made: own pieces, none fixed
	Owned.adopt(entry, owner)        when the entry is made (Reactor/Entries): ties the two,
	                                 and lets every piece go
	Owned.spent(entry) -> boolean    an owned entry whose play has nothing left to show
	Owned.gone(self, owner, natural)

	    engine's helpers. natural = true fires OnDeath and OnDestruction, as for a play that
	    ends by itself; a stop from outside (Disable, Stop Emits, Deactivate) passes false.
	    Harmless with no owner, and when called again.
	Mutates: the copy (a CLONE its own play made), never anything of the user's.
	Cross-file: Particle._reacted (Reactor/HandOver) lists the owners; gone takes one out.
	Reactor/Recarve leaves a piece marked uncut alone.

local Display = require(script.Parent.Display)

local Owned = {}

function Owned.mark(pieces, owner)
	for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		if not piece.shard and not piece.blockSize then
			piece.own = true
		end
		piece.fixed = nil
		piece.partStands = nil
		if owner.whole then
			piece.uncut = true
		end
	end
end

function Owned.adopt(entry, owner)
	entry.owner = owner
	owner.entry = entry
	local play = entry.play
	local pieces = play.pieces
	-- Every piece goes at once: there is nothing to hold another up.
	play.settings.Collapse = false
	local wholeCopy = #pieces == 1 and pieces[1].own == true and pieces[1].part == owner.copy
	if not wholeCopy then
		Display.quiet(owner.copy)
		local nested = owner.particle._nestedAlive
		if nested then
			nested[1] = false
		end
	end
	-- Play:place shows every piece now; a placed piece that is pushed flies at once.
	play:place()
	for index in ipairs(pieces) do
		play:_push(index, owner.velocity)
	end
	-- It was never stood up anywhere: a Return ends with the play restored and done.
	play.placed = false
end

function Owned.spent(entry)
	return entry.owner ~= nil and entry.play.awake <= 0
end

function Owned.gone(self, owner, natural)
	if not owner or owner.released then
		return
	end
	owner.released = true
	local listed = table.find(self._reacted, owner)
	if listed then
		table.remove(self._reacted, listed)
	end
	local particle = owner.particle
	local copy = owner.copy
	if natural then
		self:_fireOnDeath(particle)
		self:_fireOnDestruction(particle, copy)
	end
	self:_releaseOrDestroy(particle, copy)
	self:_reclaimPData(particle)
end

return Owned

--[[
	Patches  -  the engine's cut of the patches of a ground (Reactor/Wounds). A patch is a
	rectangle of a ground's face, through the ground, not a part of the place. Each is cut from a
	template, a plain block of the patch's size that is never put into the world, by the cut
	cracked ground always gets (Reactor/Shards: the crust off its base, the crust in rings
	around the hit).

	A shard's box is its place in the template's own space, so it does not matter where the
	template stands: Reactor/Wounds stands the pieces where the patch is.

	A whole square (job.whole) is the same cut every time for one size, Range and variant, so
	its shards are kept and the next such crack is answered at once. Kept shards are templates
	only: every wound copies its own stand-ins from them (Reactor/Display). The least recently
	used go when more than KEPT are held; a wound that still uses them holds on to them.

	Patches.cut(jobs, done)
	    jobs: { { size, hit, reach, count, seed, face, line, whole, variant }, ... }, or for a
	    rectangle a blade carves { size, count, seed, face, bladeFrame, bladeSize, slash, mode,
	    stands }, which Reactor/Shards hands to Reactor/Carve
	    (Reactor/Footprint.job: hit and line in the template's space, face = { axis, side }; a
	    job with a line is split along it, Reactor/Fissure). done(sets) is called when every
	    job is answered, sets[position] the shards of that job (Reactor/Shards) or false when
	    it asks for fewer than two pieces or the engine gave none. With every job kept, done is
	    called before cut returns; otherwise a few frames later.
	Patches.kept() -> how many cuts are held
	Patches.forget()  drops them all
]]

local Shards = require(script.Parent.Shards)

local KEPT = 12

local Patches = {}

local kept = {}
local held = 0
local uses = 0

local function keyOf(job)
	local size = job.size
	local key = string.format("%.2f,%.2f,%.2f|%d|%.2f|%s%d|%d", size.X, size.Y, size.Z, job.count, job.reach, job.face.axis, job.face.side, job.variant)
	for _, share in ipairs(job.layers or {}) do
		key ..= string.format("|%d:%.2f,%.2f,%.2f:%.2f,%.2f,%.2f", share.index, share.offset.X, share.offset.Y, share.offset.Z, share.size.X, share.size.Y, share.size.Z)
	end
	return key
end

local function remember(key, shards)
	uses += 1
	if not kept[key] then
		held += 1
	end
	kept[key] = { shards = shards, used = uses }
	while held > KEPT do
		local oldest, least = nil, math.huge
		for name, entry in pairs(kept) do
			if entry.used < least then
				oldest, least = name, entry.used
			end
		end
		kept[oldest] = nil
		held -= 1
	end
end

function Patches.cut(jobs, done)
	local sets = table.create(#jobs, false)
	local cuts = {}
	for position, job in ipairs(jobs) do
		local key = nil
		if job.whole then
			key = keyOf(job)
		end
		local known = key and kept[key]
		if known then
			uses += 1
			known.used = uses
			sets[position] = known.shards
		elseif job.count >= 2 then
			local template = Instance.new("Part")
			template.Anchored = true
			template.Size = job.size
			-- A kept cut is drawn from its variant alone, so every Force of that size gets it.
			local seed = job.seed
			if key then
				seed = (job.variant + 1) * 104729
			end
			table.insert(cuts, {
				part = template,
				key = Shards.key(template, job.count, seed, job.hit, job.reach, false),
				count = job.count,
				seed = seed,
				hit = job.hit,
				reach = job.reach,
				face = job.face,
				line = job.line,
				bladeFrame = job.bladeFrame,
				bladeSize = job.bladeSize,
				ribbon = job.ribbon,
				ribbonFrame = job.ribbonFrame,
				always = job.always,
				slash = job.slash,
				mode = job.mode,
				stands = job.stands,
				layers = job.layers,
				-- Where the patch stands in the world: a skin is cut where it lies (Reactor/LayerCuts).
				place = job.frame,
				loose = true,
				position = position,
				keep = key,
			})
		end
	end
	Shards.prepare(cuts, function()
		for _, cut in ipairs(cuts) do
			local shards = Shards.get(cut.part, cut.key) or false
			sets[cut.position] = shards
			if cut.keep and shards then
				remember(cut.keep, shards)
			end
			cut.part:Destroy()
		end
		done(sets)
	end)
end

function Patches.kept()
	return held
end

function Patches.forget()
	kept = {}
	held = 0
end

return Patches

--[[
	Pieces  -  the parts of a Reactor that can be pushed, as records for Reactor/Play:
	{ part, rest, halfExt, size, reach }, read each time a play starts. A shape lying off its part's
	CFrame (an engine union) rests where its shape is: standOffset and box say where.
	A Model has every BasePart under it, a one-part Reactor itself and the parts under it; a
	transformed item inside is skipped with everything under it.
	Break = "Blocks": a plain block is cut by arithmetic (Reactor/Dice.cut) into records with
	blockSize and shared siblings; any other part as shards on a grid. Each part has its own seed.
	Break = "Shards": a record per shard from shardsOf(part) (Reactor/Shards), its rest the shard's
	box in the world, with shard, standOffset, siblings, box, siteIndex and sites. Cracked ground:
	the base is fixed, the rest carry strike. A blade's cut: every record carries slash, a side or a
	bit mark (and `under`), and partStands when the part stays standing.
	  Pieces.parts(reactor), Pieces.isPlainBlock(part)
	  Pieces.ofShard(part, rest, shard, looks), Pieces.ofBlock(part, rest, size)
	  Pieces.ofSet(pieces, part, frame, shards, siblings, cut) -> siblings (cut: a ground's patch;
	      records touching its side are atEdge)
	  Pieces.touchesSide(box, halfExt, cut), Pieces.reachesFace(box, halfExt, cut)
	  Pieces.underTop(frame, size, piece), Pieces.collect(reactor, breakMode, pieceCount, shardsOf, leftOut)
	  Pieces.carry(pieces, own, origin, fullPose)   the records of a Reactor emitted elsewhere
]]

local Dice = require(script.Parent.Dice)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Fissure = require(script.Parent.Fissure)

local Pieces = {}

-- size: the edge of a cube of the volume (a Force's Size Response); reach: the longest edge.
local function record(part, rest, size)
	return {
		part = part,
		rest = rest,
		halfExt = size / 2,
		size = (size.X * size.Y * size.Z) ^ (1 / 3),
		reach = math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z),
	}
end

-- A shape this far off its part's CFrame is told apart from one around it.
local OFF_CENTRE = 0.01

-- A part that moves whole: its box is where its shape is, which for an engine union need not be
-- around its CFrame.
local function whole(part)
	local extents = part.ExtentsCFrame
	if (extents.Position - part.CFrame.Position).Magnitude < OFF_CENTRE then
		return record(part, part.CFrame, part.Size)
	end
	local piece = record(part, extents, part.ExtentsSize)
	piece.standOffset = extents:ToObjectSpace(part.CFrame)
	-- Reactor/Recarve cuts a whole part in its own space.
	piece.box = part.CFrame:ToObjectSpace(extents)
	return piece
end

-- A plain box: a Part whose Shape is Block and that carries no mesh of its own.
function Pieces.isPlainBlock(part)
	if part.ClassName ~= "Part" or part.Shape ~= Enum.PartType.Block then
		return false
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(part:GetChildren()) do
		if child:IsA("DataModelMesh") then
			return false
		end
	end
	return true
end

-- One whole block of a part at `rest` (drawn as a box in the part's look).
function Pieces.ofBlock(part, rest, size)
	local piece = record(part, rest, size)
	piece.blockSize = size
	return piece
end

-- looks: a stacked ground's layers; each fragment is drawn in its own layer's look.
function Pieces.ofShard(part, rest, shard, looks)
	local piece = record(part, rest, shard.size)
	piece.shard = shard.template
	piece.standOffset = shard.standOffset
	piece.box = shard.box
	piece.siteIndex = shard.siteIndex
	if looks and shard.layer then
		piece.looks = looks
		piece.part = looks[shard.layer].part
		piece.plain = not looks[shard.layer].aligned
		piece.skin = looks[shard.layer].skin
		if shard.parts then
			local layered = table.create(#shard.parts)
			for position, fragment in ipairs(shard.parts) do
				local look = looks[fragment.layer]
				layered[position] = {
					shard = fragment.template,
					layer = fragment.layer,
					part = look.part,
					plain = not look.aligned,
					skin = look.skin,
					standOffset = fragment.standOffset,
					offset = fragment.offset,
					halfExt = fragment.size / 2,
				}
			end
			piece.layered = layered
		end
	end
	return piece
end

-- A box this near a side of its patch meets it.
local EDGE_SLACK = 0.05

-- How far a box of half-lengths `half` at `frame` reaches up from its middle.
local function halfHeight(frame, half)
	return math.abs(frame.XVector.Y) * half.X + math.abs(frame.YVector.Y) * half.Y + math.abs(frame.ZVector.Y) * half.Z
end

function Pieces.touchesSide(box, halfExt, cut)
	local alongX = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(halfExt.X, 0, 0))
	local alongY = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(0, halfExt.Y, 0))
	local alongZ = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(0, 0, halfExt.Z))
	local uAxis, vAxis = Sites.faceAxes(cut.face.axis)
	for _, axis in ipairs({ uAxis, vAxis }) do
		local reach = math.abs(alongX[axis]) + math.abs(alongY[axis]) + math.abs(alongZ[axis])
		if math.abs(box.Position[axis]) + reach > cut.size[axis] / 2 - EDGE_SLACK then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

function Pieces.reachesFace(box, halfExt, cut)
	local axis = cut.face.axis
	local alongX = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(halfExt.X, 0, 0))
	local alongY = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(0, halfExt.Y, 0))
	local alongZ = box:VectorToWorldSpace(Vector3.new(0, 0, halfExt.Z))
	local reach = math.abs(alongX[axis]) + math.abs(alongY[axis]) + math.abs(alongZ[axis])
	return box.Position[axis] * cut.face.side + reach > cut.size[axis] / 2 - EDGE_SLACK
end

-- How far a piece's top lies under the top of the box it was cut from (its flight starts that much higher).
function Pieces.underTop(frame, size, piece)
	local top = frame.Position.Y + halfHeight(frame, size / 2)
	return math.max(top - piece.rest.Position.Y - halfHeight(piece.rest, piece.halfExt), 0)
end

function Pieces.ofSet(pieces, part, frame, shards, siblings, cut, looks)
	local strike = nil
	if shards.strike then
		strike = {
			origin = frame:PointToWorldSpace(shards.strike.origin),
			normal = frame:VectorToWorldSpace(shards.strike.normal),
			reach = shards.strike.reach,
			crust = shards.strike.crust,
		}
		-- A split's path (Reactor/Fissure), out of the cut's space into the world.
		if shards.strike.path then
			strike.path = Fissure.moved(shards.strike.path, frame, false)
		end
	end
	local slash = nil
	if shards.slash then
		slash = {
			origin = frame:PointToWorldSpace(shards.slash.origin),
			normal = frame:VectorToWorldSpace(shards.slash.normal),
			heading = frame:VectorToWorldSpace(shards.slash.heading),
			kerf = shards.slash.kerf,
		}
	end
	local partStands = nil
	if slash then
		for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
			if shard.fixed then
				partStands = true
			end
		end
	end
	siblings = siblings or table.create(#shards)
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
		local piece = Pieces.ofShard(part, frame * shard.box, shard, looks)
		piece.siblings = siblings
		piece.cut = cut
		piece.slash = slash
		piece.partStands = partStands
		piece.baked = shard.baked
		piece.side = shard.side
		piece.bit = shard.bit
		if shard.bit then
			local size = part.Size
			if cut then
				size = cut.size
			end
			piece.under = Pieces.underTop(frame, size, piece)
		end
		if shard.fixed then
			piece.fixed = true
			-- What a blade left of a ground's patch is the ground's surface there.
			if slash and cut and Pieces.reachesFace(shard.box, piece.halfExt, cut) then
				piece.atFace = true
			end
		else
			piece.strike = strike
			piece.sites = shards.sites
			if cut and Pieces.touchesSide(shard.box, piece.halfExt, cut) then
				piece.atEdge = true
			end
			if cut and Pieces.reachesFace(shard.box, piece.halfExt, cut) then
				piece.atFace = true
			end
		end
		table.insert(pieces, piece)
		table.insert(siblings, #pieces)
	end
	return siblings
end

-- One record per shard of a part, or false when the caller has none for it.
local function addShards(pieces, part, shardsOf)
	local shards = shardsOf and shardsOf(part) or nil
	if not shards or #shards == 0 or (#shards < 2 and not shards.slash) then
		return false
	end
	Pieces.ofSet(pieces, part, part.CFrame, shards)
	return true
end

local function add(pieces, part, breakMode, pieceCount, shardsOf)
	local plainBlock = breakMode == "Blocks" and Pieces.isPlainBlock(part)
	-- What the engine cut stands in for the part, whatever the Break.
	if addShards(pieces, part, shardsOf) then
		return
	end
	if not plainBlock then
		table.insert(pieces, whole(part))
		return
	end
	local blocks = Dice.cut(part.Size, Sites.count(part.Size, pieceCount), Sites.sequence(#pieces * 7919 + 13))
	if #blocks == 1 then
		table.insert(pieces, record(part, part.CFrame, part.Size))
		return
	end
	local siblings = table.create(#blocks)
	for _, block in ipairs(blocks) do
		local piece = record(part, part.CFrame * CFrame.new(block.offset.X, block.offset.Y, block.offset.Z), block.size)
		piece.blockSize = block.size
		piece.siblings = siblings
		table.insert(pieces, piece)
		table.insert(siblings, #pieces)
	end
end

local function visit(parent, parts)
	for _, child in ipairs(parent:GetChildren()) do
		if not child:GetAttribute("Transformed") then
			if child:IsA("BasePart") and not child:IsA("Terrain") then
				table.insert(parts, child)
			end
			visit(child, parts)
		end
	end
end

function Pieces.parts(reactor)
	local parts = {}
	if reactor:IsA("BasePart") then
		table.insert(parts, reactor)
	end
	visit(reactor, parts)
	return parts
end

-- Moves every rest pose for a Reactor emitted at `origin`: a full pose brings the layout, otherwise
-- each piece keeps its rotation.
function Pieces.carry(pieces, own, origin, fullPose)
	-- A strike or slash is shared by its pieces: each moved once.
	local strikes = {}
	local slashes = {}
	for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		if piece.strike then
			strikes[piece.strike] = true
		end
		if piece.slash then
			slashes[piece.slash] = true
		end
	end
	if fullPose then
		for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
			piece.rest = origin * own:ToObjectSpace(piece.rest)
		end
		for strike in pairs(strikes) do
			strike.origin = origin:PointToWorldSpace(own:PointToObjectSpace(strike.origin))
			strike.normal = origin:VectorToWorldSpace(own:VectorToObjectSpace(strike.normal))
			if strike.path then
				strike.path = Fissure.moved(Fissure.moved(strike.path, own, true), origin, false)
			end
		end
		for slash in pairs(slashes) do
			slash.origin = origin:PointToWorldSpace(own:PointToObjectSpace(slash.origin))
			slash.normal = origin:VectorToWorldSpace(own:VectorToObjectSpace(slash.normal))
			slash.heading = origin:VectorToWorldSpace(own:VectorToObjectSpace(slash.heading))
		end
		return
	end
	local shift = origin.Position - own.Position
	for _, piece in ipairs(pieces) do
		piece.rest = piece.rest + shift
	end
	for strike in pairs(strikes) do
		strike.origin = strike.origin + shift
		if strike.path then
			strike.path = Fissure.moved(strike.path, CFrame.new(shift), false)
		end
	end
	for slash in pairs(slashes) do
		slash.origin = slash.origin + shift
	end
end

-- leftOut(part): a ground, whose cracks are wounds of their own.
function Pieces.collect(reactor, breakMode, pieceCount, shardsOf, leftOut)
	local pieces = {}
	for _, part in ipairs(Pieces.parts(reactor)) do
		if not (leftOut and leftOut(part)) then
			add(pieces, part, breakMode, pieceCount or 50, shardsOf)
		end
	end
	return pieces
end

return Pieces

--[[
	Play  -  one disturbed Reactor: which pieces are out of place, on what paths, and what happens once
	they rest (Fade and Return: Reactor/After; what Forces do: Reactor/Follow, mixed in). Logic only:
	instances through `display`, the world through `castRay`, so it runs under the luau CLI.
	A piece: { rest = CFrame, halfExt = Vector3, size = number, reach = number }. States: RESTING
	(never pushed), FLYING (on a path), LANDED, GONE, DRIVEN (carried by a Continuous Force,
	Reactor/Driven). A push flies a plain arc at once, replaced by the built path (Rocks/Trajectory)
	within the frame's budget. A Force's strength and Hold are distances in studs.
	With Collapse, a piece with no chain of standing neighbours to a support falls (Reactor/Support).
	Cracked ground (Reactor/Crack): a fixed piece is never pushed; a crust piece an Impulse does not
	throw is stood a little out of place and stays RESTING.
	settings: Hold, HoldSpread, Collapse, isAnchored(index), After ("Stay" | "Fade" | "Return"),
	AfterDelay, AfterTime, closes, MaxPieces, MaxAirTime, wakeBudget, buildBudget, rollGravity(),
	rollBounciness(), rollFriction(), rollTumble(), random().
	display: wake(index) -> stand-ins made, move(indices, frames, count), drop(index), restore(index).
	Play:place() stands every piece up as a stand-in at once. step(dt) -> "active", "dormant" (the
	pieces lie still, nothing more without a new Force) or "done" (all back; throw the play away).
	AfterDelay counts from when nothing moves; a live Force that may yet move a piece holds it.
]]

local Trajectory = require(script.Parent.Parent.Rocks.Trajectory)
local Driven = require(script.Parent.Driven)
local Support = require(script.Parent.Support)
local After = require(script.Parent.After)
local Crack = require(script.Parent.Crack)
local Follow = require(script.Parent.Follow)

local RESTING = 0
local FLYING = 1
local LANDED = 2
local GONE = 3
local DRIVEN = Driven.STATE

local ZERO = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)
local UP = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
local TINY = 1e-4
-- The least a play's Max Air Time counts as.
local LEAST_AIR_TIME = 1
-- How far above a surface a piece buried past its middle starts its flight.
local SURFACE_MARGIN = 0.02

local Play = {}
Play.__index = Play
-- watch, strike, kickAgain, _takeTime, _applyImpulse and _followForces: what Forces do to a play.
for name, method in pairs(Follow.methods) do
	Play[name] = method
end

function Play.new(pieces, settings, display, castRay)
	local self = setmetatable({}, Play)
	self.pieces = pieces
	self.settings = settings
	self.display = display
	self.castRay = castRay
	-- A piece whose built path meets no ground within this many seconds is taken away then.
	self.airTime = math.max(settings.MaxAirTime, LEAST_AIR_TIME)
	-- Rocks/Trajectory.build's rules for a piece: off walls, from rest (on or in the ground), ground
	-- looked for through its air time, and a roll off an edge falls on.
	self.pathRules = { offWalls = true, fromRest = true, airTime = self.airTime, offEdges = true }
	self.clock = 0
	self.state = table.create(#pieces, RESTING)
	-- Per piece, set at its first launch.
	self.path = {}
	self.pathStart = {}
	self.pathBuilt = {}
	self.gravity = {}
	self.bounciness = {}
	self.friction = {}
	self.lastFrame = {}
	self.landedAfter = {}
	self.holdOf = {}
	-- Reactor/Support's graph, and whether pieces have left since it was last walked.
	self.support = nil
	self.supportStale = false
	-- record -> the pieces it has already reached.
	self.kicks = {}
	self.flying = {}
	-- The pieces a Continuous Force carries, and their live state (Reactor/Driven).
	self.driven = {}
	-- index -> the way a Continuous Force carried the piece (Reactor/Driven).
	self.track = {}
	self.drivePosition = {}
	self.driveRotation = {}
	self.driveVelocity = {}
	self.driveSpin = {}
	self.pendingWake = {}
	self.pendingPush = {}
	-- Cracked ground (Reactor/Crack): the pieces queued or stood out of place, and their poses.
	self.cracked = {}
	self.crackPower = {}
	self.crackFrame = {}
	self.pendingCrack = {}
	-- record -> true while its later crack is being cut (Reactor/Recrack): that Force leaves the
	-- crust alone until then and kicks it late. "all" while a blade's later cut is made (Recarve).
	self.recracking = {}
	self.buildQueue = {}
	self.moveIndices = {}
	self.moveFrames = {}
	self.moveCount = 0
	-- Pieces with a stand-in, and pieces whose original is hidden (a faded piece is still hidden).
	self.awake = 0
	self.hidden = 0
	-- True once Play:place has stood every piece up as a stand-in.
	self.placed = false
	self.phase = "live"
	self.phaseTime = 0
	self.idleFor = 0
	-- held: a live Force may yet move a piece. busy: something moves, is to come or is on its way
	-- back (Reactor/Wounds waits on it).
	self.held = false
	self.busy = false
	-- The time sources of the Forces that moved a piece (record.time, record.ownTime); the play
	-- steps by the slowest.
	self.times = {}
	return self
end

-- Where a piece is for a Force: cracked ground at rest, a piece standing out of place where it stands.
function Play:_position(index)
	if self.state[index] == RESTING then
		local piece = self.pieces[index]
		return ((not piece.strike and self.crackFrame[index]) or piece.rest).Position
	end
	return self.lastFrame[index].Position
end

local function randomAxis(random)
	local axis = Vector3.new(random() * 2 - 1, random() * 2 - 1, random() * 2 - 1)
	if axis.Magnitude < TINY then
		return UP
	end
	return axis.Unit
end

-- A piece's own Hold: the Reactor's, spread by HoldSpread, rolled the first time it is asked for.
function Play:_holdOf(index)
	local hold = self.holdOf[index]
	if hold == nil then
		local settings = self.settings
		hold = settings.Hold * (1 + settings.HoldSpread * (settings.random() * 2 - 1))
		self.holdOf[index] = hold
	end
	return hold
end

-- A piece's own gravity, bounciness and friction, rolled the first time they are asked for.
function Play:_rolled(index)
	local settings = self.settings
	if self.gravity[index] == nil then
		self.gravity[index] = settings.rollGravity()
		self.bounciness[index] = settings.rollBounciness()
		self.friction[index] = settings.rollFriction()
	end
	return self.gravity[index]
end

-- Puts a piece on a plain arc from `frame` and queues the whole path for building.
function Play:_launch(index, frame, velocity, spin)
	local settings = self.settings
	-- Only a flight that starts where a Force let the piece go has that Force's way before it.
	local track = self.track[index]
	if track and not track.kept then
		self.track[index] = nil
	elseif track then
		track.kept = nil
	end
	self:_rolled(index)
	if spin.Magnitude < TINY then
		spin = randomAxis(settings.random) * settings.rollTumble()
	end
	self.path[index] = Trajectory.ballistic(frame.Position, velocity, frame.Rotation, spin)
	self.pathStart[index] = self.clock
	self.pathBuilt[index] = false
	self.lastFrame[index] = frame
	table.insert(self.buildQueue, index)
	if self.state[index] ~= FLYING then
		self.state[index] = FLYING
		table.insert(self.flying, index)
	end
end

-- Where a resting piece starts its flight: from `stood` (a crack moved it) or its rest; one buried
-- past its middle starts just above the surface, or its flight would never land.
function Play:_surfaced(index, stood)
	local piece = self.pieces[index]
	local rest = stood or piece.rest
	local reach = Support.worldHalf(piece).Y + SURFACE_MARGIN + Crack.buried(piece, rest.Position) + (piece.under or 0)
	local over = self.castRay(rest.Position + UP * reach, UP * -reach)
	if not over then
		return rest
	end
	return rest + UP * (over.Position.Y - rest.Position.Y + SURFACE_MARGIN)
end

-- A push on one piece. A resting piece waits for its stand-in; a moving one is re-launched now.
function Play:_push(index, push)
	local state = self.state[index]
	if state == GONE or self.pieces[index].fixed then
		return
	end
	if state == RESTING then
		if self.placed then
			-- Its stand-in stands there already: it goes now, and counts against no cap.
			self:_launch(index, self:_surfaced(index, self.crackFrame[index]), push, ZERO)
			self.supportStale = true
			return
		end
		if self.pendingPush[index] then
			self.pendingPush[index] += push
			return
		end
		if self.awake + #self.pendingWake >= self.settings.MaxPieces then
			return
		end
		self.pendingPush[index] = push
		table.insert(self.pendingWake, index)
		return
	end
	if state == DRIVEN then
		self.driveVelocity[index] += push
		return
	end
	self:_buildPath(index)
	local elapsed = self.clock - self.pathStart[index]
	local gravity = self.gravity[index]
	local frame = Trajectory.evaluate(self.path[index], elapsed, gravity)
	local velocity, spin = Trajectory.velocity(self.path[index], elapsed, gravity)
	self:_launch(index, frame, velocity + push, spin)
end

-- Stand-ins for the pieces waiting to move, until the frame's budget of new stand-ins is spent.
function Play:_wakePending()
	local pending = self.pendingWake
	local budget = self.settings.wakeBudget
	local taken = 0
	local made = 0
	while taken < #pending and made < budget do
		taken += 1
		local index = pending[taken]
		local push = self.pendingPush[index]
		self.pendingPush[index] = nil
		made += self.display.wake(index) or 1
		self.awake += 1
		self.hidden += 1
		-- A cracked piece flies from where it was stood, or from the surface over that.
		self:_launch(index, self:_surfaced(index, self.crackFrame[index]), push, ZERO)
	end
	if taken == 0 then
		return
	end
	self.supportStale = true
	local remaining = {}
	for position = taken + 1, #pending do
		table.insert(remaining, pending[position])
	end
	self.pendingWake = remaining
end

-- Lets go of every standing piece that has lost its last chain to something that carries it.
-- Those wake over the next frames like any other, and may bring more down in their turn.
function Play:_collapse()
	self.supportStale = false
	local settings = self.settings
	if not settings.Collapse then
		return
	end
	if not self.support then
		self.support = Support.build(self.pieces, settings.isAnchored)
	end
	local fallen = Support.unsupported(self.support, function(index)
		return self.state[index] == RESTING and self.pendingPush[index] == nil
	end)
	for _, index in ipairs(fallen) do
		self:_push(index, ZERO)
	end
end

-- The whole path of one flying piece in place of its plain arc, now, whatever the budget.
-- Nothing to do for a piece whose path is built or that does not fly.
function Play:_buildPath(index)
	if self.state[index] ~= FLYING or self.pathBuilt[index] then
		return
	end
	-- The flight is the last stretch of an unbuilt path: a slide may lead it.
	local plain = self.path[index]
	local start = plain.segs[#plain.segs]
	local built = Trajectory.build(start.p0, start.v0, start.rot0, start.w, self.pieces[index].halfExt, 1,
		self.gravity[index], self.bounciness[index], self.friction[index], self.castRay, self.pathRules)
	if plain.lead then
		built = Trajectory.led(plain.lead, built)
	end
	self.path[index] = built
	self.pathBuilt[index] = true
end

-- Whole paths in place of plain arcs, as many as the frame's budget allows.
function Play:_buildPaths()
	local queue = self.buildQueue
	local taken = math.min(#queue, self.settings.buildBudget)
	if taken == 0 then
		return
	end
	for position = 1, taken do
		self:_buildPath(queue[position])
	end
	local remaining = {}
	for position = taken + 1, #queue do
		table.insert(remaining, queue[position])
	end
	self.buildQueue = remaining
end

-- Hands this frame's poses (flying, then driven pieces) to the display in one go, cut to `count`
-- so they can go straight to BulkMoveTo.
function Play:_flush(count)
	local indices = self.moveIndices
	local frames = self.moveFrames
	for position = count + 1, self.moveCount do
		indices[position] = nil
		frames[position] = nil
	end
	self.moveCount = count
	if count > 0 then
		self.display.move(indices, frames, count)
	end
end

-- Returns how many poses it listed.
function Play:_moveFlying()
	local flying = self.flying
	local count = 0
	local position = 1
	while position <= #flying do
		local index = flying[position]
		-- A piece a Continuous Force took over is dropped from the list here.
		if self.state[index] ~= FLYING then
			local last = #flying
			flying[position] = flying[last]
			flying[last] = nil
			continue
		end
		local path = self.path[index]
		local elapsed = self.clock - self.pathStart[index]
		-- A lost piece leaves before it is listed: one gone stand-in stops the whole move.
		if self.pathBuilt[index] and path.restT == math.huge and elapsed > self.airTime then
			local last = #flying
			flying[position] = flying[last]
			flying[last] = nil
			self.state[index] = GONE
			self.display.drop(index)
			self.awake -= 1
			continue
		end
		local frame = Trajectory.evaluate(path, elapsed, self.gravity[index])
		self.lastFrame[index] = frame
		count += 1
		self.moveIndices[count] = index
		self.moveFrames[count] = frame

		if self.pathBuilt[index] and elapsed >= path.restT then
			local last = #flying
			flying[position] = flying[last]
			flying[last] = nil
			self.state[index] = LANDED
			self.landedAfter[index] = path.restT
		else
			position += 1
		end
	end
	return count
end

function Play:step(dt)
	self.clock += dt
	self.busy = true
	if self.phase == "fading" then
		return After.fade(self, dt)
	elseif self.phase == "returning" then
		return After.back(self, dt)
	elseif self.phase == "closing" then
		return After.close(self, dt)
	end

	self:_followForces()
	self:_wakePending()
	if self.supportStale then
		self:_collapse()
	end
	self:_buildPaths()
	self:_flush(Crack.settle(self, Driven.step(self, dt, self:_moveFlying())))

	self.busy = #self.flying > 0 or #self.driven > 0 or #self.pendingWake > 0 or #self.pendingCrack > 0 or next(self.recracking) ~= nil or self.held
	if self.busy then
		self.idleFor = 0
		return "active"
	end
	-- A live Force keeps the play at work, but the wait below runs from when the pieces lay still.
	local followed = next(self.kicks) ~= nil
	if self.hidden == 0 then
		return if followed then "active" else "done"
	end
	local after = self.settings.After
	-- Something to fade or to bring back: what has landed and, for a Return, what is cracked.
	local settles = self.awake > 0 and After.anyLanded(self)
	if after == "Return" and next(self.crackFrame) ~= nil then
		settles = true
	end
	-- A wound gives its ground back whatever was moved in it (After.close).
	if self.settings.closes then
		settles = true
	end
	if after == "Stay" or not settles then
		return if followed then "active" else "dormant"
	end
	self.idleFor += dt
	if self.idleFor >= self.settings.AfterDelay then
		self.phaseTime = 0
		self.phase = After.begin(self)
	end
	return "active"
end

-- Stands the whole Reactor up as stand-ins, the originals hidden, for a play whose rest poses are
-- elsewhere (Reactor/Pieces.carry). Called once, on a new play.
function Play:place()
	if self.placed then
		return
	end
	self.placed = true
	for index in ipairs(self.pieces) do
		self.display.wake(index)
		self.awake += 1
		self.hidden += 1
	end
end

-- Everything back: stand-ins removed, originals shown. A piece cut again stays out: its pieces
-- stand for it.
function Play:restore()
	for index, piece in ipairs(self.pieces) do
		if self.state[index] ~= RESTING or self.placed or self.crackFrame[index] then
			self.display.restore(index)
			self.state[index] = RESTING
			if piece.retired then
				self.state[index] = GONE
			end
		end
	end
	self.placed = false
	self.flying = {}
	self.driven = {}
	self.track = {}
	self.pendingWake = {}
	self.pendingPush = {}
	self.cracked = {}
	self.crackPower = {}
	self.crackFrame = {}
	self.pendingCrack = {}
	self.buildQueue = {}
	self.kicks = {}
	self:_flush(0)
	self.awake = 0
	self.hidden = 0
	self.phase = "live"
	self.phaseTime = 0
	self.idleFor = 0
end

Play.RESTING = RESTING
Play.FLYING = FLYING
Play.LANDED = LANDED
Play.GONE = GONE
Play.DRIVEN = DRIVEN

return Play
