--[[
	Reach: whether a Force reaches a part-icle that may react (Reactor/HandOver). Numbers only. These
	are a Reactor piece's own rules (Reactor/Follow, Reactor/Driven) asked of something that is not a
	piece yet: inside the field's shape, behind its front, and moved by it more than the Hold. Nothing
	here makes a table. Reactor/HandOver asks only inside a ball round the shape.

	  Reach.moved(record, position, extent, hold, age) -> whether the record's Force moves it now
	    extent  the part-icle's Size; a Force's Size Response goes by the cube of its volume
	    hold    the throw in studs it shrugs off (an Impulse), or the speed (a Continuous Force)
	    age     seconds since the part-icle was emitted
	  Reach.inBlade(record, position, radius, age) -> whether the box of a Linear record, grown by the
	    radius, holds the place and its front has come that far: the first test for a blade
	    (Reactor/Blade.touches decides)

	A part-icle emitted where an Impulse's front has already passed is left alone: the blast went by
	before it was there. A Force that is itself on its way (record.moving, Force/init) reaches whatever
	it comes to.
	Cross-file: the two formulas are Follow's (throw against Hold) and Driven's (speed against Hold),
	without a kick's Variation: a part-icle is asked every frame, and a per-frame roll would let it through.
]]

local Fields = require(script.Parent.Parent.Force.Fields)

local Reach = {}

-- Whether an Impulse's front had passed a place `distance` along its way before a part-icle `age`
-- seconds old was emitted there.
local function passedBefore(record, distance, age)
	if record.actsAs ~= "Impulse" or record.moving then
		return false
	end
	local ageThen = record.age - age
	if ageThen <= 0 then
		return false
	end
	if record.travelSpeed <= 0 then
		return true
	end
	return record.travelSpeed * ageThen >= distance
end

function Reach.moved(record, position, extent, hold, age)
	local strength = record.strength
	local direction, distance, distance01 = Fields.sample(record.field, position, strength < 0)
	if not direction or distance > record.front then
		return false
	end
	if passedBefore(record, distance, age) then
		return false
	end
	local size = (extent.X * extent.Y * extent.Z) ^ (1 / 3)
	local moves = math.abs(strength) * Fields.kept(record.falloff, distance01) * Fields.sizeShare(size, record.sizeResponse)
	return moves > hold
end

function Reach.inBlade(record, position, radius, age)
	local field = record.field
	local point = field.origin:PointToObjectSpace(position)
	local forward = -point.Z
	if forward > field.range + radius or forward < field.inner - radius then
		return false
	end
	if math.abs(point.X) > field.halfWidth + radius or math.abs(point.Y) > field.halfHeight + radius then
		return false
	end
	if forward - radius > record.front then
		return false
	end
	return not passedBefore(record, forward, age)
end

return Reach

--[[
	Recarve  -  a blade through a Reactor that is out of place already. A part is carved for the
	first Force that cuts it (Reactor/CutPlan, Reactor/Carve); every cutting Force after it cuts the
	PIECES its blade touches, while the play has room for more (its Max Pieces).

	A piece is cut where it is (standing, stood out of place, lying or in the air): the blade is taken
	into the piece's own space, the engine cuts the piece's own shard there, and the results stand in
	for the piece as it is: standing, lying (LANDED) or in flight at its speed and spin. The piece
	itself leaves the play (piece.retired).

	A ground's gash is cut again the same way (Reactor/Wounds). A PART with a slot in it stands only
	while it is in one piece; a later blade gives two ordinary sides, which Reactor/Slash lets go.

	What stands is cut before the debris that lies about, even when the play has no room left; a cut
	whose debris or breaking has no room is made as Halves.

	Not cut again: a piece carried by a Continuous Force, cracked ground and the base under its crust
	(Reactor/Crack), the debris of a Band, a piece whose longest edge is under LEAST_PIECE, and the
	pieces of this Force's own cut.

	The cut takes a few frames. Until it is in, its Force leaves the whole play alone
	(play.recracking[record] = "all") and then kicks late (Play:kickAgain). A second request waits
	for the first.

	Recarve.request(entry, record, kicked, isCurrent, revive)
	    entry: Reactor/Entries', with play, pieceCount and breaks (whether the Reactor's Break
	    gives a part pieces of its own). Keeps entry.carves (the requests waiting) and entry.carved
	    (the Forces that have asked: one cut a Force). kicked, isCurrent, revive: as
	    Reactor/Recrack.request takes them.
	Recarve.plan(play, blade, record, pieceCount) -> { blade, record, jobs }
	    jobs: Reactor/Carve's, each with the index of the piece it cuts; nearest the Force first.
	Recarve.apply(play, plan, results) -> the places of the new pieces in play.pieces
]]

local Trajectory = require(script.Parent.Parent.Rocks.Trajectory)
local Blade = require(script.Parent.Blade)
local Pieces = require(script.Parent.Pieces)
local Shards = require(script.Parent.Shards)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Carve = require(script.Parent.Carve)

local RESTING = 0
local FLYING = 1
local LANDED = 2
local GONE = 3

local IDENTITY = CFrame.new(0, 0, 0)
local UP = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
local TINY = 1e-6
-- A piece whose longest edge is under this many studs is not cut again.
local LEAST_PIECE = 1
-- Pieces cut for one Force.
local MOST_JOBS = 64
-- A point a side breaks around keeps this far inside the piece's box.
local INSET = 0.9
-- Debris of a kerf: about one bit for this many studs square of the piece's face (Reactor/Carve).
local BIT_AREA = 9
local LEAST_BITS = 3

local Recarve = {}

local function poseOf(play, index)
	if play.state[index] == RESTING then
		return play.crackFrame[index] or play.pieces[index].rest
	end
	return play.lastFrame[index]
end

local function carvable(play, index, record)
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	local state = play.state[index]
	if state ~= RESTING and state ~= LANDED and state ~= FLYING then
		return false
	end
	-- A Matte's shape that has reacted is a window, never cut (Reactor/Owned).
	if piece.retired or piece.bit or piece.uncut or play.pendingPush[index] ~= nil or piece.reach < LEAST_PIECE then
		return false
	end
	-- Cracked ground and the base under its crust are Reactor/Crack's.
	if piece.strike or (piece.fixed and not piece.slash) then
		return false
	end
	if piece.slash and piece.slash.by == record then
		return false
	end
	return piece.shard ~= nil or piece.blockSize ~= nil or Shards.cuttable(piece.part)
end

-- How many pieces a job is expected to add to the play.
local function growth(piece, mode, count)
	if mode == "Pieces" then
		return math.max(count, 1)
	elseif mode == "Band" then
		local size = piece.halfExt * 2
		local longest = math.max(size.X, size.Y, size.Z)
		local middling = size.X + size.Y + size.Z - longest - math.min(size.X, size.Y, size.Z)
		return 1 + math.clamp(math.round(longest * middling / BIT_AREA), LEAST_BITS, Carve.MOST_BITS)
	end
	return 1
end

-- The cut of one piece by the blade, in the piece's own space.
local function jobFor(play, index, blade, record, pieceCount)
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	local box = piece.box or IDENTITY
	-- The space the piece's box is told in, where what the engine cuts lies: a shard's
	-- template where it was cut, a whole part where it is, a block at the origin.
	local space = IDENTITY
	if piece.shard then
		space = piece.shard.ExtentsCFrame * box:Inverse()
	elseif not piece.blockSize then
		space = piece.part.CFrame
	end
	-- The world as it is now, seen from that space: the blade goes where the piece has gone.
	local inSpace = box * poseOf(play, index):Inverse()
	local mode = record.cut.mode
	local seed = Sites.seedAt(blade.origin) + index
	-- Asked with the whole part: all its pieces are cut by the same ribbon of a jagged blade.
	local ribbon, ribbonFrame = Blade.ribbonFor(blade, piece.part.CFrame, piece.part.Size, inSpace)
	local count = 0
	local points = nil
	if mode == "Pieces" and pieceCount >= 2 then
		local size = piece.halfExt * 2
		local whole = piece.part.Size
		local share = size.X * size.Y * size.Z / math.max(whole.X * whole.Y * whole.Z, TINY)
		count = math.round(math.min(pieceCount * share, Sites.MAX))
		if count >= 2 then
			local random = Sites.sequence(seed)
			points = table.create(count)
			for position = 1, count do
				local inBox = Vector3.new((random() - 0.5) * size.X, (random() - 0.5) * size.Y, (random() - 0.5) * size.Z) * INSET
				points[position] = box:PointToWorldSpace(inBox)
			end
		else
			count = 0
		end
	end
	return {
		index = index,
		part = piece.part,
		template = piece.shard,
		blockSize = piece.blockSize,
		baked = piece.baked,
		frame = space,
		bladeFrame = inSpace * blade.frame,
		bladeSize = blade.size,
		ribbon = ribbon,
		ribbonFrame = ribbonFrame,
		slash = {
			origin = inSpace:PointToWorldSpace(blade.origin),
			normal = inSpace:VectorToWorldSpace(blade.normal),
			heading = inSpace:VectorToWorldSpace(blade.heading),
			kerf = blade.kerf,
		},
		mode = mode,
		count = count,
		points = points,
		seed = seed,
		-- A ground's patch stands however it is cut; a part does while it is in one piece.
		stands = piece.fixed == true and piece.cut ~= nil,
	}
end

function Recarve.plan(play, blade, record, pieceCount)
	local live = 0
	local touched = {}
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if play.state[index] ~= GONE then
			live += 1
		end
		if carvable(play, index, record) then
			local pose = poseOf(play, index)
			if Blade.touches(blade, pose, piece.halfExt * 2) then
				table.insert(touched, { index = index, fixed = piece.fixed == true, away = (pose.Position - blade.origin).Magnitude })
			end
		end
	end
	table.sort(touched, function(first, second)
		if first.fixed ~= second.fixed then
			return first.fixed
		end
		return first.away < second.away
	end)
	local settings = play.settings
	local room = (settings.MostPieces or settings.MaxPieces) - live
	-- Debris and breaking are made within Max Pieces itself; the bare cut within the room a
	-- wound's later cracks have (Reactor/WoundBudget).
	local spare = settings.MaxPieces - live
	local jobs = {}
	for _, entry in ipairs(touched) do
		if #jobs >= MOST_JOBS then
			break
		end
		local job = jobFor(play, entry.index, blade, record, pieceCount)
		local grows = growth(play.pieces[entry.index], job.mode, job.count)
		if grows > math.min(room, spare) then
			job.mode = "Halves"
			job.count = 0
			job.points = nil
			grows = 1
		end
		if grows <= room or entry.fixed then
			room -= grows
			table.insert(jobs, job)
		end
	end
	return { blade = blade, record = record, jobs = jobs }
end

local function discard(shards)
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards or {}) do
		shard.template:Destroy()
	end
end

local function replace(play, plan, job, shards, taken, movedIndices, movedFrames)
	local index = job.index
	local leaf = play.pieces[index]
	local box = leaf.box or IDENTITY
	local stood = play.crackFrame[index]
	local lying = nil
	local lyingOn = UP
	local flying = nil
	local velocity, spin = nil, nil
	if play.state[index] == LANDED then
		lying = play.lastFrame[index]
		lyingOn = play.path[index].restNormal or UP
	elseif play.state[index] == FLYING then
		local elapsed = play.clock - play.pathStart[index]
		flying = Trajectory.evaluate(play.path[index], elapsed, play.gravity[index])
		velocity, spin = Trajectory.velocity(play.path[index], elapsed, play.gravity[index])
	end
	local siblings = leaf.siblings
	if siblings then
		local place = table.find(siblings, index)
		if place then
			table.remove(siblings, place)
		end
	else
		siblings = {}
	end
	-- A ground's patch stands however it is cut; a part with a slot while it is in one piece.
	local sides = 0
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
		if not shard.bit then
			sides += 1
		end
	end
	local standsOn = leaf.fixed == true and (leaf.cut ~= nil or sides <= 1)
	local space = leaf.rest * box:Inverse()
	local wholeSize = leaf.part.Size
	if leaf.cut then
		wholeSize = leaf.cut.size
	end
	local blade = plan.blade
	local slash = { origin = blade.origin, normal = blade.normal, heading = blade.heading, kerf = blade.kerf, by = plan.record }
	local shown = nil
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
		local rest = leaf.rest * box:ToObjectSpace(shard.box)
		local piece = Pieces.ofShard(leaf.part, rest, shard)
		piece.siblings = siblings
		piece.slash = slash
		piece.side = shard.side
		piece.bit = shard.bit
		piece.baked = shard.baked
		-- A part that is parted stands no longer: its sides are ordinary pieces, and the
		-- hidden part itself leaves the play's rays when one of them wakes (Reactor/Entries).
		if standsOn then
			piece.partStands = leaf.partStands
			piece.fixed = not shard.bit or nil
		end
		-- A patch's pieces stay its patch's: Reactor/Display lays the ground's Texture by it.
		piece.cut = leaf.cut
		if leaf.cut and piece.fixed and Pieces.reachesFace(shard.box, piece.halfExt, leaf.cut) then
			piece.atFace = true
		end
		if standsOn and shard.bit then
			piece.under = Pieces.underTop(space, wholeSize, piece)
		end
		table.insert(play.pieces, piece)
		local child = #play.pieces
		table.insert(siblings, child)
		table.insert(taken, child)
		shown = shown or child
		play.state[child] = RESTING
		local now = nil
		if lying then
			now = lying * leaf.rest:ToObjectSpace(rest)
			play.state[child] = LANDED
			play.path[child] = Trajectory.lying(now, lyingOn)
			play.pathStart[child] = play.clock
			play.pathBuilt[child] = true
			play.lastFrame[child] = now
			play.landedAfter[child] = 0
			play:_rolled(child)
			play.awake += 1
		elseif flying then
			now = flying * leaf.rest:ToObjectSpace(rest)
			play:_launch(child, now, velocity, spin)
			play.awake += 1
		elseif stood and not (standsOn and shard.bit) then
			-- Debris of something fixed keeps no pose of its own: it starts on top (Play:_surfaced).
			now = stood * leaf.rest:ToObjectSpace(rest)
			play.crackFrame[child] = now
		end
		if now then
			table.insert(movedIndices, child)
			table.insert(movedFrames, now)
		end
	end
	leaf.retired = true
	play.state[index] = GONE
	play.cracked[index] = nil
	play.crackFrame[index] = nil
	play.display.drop(index)
	if lying or flying then
		play.awake -= 1
	elseif not stood then
		-- The part is hidden for as long as its pieces stand in for it: that counts once.
		play.hidden += 1
	end
	-- Waking one piece shows every piece of its part that has no stand-in yet (Reactor/Display).
	if shown then
		play.display.wake(shown)
	end
end

function Recarve.apply(play, plan, results)
	local taken = {}
	local movedIndices = {}
	local movedFrames = {}
	for position, job in ipairs(plan.jobs) do
		local shards = results[position]
		if shards and #shards >= 1 and carvable(play, job.index, plan.record) then
			replace(play, plan, job, shards, taken, movedIndices, movedFrames)
		else
			discard(shards or nil)
		end
	end
	if #movedIndices > 0 then
		play.display.move(movedIndices, movedFrames, #movedIndices)
	end
	-- Reactor/Support's graph names pieces by their place in the list, which has grown.
	play.support = nil
	return taken
end

local function takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	local request = entry.carves[1]
	if not request then
		return
	end
	local play = entry.play
	local record = request.record

	-- The Force left the play alone while its cut was made (Play.recracking): it kicks now,
	-- and Reactor/Slash lets go of the sides it finds for this Force.
	local function finish(indices)
		table.remove(entry.carves, 1)
		play.recracking[record] = nil
		if play.slashed then
			play.slashed[record] = nil
		end
		play:kickAgain(record, request.kicked, indices or {})
		revive()
		takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	end

	local blade = Blade.of(record.field, record.cut)
	if play.phase ~= "live" or not blade then
		finish(nil)
		return
	end
	local pieceCount = 0
	if entry.breaks then
		pieceCount = entry.pieceCount
	end
	local plan = Recarve.plan(play, blade, record, pieceCount)
	if #plan.jobs == 0 then
		finish(nil)
		return
	end
	Shards.recut(plan.jobs, function(results)
		if not isCurrent() or play.phase ~= "live" then
			for _, shards in ipairs(results) do
				discard(shards or nil)
			end
			if isCurrent() then
				finish(nil)
			else
				table.clear(entry.carves)
			end
			return
		end
		finish(Recarve.apply(play, plan, results))
	end)
end

function Recarve.request(entry, record, kicked, isCurrent, revive)
	if not kicked or not record.cut then
		return
	end
	if not entry.carved then
		entry.carved = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
		entry.carves = {}
	end
	if entry.carved[record] then
		return
	end
	entry.carved[record] = true
	table.insert(entry.carves, { record = record, kicked = kicked })
	entry.play.recracking[record] = "all"
	if #entry.carves == 1 then
		takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	end
end

return Recarve

--[[
	Recrack  -  the later cracks of one Reactor's play, taken one after another.

	Reactor/init asks for one each time an Impulse reaches a Reactor that is out of place already
	(Recrack.request). Reactor/Recut plans it, Reactor/Shards cuts the pieces (a few frames), Recut
	puts them into the play, and the Force that asked is then given to the new pieces late
	(Play:kickAgain). A second request waits for the first: it is planned on the pieces the first
	one left.

	One Force cracks one place once: asked again where it last cracked, it is given nothing
	(Reactor/Entries asks for every Force a Reactor is told of, and is told again of one that has
	moved). Another Force at that place cracks the ground again with rings laid from other numbers,
	so the pieces there are cut finer and moved on.

	Recrack.request(entry, record, kicked, isCurrent, revive)
	    entry: Reactor/init's, with play, pieceCount (the Reactor's Pieces) and cracks (the requests
	    waiting, oldest first); a wound of Reactor/Wounds has that shape. Recrack keeps two fields
	    of its own on it: places (record -> where it last cracked) and taken (the cracks planned so
	    far). kicked: the record's own list of the pieces it has kicked in this play (Play.kicks[record],
	    or what Play:strike returned for an Impulse that is over); nil asks for nothing.
	    isCurrent() -> whether the entry is still its Reactor's: a Reactor put back while a cut
	    runs gets nothing. revive(): the play has work again.
	Recrack.opened(entry, records, hit)
	    The entry's first cut was made around `hit`: the first Impulse of `records` that stands
	    there has cracked that place, and asks for nothing more at it.
]]

local Recut = require(script.Parent.Recut)
local Shards = require(script.Parent.Shards)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)

-- A Force within this many studs of where it last cracked is at that place still.
local SAME_PLACE = 1
-- Keeps the rings of one crack apart from those of the crack before it at the same place.
local SEED_STEP = 104729

local Recrack = {}

-- record -> where it last cracked this entry's ground; a record that is over is forgotten.
local function placesOf(entry)
	if not entry.places then
		entry.places = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
	end
	return entry.places
end

local function takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	local request = entry.cracks[1]
	if not request then
		return
	end
	local play = entry.play
	local record = request.record

	-- The Force left the standing crust alone while its crack was cut (Play.recracking): it
	-- kicks now, the new pieces and those that joined (`indices`) included.
	local function finish(indices)
		table.remove(entry.cracks, 1)
		play.recracking[record] = nil
		play:kickAgain(record, request.kicked, indices or {})
		revive()
		takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	end

	if play.phase ~= "live" then
		finish(nil)
		return
	end
	local hit = record.field.origin.Position
	-- A Force may name the pieces of its own crack (record.pieces, Force/Registry).
	entry.taken = (entry.taken or 0) + 1
	local seed = Sites.seedAt(hit) + entry.taken * SEED_STEP
	local plan = Recut.plan(play, hit, record.field.range, record.pieces or entry.pieceCount, seed, record.field)
	if not plan then
		finish(nil)
		return
	end
	-- The strikes are this Force's: Reactor/Crack tells by that which pieces its split reaches.
	for _, strike in ipairs(plan.strikes) do
		strike.by = record
	end
	if #plan.jobs == 0 then
		finish(Recut.apply(play, plan, {}))
		return
	end
	Shards.recut(plan.jobs, function(results)
		if not isCurrent() then
			table.clear(entry.cracks)
			return
		end
		if play.phase ~= "live" then
			finish(nil)
			return
		end
		finish(Recut.apply(play, plan, results))
	end)
end

function Recrack.request(entry, record, kicked, isCurrent, revive)
	if not kicked then
		return
	end
	local places = placesOf(entry)
	local hit = record.field.origin.Position
	local last = places[record]
	if last and (last - hit).Magnitude < SAME_PLACE then
		return
	end
	places[record] = hit
	table.insert(entry.cracks, { record = record, kicked = kicked })
	entry.play.recracking[record] = true
	if #entry.cracks == 1 then
		takeNext(entry, isCurrent, revive)
	end
end

function Recrack.opened(entry, records, hit)
	for _, record in ipairs(records) do
		local stands = record.field.origin.Position
		if record.actsAs == "Impulse" and (stands - hit).Magnitude < SAME_PLACE then
			placesOf(entry)[record] = stands
			return
		end
	end
end

return Recrack

--[[
	Recut  -  a later crack in ground already cracked ("Cracks"). Part of Reactor/Play. Maths only;
	the cut is Reactor/Shards.recut.
	A later Impulse lays rings of its own (Sites.cracks around its hit). A standing crust piece two or
	more of its points fall in is cut again around them: its pieces take its place with a strike of
	their own. A standing piece within the reach that is not cut joins the crack whole. Thrown pieces
	and the base stay. A piece keeps what earlier cracks did to it (Reactor/Crack.pose).
	No crack is refused for room: past Max Pieces fewer points are used (nearest first), and a piece
	with no room joins whole; one wider than the crater may use up to PLATE_ROOM times Max Pieces.
	Which piece a point falls in: the nearest point of a cut owns the space (sites / siteIndex, and
	cutPoints / children for a piece cut again).
	  Recut.plan(play, hit, reach, count, seed, field) -> plan or nil
	      plan.jobs { { index, template, points, strike, within, always } }, plan.joins { { index,
	      strike } }, plan.strikes. A Linear Force splits along its path (Reactor/Fissure), one path
	      across every ground it crosses.
	  Recut.apply(play, plan, results) -> indices (Play:kickAgain gives them the Force's kick)
	  Recut.PLATE_ROOM
]]

local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Pieces = require(script.Parent.Pieces)
local Fissure = require(script.Parent.Fissure)
local Crack = require(script.Parent.Crack)

local RESTING = 0
local GONE = 3

-- Two unit normals with at least this dot product face the same way.
local SAME_FACE = 0.99
-- A piece whose longest edge is under this many studs is not cut again.
local LEAST_RECUT = 1.5

local Recut = {}

Recut.PLATE_ROOM = 1.5

-- Where a piece's part stands for the play.
local function partFrame(piece)
	return piece.rest * piece.box:Inverse()
end

local function stands(play, index)
	local piece = play.pieces[index]
	return play.state[index] == RESTING and play.pendingPush[index] == nil and not piece.retired and not piece.fixed
end

-- The place in `points` of the one nearest to `point`.
local function nearest(points, point)
	local best = nil
	local least = math.huge
	for index, candidate in ipairs(points) do
		local distance = (candidate - point).Magnitude
		if distance < least then
			least = distance
			best = index
		end
	end
	return best
end

-- The crust piece a point of the part falls in now, or nil; walks down through every later cut.
local function ownerOf(play, ground, point)
	local index = ground.pieceOf[nearest(ground.sites, point)]
	while index do
		local piece = play.pieces[index]
		if not piece.retired then
			return index
		end
		index = piece.children[nearest(piece.cutPoints, point)]
	end
	return nil
end

-- Every cracked ground of the play (a part, or a patch of one): frame, size, first cut, strikes.
local function grounds(play)
	local bySpace = {}
	local ordered = {}
	local live = 0
	for index, piece in ipairs(play.pieces) do
		if not piece.retired then
			live += 1
		end
		if piece.box and piece.siteIndex and not piece.fixed then
			local space = piece.cut or piece.part
			local ground = bySpace[space]
			if not ground then
				local size = piece.part.Size
				if piece.cut then
					size = piece.cut.size
				end
				ground = { size = size, face = piece.cut and piece.cut.face, frame = partFrame(piece), pieceOf = {}, strikes = {}, pieces = {} }
				bySpace[space] = ground
				table.insert(ordered, ground)
			end
			table.insert(ground.pieces, index)
			if piece.sites then
				ground.sites = piece.sites
				ground.pieceOf[piece.siteIndex] = index
			end
			if piece.strike and not table.find(ground.strikes, piece.strike) then
				table.insert(ground.strikes, piece.strike)
			end
		end
	end
	return ordered, live
end

-- Whether a crack comes near a part: a round one by its Force, a split by its path.
local function comesNear(size, hitInPart, reach, line)
	if not line then
		return (hitInPart - Sites.hitIn(size, hitInPart)).Magnitude <= reach * Sites.RUN_ON
	end
	for _, point in ipairs(line.path.points) do
		if (point - Sites.hitIn(size, point)).Magnitude <= line.reach * Sites.RUN_ON then
			return true
		end
	end
	return false
end

-- One part's new crack, added to the plan. crack = { hit, reach, count, seed, field }.
local function planGround(play, ground, crack, position, plan)
	if not ground.sites or #ground.strikes == 0 then
		return
	end
	local frame = ground.frame
	local size = ground.size
	local hit, reach = crack.hit, crack.reach
	local hitInPart = frame:PointToObjectSpace(hit)
	local points = Sites.count(size, crack.count)
	local first = ground.strikes[1]
	local normal = frame:VectorToObjectSpace(first.normal)
	local line = nil
	if crack.field then
		line = Fissure.of(crack.field, frame, frame:PointToObjectSpace(first.origin), normal, Sites.sequence(Sites.seedAt(hit)))
	end
	if points < 2 or not comesNear(size, hitInPart, reach, line) then
		return
	end
	if line then
		-- One layout for the whole split.
		line.seed = crack.seed
	end
	-- The crust keeps the first cut's thickness.
	local random = Sites.sequence(crack.seed + position * 7919)
	local offsets, cut = Sites.cracks(size, points, hitInPart, reach, random, { face = ground.face, crust = first.crust, line = line })
	if cut.normal:Dot(normal) < SAME_FACE then
		return
	end
	local origin = frame:PointToWorldSpace(cut.origin)
	local strike = { origin = origin, normal = first.normal, reach = cut.reach, crust = first.crust }
	if cut.path then
		strike.path = Fissure.moved(cut.path, frame, false)
	end
	table.insert(plan.strikes, strike)

	local byPiece = {}
	for _, point in ipairs(offsets) do
		local owner = ownerOf(play, ground, point)
		if owner and stands(play, owner) then
			local list = byPiece[owner]
			if not list then
				list = {}
				byPiece[owner] = list
			end
			table.insert(list, point)
		end
	end

	for _, index in ipairs(ground.pieces) do
		if stands(play, index) then
			local piece = play.pieces[index]
			local within = Crack.shareAt(strike, piece.rest.Position) <= 1
			local list = byPiece[index]
			if list and #list >= 2 and piece.reach >= LEAST_RECUT then
				table.insert(plan.jobs, { index = index, template = piece.shard, layered = piece.layered, points = list, strike = strike, within = within, always = Crack.outsizes(piece, strike) })
			elseif within then
				table.insert(plan.joins, { index = index, strike = strike })
			end
		end
	end
end

-- Holds a plan to the room left (`room`, `plateRoom` for pieces wider than the crater); the
-- farthest points go first.
local function fit(plan, room, plateRoom)
	local jobs = {}
	for _, job in ipairs(plan.jobs) do
		local points = job.points
		local allowed = room
		if job.always then
			allowed = plateRoom
		end
		for position = #points, math.max(allowed + 2, 1), -1 do
			points[position] = nil
		end
		if #points >= 2 then
			room -= #points - 1
			plateRoom -= #points - 1
			table.insert(jobs, job)
		elseif job.within then
			table.insert(plan.joins, { index = job.index, strike = job.strike })
		end
	end
	plan.jobs = jobs
end

function Recut.plan(play, hit, reach, count, seed, field)
	local ordered, live = grounds(play)
	local plan = { jobs = {}, joins = {}, strikes = {} }
	local crack = { hit = hit, reach = reach, count = count, seed = seed, field = field }
	for position, ground in ipairs(ordered) do
		planGround(play, ground, crack, position, plan)
	end
	if #plan.jobs == 0 and #plan.joins == 0 then
		return nil
	end
	local settings = play.settings
	local most = settings.MostPieces or settings.MaxPieces * Recut.PLATE_ROOM
	fit(plan, settings.MaxPieces - live, most - live)
	return plan
end

-- Takes a cut piece out of the play and puts its pieces in (they stand where it stood); new pieces
-- go to `taken`, those out of place to the move lists.
local function replace(play, job, shards, taken, movedIndices, movedFrames)
	local leaf = play.pieces[job.index]
	local siblings = leaf.siblings
	local place = table.find(siblings, job.index)
	if place then
		table.remove(siblings, place)
	end
	local stood = play.crackFrame[job.index]
	local children = {}
	local shown = nil
	for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
		local rest = leaf.rest * leaf.box:ToObjectSpace(shard.box)
		local piece = Pieces.ofShard(leaf.part, rest, shard, leaf.looks)
		piece.siblings = siblings
		piece.strike = job.strike
		-- Baked colours carry down.
		piece.baked = leaf.baked
		piece.cut = leaf.cut
		if leaf.cut and Pieces.touchesSide(shard.box, piece.halfExt, leaf.cut) then
			piece.atEdge = true
		end
		if leaf.cut and Pieces.reachesFace(shard.box, piece.halfExt, leaf.cut) then
			piece.atFace = true
		end
		table.insert(play.pieces, piece)
		local index = #play.pieces
		play.state[index] = RESTING
		table.insert(siblings, index)
		table.insert(taken, index)
		if shard.siteIndex then
			children[shard.siteIndex] = index
		end
		shown = shown or index
		if stood then
			local frame = stood * leaf.rest:ToObjectSpace(rest)
			play.crackFrame[index] = frame
			table.insert(movedIndices, index)
			table.insert(movedFrames, frame)
		end
	end
	leaf.retired = true
	leaf.children = children
	leaf.cutPoints = job.points
	play.state[job.index] = GONE
	play.cracked[job.index] = nil
	play.crackFrame[job.index] = nil
	play.display.drop(job.index)
	-- The part is hidden once, however many cut pieces stand for it.
	if not stood then
		play.hidden += 1
	end
	-- Waking one piece shows its part's others.
	play.display.wake(shown)
end

function Recut.apply(play, plan, results)
	local taken = {}
	local movedIndices = {}
	local movedFrames = {}
	local function join(index, strike)
		if not stands(play, index) then
			return
		end
		local piece = play.pieces[index]
		piece.strike = strike
		piece.joined = true
		play.cracked[index] = nil
		table.insert(taken, index)
	end
	for position, job in ipairs(plan.jobs) do
		local shards = results[position]
		if shards and #shards >= 2 and stands(play, job.index) then
			replace(play, job, shards, taken, movedIndices, movedFrames)
		elseif job.within then
			join(job.index, job.strike)
		end
	end
	for _, joined in ipairs(plan.joins) do
		join(joined.index, joined.strike)
	end
	if #movedIndices > 0 then
		play.display.move(movedIndices, movedFrames, #movedIndices)
	end
	-- Reactor/Support's graph is by list place, which has grown.
	play.support = nil
	return taken
end

return Recut

--[[
	Refusals: what the engine has said, this session, of the meshes it was asked to cut.

	A mesh that is not a closed solid is refused by every engine solid-modelling call (Fragment,
	Subtract, Intersect, Union: "Non-manifold mesh part"). The refusal takes about half a second
	unless the engine was asked about that mesh in the previous two seconds. So a refusal is kept by
	mesh for the session, and a mesh is asked about ahead of the Force that would cut it
	(Refusals.judge): a part of a refused mesh moves whole at once. A mesh is named by its MeshId or,
	for an EditableMesh part, by that mesh (its copies share it). A plugin cannot read a mesh it does
	not own, so it cannot close one either.

	  Refusals.refused(part) -> boolean     a mesh part whose mesh the engine refused as not solid
	  Refusals.notSolid(reason) -> boolean  whether an engine reason is that refusal
	  Refusals.cut(part)                    the engine cut a part: its mesh is one it cuts
	  Refusals.refuse(part, reason)         a refused cut; kept when the mesh is the reason, and told
	  Refusals.explain(part)                tells why a part to be cut moves whole, if its mesh was refused
	  Refusals.judge(part, fragment, done)
	    Asks the engine, once per mesh a session, whether it cuts a mesh part at all: a cut in two of
	    a copy kept out of the world, by fragment(part, points) -> fragments | nil, reason
	    (Reactor/Shards'). Calls done() when the answer is in, at once for a mesh already asked about
	    or a part that is no mesh part. Returns at once.

	Told: one Log.warn line per mesh (or part without one) a session.
]]

local Log = require(script.Parent.Parent.Log)

-- Probes of a mesh running at once.
local JUDGES = 2
-- The engine's word for a mesh that is not a closed solid.
local NOT_SOLID = "manifold"

local Refusals = {}

-- mesh -> the engine's reason once it refused the mesh, true once it cut it, or the list of who
-- waits while it is asked. Strong: Roblox hands out a new EditableMesh handle once none is held,
-- so a weak table would lose the entry while the mesh lives (docs/bug-prevention.md).
local verdicts = {}
-- An EditableMesh the engine cut; weak, losing it costs one quick question.
local cutMeshes = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
-- Meshes, and meshless parts (by full name), whose refusal has been told.
local told = {}
-- Parts whose meshes wait to be asked about, and how many probes run.
local waiting = {}
local judges = 0

local function contentObject(part)
	return part.MeshContent.Object
end

-- What names a mesh part's mesh, or nil for any other part.
local function meshOf(part)
	if not part:IsA("MeshPart") then
		return nil
	end
	local id = part.MeshId
	if id ~= nil and id ~= "" then
		return id
	end
	local ok, object = pcall(contentObject, part)
	if ok then
		return object
	end
	return nil
end

local function notSolid(reason)
	return string.find(reason, NOT_SOLID, 1, true) ~= nil
end
Refusals.notSolid = notSolid

-- The engine's word on a mesh so far: a reason, true, a list of who waits, or nil.
local function verdictOf(mesh)
	return verdicts[mesh] or (cutMeshes[mesh] and true) or nil
end

local function tell(part, reason)
	local key = meshOf(part) or ("part:" .. part:GetFullName())
	if told[key] then
		return
	end
	told[key] = true
	local hint = ""
	if notSolid(reason) then
		hint = " A mesh must be a closed solid to be cut."
	end
	Log.warn(string.format("[Part-Icles] Reactor: the engine will not cut %s (%s), so it moves whole.%s", part:GetFullName(), reason, hint))
end

-- Keeps the engine's word on a mesh and answers who waited. A refusal stays.
local function settle(mesh, verdict)
	local before = verdictOf(mesh)
	if type(before) == "string" then
		return
	end
	if verdict == true and type(mesh) ~= "string" then
		verdicts[mesh] = nil
		cutMeshes[mesh] = true
	else
		verdicts[mesh] = verdict
	end
	if type(before) == "table" then
		for _, done in ipairs(before) do
			done()
		end
	end
end

function Refusals.refused(part)
	local mesh = meshOf(part)
	return mesh ~= nil and type(verdictOf(mesh)) == "string"
end

function Refusals.cut(part)
	local mesh = meshOf(part)
	if mesh then
		settle(mesh, true)
	end
end

function Refusals.refuse(part, reason)
	local mesh = meshOf(part)
	if mesh and notSolid(reason) then
		settle(mesh, reason)
	end
	tell(part, reason)
end

function Refusals.explain(part)
	local mesh = meshOf(part)
	local reason = mesh and verdictOf(mesh)
	if type(reason) == "string" then
		tell(part, reason)
	end
end

-- Asks the engine about the waiting meshes one after another. Yields.
local function judgeWaiting(fragment)
	while #waiting > 0 do
		local part = table.remove(waiting, 1)
		local mesh = meshOf(part)
		local copy = Instance.fromExisting(part)
		copy.Archivable = true
		copy.Anchored = true
		local frame = copy.CFrame
		local reach = copy.Size / 4
		local fragments, reason = fragment(copy, { frame:PointToWorldSpace(reach), frame:PointToWorldSpace(-reach) })
		copy:Destroy()
		for _, entry in ipairs(fragments or {}) do
			entry.Instance:Destroy()
		end
		if mesh then
			if reason and notSolid(reason) then
				settle(mesh, reason)
			else
				settle(mesh, true)
			end
		end
	end
	judges -= 1
end

function Refusals.judge(part, fragment, done)
	local mesh = meshOf(part)
	local verdict = nil
	if mesh then
		verdict = verdictOf(mesh)
	end
	if type(verdict) == "table" then
		if done then
			table.insert(verdict, done)
		end
		return
	end
	if not mesh or verdict ~= nil then
		if done then
			done()
		end
		return
	end
	verdicts[mesh] = { done }
	table.insert(waiting, part)
	if judges < JUDGES then
		judges += 1
		task.spawn(judgeWaiting, fragment)
	end
end

return Refusals

--[[
	Ribbon  -  the cutter of a jagged blade (Reactor/Blade.ribbon): a thin box swept through the
	ribbon's frames (GeometryService:SweepPartAsync joins every two of them up), which is the blade's
	own box bent along a zig-zag. It is made ONCE for a Force and a way of the blade and kept out of
	the world; Reactor/Carve sets a copy of it where the blade stands for each thing it cuts. So
	everything one Force cuts is cut along the very same surface, and a jagged cut costs one engine
	call more than a clean one, whatever it cuts.

	A sweep costs about a millisecond a joint while the box is short, and six times that for a box
	500 studs long. So the box is swept short and the ribbon stretched along its straight way
	afterwards (a MeshPart's Size scales its shape, and the ribbon stands square to the space it was
	made in).

	Ribbon.cutter(ribbon) -> the cutter (a MeshPart, never parented), or nil when the engine
	    refuses. Yields the first time a Force's ribbon is asked for. The cutter is made in
	    the blade's own space: at blade.frame * cutter.CFrame it lies where the blade stands.
]]

local GeometryService = game:GetService("GeometryService")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local Ribbon = {}

-- A Force's cut table (Force/init: record.cut) -> { [lengthwise] = { cutter, making } }. The
-- keys are weak: a cutter goes with its Force.
local made = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })

local function sweep(ribbon)
	local tool = Instance.new("Part")
	tool.Anchored = true
	tool.Size = ribbon.tool
	local ok, swept = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:SweepPartAsync(tool, ribbon.frames)
	end)
	tool:Destroy()
	if not ok or typeof(swept) ~= "Instance" then
		return nil
	end
	local size = swept.Size
	local stretched = { X = size.X, Y = size.Y, Z = size.Z }
	stretched[ribbon.straight] = ribbon.length
	swept.Size = Vector3.new(stretched.X, stretched.Y, stretched.Z)
	return swept
end

function Ribbon.cutter(ribbon)
	local ofForce = made[ribbon.key]
	if not ofForce then
		ofForce = {}
		made[ribbon.key] = ofForce
	end
	local entry = ofForce[ribbon.lengthwise]
	if not entry then
		entry = { making = true }
		ofForce[ribbon.lengthwise] = entry
		entry.cutter = sweep(ribbon)
		entry.making = false
	end
	-- Asked for again while it is being made: every cut of the Force waits for the one cutter.
	while entry.making do
		RunService.Heartbeat:Wait()
	end
	return entry.cutter
end

return Ribbon

--[[
	Shards  -  what a part breaks into with Break = "Shards": fragments cut by the engine
	(GeometryService:FragmentAsync) around points of ours (Reactor/Sites), kept out of the world as
	templates that Reactor/Display copies. The part is read, never changed. Break = "Blocks" on a part
	that is not a plain box comes here too, cut around a grid (Reactor/Dice.centres).
	A cut yields, and a play needs its pieces up front, so shards are cut ahead and kept per part under
	a key naming all the cut depends on; a Reactor without them answers its Force a few frames late.
	  Shards.cuttable(part), Shards.refused(part), Shards.explain(part), Shards.judge(part, done)
	  Shards.key(part, count, seed, hit, reach, grid) -> string
	  Shards.get(part, key) -> shards | false (refused, or under two: moves whole) | nil (not cut yet)
	      shards: { { template, box, size, standOffset, fixed, siteIndex, baked } }, .sites, .strike.
	      A stand-in at frame F stands at F * standOffset. Cracked ground is cut into crust and base
	      first, then the crust into pieces. A blade's cut is Reactor/Carve's.
	  Shards.prepare(jobs, done): jobs { { part, key, count, seed, hit, reach, grid, face, line, loose } }
	  Shards.recut(jobs, done): jobs { { template, points } }, a play's own, not kept
	  Shards.without(part, boxes) -> the part with boxes taken out (Reactor/SkinDisplay)
	A kept set goes with its part (InstanceMap). Fragments are never saved: each session cuts again.
]]

local GeometryService = game:GetService("GeometryService")
local Refusals = require(script.Parent.Refusals)
local Sites = require(script.Parent.Sites)
local Dice = require(script.Parent.Dice)
local Carve = require(script.Parent.Carve)
local LayerCuts = require(script.Parent.LayerCuts)
local InstanceMap = require(script.Parent.Parent.InstanceMap)

-- Cuts running at once.
local WORKERS = 4
-- A hit is the same hit within this many studs: the key rounds to it.
local HIT_STEP = 0.5

local Shards = {}

-- part -> { key = string, shards = table or false }
local kept = InstanceMap.new()

-- Whether a part's fragments come with its colours in their geometry: a union showing its parts'
-- colours (UsePartColor off) does, and given its Color too would show it twice, too dark.
local function bakesColours(part)
	return part:IsA("PartOperation") and not part.UsePartColor
end

Shards.refused = Refusals.refused
Shards.explain = Refusals.explain

function Shards.cuttable(part)
	if part:IsA("MeshPart") then
		return not Refusals.refused(part)
	end
	if part:IsA("PartOperation") then
		return true
	end
	if part:IsA("Part") or part:IsA("WedgePart") or part:IsA("CornerWedgePart") then
		-- A Part that carries a mesh draws the mesh, which is not what the engine would cut.
		return part:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("DataModelMesh") == nil
	end
	return false
end

function Shards.key(part, count, seed, hit, reach, grid, line)
	local size = part.Size
	local shape = part.ClassName
	if part:IsA("MeshPart") then
		shape ..= part.MeshId
	elseif part:IsA("Part") then
		shape ..= part.Shape.Name
	elseif bakesColours(part) then
		-- A cut with the parts' colours is no cut for a union using its own.
		shape ..= ":baked"
	end
	local where = "even"
	if hit then
		where = string.format("%d,%d,%d", math.round(hit.X / HIT_STEP), math.round(hit.Y / HIT_STEP), math.round(hit.Z / HIT_STEP))
	end
	if reach then
		where = string.format("cracks:%s:%d", where, math.round(reach / HIT_STEP))
	end
	if line then
		-- A split is its path's ends, its reach and its wander.
		local points = line.path.points
		local first, last = points[1], points[#points]
		where = string.format("%s:split:%d,%d,%d:%d,%d,%d:%.2f:%d", where,
			math.round(first.X / HIT_STEP), math.round(first.Y / HIT_STEP), math.round(first.Z / HIT_STEP),
			math.round(last.X / HIT_STEP), math.round(last.Y / HIT_STEP), math.round(last.Z / HIT_STEP), line.reach, line.seed or 0)
	end
	if grid then
		where = "blocks"
	end
	return string.format("%s|%.3f,%.3f,%.3f|%d|%d|%s", shape, size.X, size.Y, size.Z, count, seed, where)
end

function Shards.get(part, key)
	local set = kept:get(part)
	if set and set.key == key then
		return set.shards
	end
	return nil
end

-- The engine's fragments of `part` around world points, or nil and its reason. Yields. A wedge is
-- cut as a union of itself.
local function fragment(part, points)
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:FragmentAsync(part, points)
	end)
	if ok and type(result) == "table" then
		return result
	end
	local reason = nil
	if not ok then
		reason = tostring(result)
	end
	local united, union = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:UnionAsync(part, {})
	end)
	local solid = united and type(union) == "table" and union[1] or nil
	if not solid then
		return nil, reason
	end
	ok, result = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:FragmentAsync(solid, points)
	end)
	solid:Destroy()
	if ok and type(result) == "table" then
		return result
	end
	return nil, reason
end

-- A fragment as a shard of the part whose frame is `frame`.
local function shardOf(template, frame, fixed, siteIndex)
	local extents = template.ExtentsCFrame
	return {
		template = template,
		box = frame:ToObjectSpace(extents),
		size = template.ExtentsSize,
		standOffset = extents:ToObjectSpace(template.CFrame),
		fixed = fixed,
		siteIndex = siteIndex,
	}
end

-- A copy of a part the engine takes as it is: Archivable, and out of the world.
local function solidCopy(part)
	local copy = Instance.fromExisting(part)
	copy.Archivable = true
	copy.Anchored = true
	return copy
end

-- What of `template`'s box lies inside `part` (the engine's intersection, keeping the box's frame).
-- into: the part's place in the template's space when the template stands elsewhere. nil when
-- nothing is shared or the engine refuses. Yields.
local function clip(template, part, into)
	local other = solidCopy(part)
	if into then
		other.CFrame = into * part.CFrame
	end
	-- White, as every cut's source is; a stand-in is given its part's colour on top.
	other.Color = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
	if other:IsA("PartOperation") then
		other.UsePartColor = true
	end
	local box = Instance.new("Part")
	box.Anchored = true
	box.Size = template.Size
	box.CFrame = template.CFrame
	box.Color = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:IntersectAsync(box, { other })
	end)
	box:Destroy()
	other:Destroy()
	if not ok or type(result) ~= "table" or not result[1] then
		return nil
	end
	for position = 2, #result do
		result[position]:Destroy()
	end
	return result[1]
end

LayerCuts.use(fragment, shardOf, clip)

-- The engine's first intersection with a shape is slow, later ones fast: a skin is warmed once,
-- ahead of its first crack (Reactor/Entries.prepare). Returns at once.
local warmed = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
function Shards.warm(part)
	if warmed[part] then
		return
	end
	warmed[part] = true
	task.spawn(function()
		local probe = Instance.new("Part")
		probe.Size = Vector3.new(1, 1, 1)
		probe.CFrame = part.CFrame
		local made = clip(probe, part, nil)
		probe:Destroy()
		if made then
			made:Destroy()
		end
	end)
end

-- `part` with boxes taken out: one new part, out of the world, or nil. Yields.
function Shards.without(part, boxes)
	local source = solidCopy(part)
	local cutters = table.create(#boxes)
	for position, box in ipairs(boxes) do
		local cutter = Instance.new("Part")
		cutter.Anchored = true
		cutter.Size = box.size
		cutter.CFrame = box.frame
		cutters[position] = cutter
	end
	local ok, result = pcall(function()
		return GeometryService:SubtractAsync(source, cutters, { SplitApart = false })
	end)
	source:Destroy()
	for _, cutter in ipairs(cutters) do
		cutter:Destroy()
	end
	if not ok or type(result) ~= "table" or not result[1] then
		return nil
	end
	for position = 2, #result do
		result[position]:Destroy()
	end
	return result[1]
end

-- What is given to the engine to cut. It refuses a part that is not Archivable, as every runtime
-- copy is (Reactor/HandOver makes Reactors of those): such a part is cut as an Archivable copy,
-- the second value true for whoever asked to destroy it.
local function archivable(part)
	if part.Archivable then
		return part, false
	end
	local copy = Instance.fromExisting(part)
	copy.Archivable = true
	return copy, true
end

-- Cuts one job and returns its shards, or false. Yields.
local function cut(job)
	local part = job.part
	if not part.Parent and not job.loose then
		return false
	end
	-- A stacked ground's patch within one layer is cut as any patch, its shards marked with the layer.
	local shares = job.layers
	local stacked = shares ~= nil and #shares > 1
	if job.bladeFrame then
		if stacked then
			return LayerCuts.carve(job, part.CFrame, Carve.cut)
		end
		-- Only a mesh's own refusal is kept and told; any other failed carve moves whole in silence.
		local carved, refusal = Carve.cut(job, fragment, shardOf)
		if refusal and Refusals.notSolid(refusal) and not job.loose then
			Refusals.refuse(part, refusal)
		end
		if carved and shares then
			LayerCuts.stamp(carved, shares[1])
		end
		return carved
	end
	local frame = part.CFrame
	local whole, madeHere = archivable(part)
	local random = Sites.sequence(job.seed)
	local offsets
	local strike, split = nil, nil
	if job.grid then
		offsets = Dice.centres(part.Size, job.count)
	elseif job.reach then
		-- A ground's patch (loose) is always cut: one left whole could never crack again.
		offsets, strike, split = Sites.cracks(part.Size, job.count, job.hit, job.reach, random, { face = job.face, fill = job.loose == true, line = job.line })
	elseif job.hit then
		offsets = Sites.aroundHit(part.Size, job.count, job.hit, random)
	else
		offsets = Sites.even(part.Size, job.count, random)
	end
	local points = table.create(#offsets)
	for index, offset in ipairs(offsets) do
		points[index] = frame:PointToWorldSpace(offset)
	end

	if stacked then
		local layered = LayerCuts.cut(job, whole, frame, points, split)
		if madeHere then
			whole:Destroy()
		end
		if layered then
			layered.sites = offsets
			layered.strike = strike
		end
		return layered
	end

	-- Cracked ground: crust off its base first, then the crust into pieces. A fragment's Index is its
	-- point's place in the cut.
	local source = whole
	local crust, base = nil, nil
	if split then
		local halves = fragment(whole, { frame:PointToWorldSpace(split.inCrust), frame:PointToWorldSpace(split.inBase) })
		if halves and #halves == 2 then
			for _, entry in ipairs(halves) do
				if entry.Index == 1 then
					crust = entry.Instance
				else
					base = entry.Instance
				end
			end
		end
		if crust and base then
			source = crust
		else
			base = nil
		end
	end

	local fragments, reason = fragment(source, points)
	if crust then
		crust:Destroy()
	end
	if madeHere then
		whole:Destroy()
	end
	if not fragments or #fragments < 2 then
		if base then
			base:Destroy()
		end
		if reason and not job.loose then
			Refusals.refuse(part, reason)
		end
		return false
	end
	Refusals.cut(part)
	local shards = table.create(#fragments + 1)
	for _, entry in ipairs(fragments) do
		table.insert(shards, shardOf(entry.Instance, frame, false, entry.Index))
	end
	if base then
		table.insert(shards, shardOf(base, frame, true, nil))
	end
	if bakesColours(part) then
		for _, shard in ipairs(shards) do
			shard.baked = true
		end
	end
	if shares then
		LayerCuts.stamp(shards, shares[1])
	end
	shards.sites = offsets
	shards.strike = strike
	return shards
end

-- Cuts a fragment of an earlier cut again (it keeps its part's frame, the frame of its points).
local function cutAgain(job)
	if job.bladeFrame then
		local carved, refusal = Carve.cut(job, fragment, shardOf)
		-- A whole part cut again is cut as itself: its mesh may be what the engine refuses.
		if refusal and Refusals.notSolid(refusal) and job.part and not job.template and not job.blockSize then
			Refusals.refuse(job.part, refusal)
		end
		return carved
	end
	if job.layered then
		return LayerCuts.cutAgain(job)
	end
	local template = job.template
	local frame = template.CFrame
	local points = table.create(#job.points)
	for index, offset in ipairs(job.points) do
		points[index] = frame:PointToWorldSpace(offset)
	end
	local fragments = fragment(template, points)
	if not fragments or #fragments < 2 then
		return false
	end
	local shards = table.create(#fragments)
	for _, entry in ipairs(fragments) do
		table.insert(shards, shardOf(entry.Instance, frame, false, entry.Index))
	end
	return shards
end

function Shards.judge(part, done)
	Refusals.judge(part, fragment, done)
end

function Shards.prepare(jobs, done)
	local total = #jobs
	if total == 0 then
		done()
		return
	end
	local taken = 0
	local finished = 0
	local function work()
		while taken < total do
			taken += 1
			local job = jobs[taken]
			local ok, shards = pcall(cut, job)
			kept:set(job.part, { key = job.key, shards = ok and shards or false })
			finished += 1
		end
		if finished == total and done then
			local callback = done
			done = nil
			callback()
		end
	end
	for _ = 1, math.min(WORKERS, total) do
		task.spawn(work)
	end
end

function Shards.recut(jobs, done)
	local total = #jobs
	local results = table.create(total, false)
	if total == 0 then
		done(results)
		return
	end
	local taken = 0
	local finished = 0
	local function work()
		while taken < total do
			taken += 1
			local position = taken
			local ok, shards = pcall(cutAgain, jobs[position])
			results[position] = ok and shards or false
			finished += 1
		end
		if finished == total and done then
			local callback = done
			done = nil
			callback(results)
		end
	end
	for _ = 1, math.min(WORKERS, total) do
		task.spawn(work)
	end
end

return Shards
